'''Grant Campbell Hanley''' (born 20 November 1991) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Hibernia}} club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

Across his club career, Hanley has previously played for [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]]. He has won the [[EFL Championship]] three times, once with Newcastle and twice with Norwich. He was named in the [[2020–21 EFL Championship|2020–21]] EFL Championship Team of the Season.

He made his full international debut for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in 2011, and has won 70 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] in his career. He also appeared at the [[UEFA Euro 2020|Euro 2020]] and [[UEFA Euro 2024|Euro 2024]] championships and the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].

==Early years==
Hanley was born in [[Dumfries]].<ref name=Hugman/> He was involved at youth level with local club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]], [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] before he joined Blackburn Rovers as a 16-year-old in 2008.<ref>[http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/muirheads-career-built-on-solid-bricks/ Muirhead's career built on solid bricks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616125249/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/muirheads-career-built-on-solid-bricks/ |date=16 June 2012 }} Scottish Football League, 14 January 2011</ref><ref name=NewCH>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/scotland/2010/05/24/i-can-be-the-new-colin-hendry-for-scotland-blackburn-vows-scots-under-19-skipper-grant-hanley-86908-22281189/ |title=I can be the new Colin Hendry for Scotland & Blackburn, vows Scots under 19 skipper Grant Hanley |newspaper=Daily Record |date=24 May 2010 |accessdate=7 August 2025 |first=Scott |last=McDermott}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Blackburn Rovers===
[[File:Grant Hanley (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|200px|Hanley playing for [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in 2014.]]

At Rovers, Hanley was [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the under-18 team.<ref name=NewCH/> He made his [[Premier League]] debut for Rovers in a 1–0 win at Aston Villa on 9 May 2010.<ref name=BRProf>{{cite web |title=Grant Hanley first team profile |url=http://www.rovers.co.uk/page/ProfilesDetail/0,,10303~51151,00.html |publisher=Blackburn Rovers F.C. |access-date=10 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120505200558/http://www.rovers.co.uk/page/ProfilesDetail/0%2C%2C10303~51151%2C00.html |archive-date=5 May 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11676/6143524/rovers-rule-at-villa-park |title=Rovers rule at Villa Park |website=Sky Sports |date=9 May 2010 |access-date=9 May 2010}}</ref> Hanley committed his future when he signed a new five-year deal with Blackburn on 21 July 2010.<ref>[http://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/8284970.Blackburn_Rovers_defender_Hanley_pens_five_year_contract/ Blackburn Rovers defender Hanley pens five-year contract] ''Lancashire Telegraph'', 22 July 2010</ref>

Hanley made his first Premier League appearance of season 2010–11 as a 67th-minute substitute in a 1–1 draw at home to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} He made his [[FA Cup]] debut on 8 January 2011, against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] in a 1–0 victory at Ewood Park.<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/football/match/2011/jan/08/blackburn-v-qpr Blackburn Rovers v QPR Match facts] ''The Guardian'', 8 January 2011</ref> On 5 March 2011, Hanley scored his first goal for Rovers in a 3–2 defeat against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] at [[Craven Cottage]].<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9411020.stm Fulham 3–2 Blackburn] BBC Sport, 5 March 2011</ref> That was the last of his nine Blackburn first team appearances that season although he was to make his international debut at the end of the season.<ref name=qosintl/> On 31 December 2011, Hanley started and scored the winning goal in a 3–2 win against local rivals [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[Old Trafford]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120712020411/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/16373420.stm|title=Match winner Grant Hanley hails Blackburn Rovers youth}} ''BBC Sport'', 31 December 2011</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120505123442/http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/premiership/news/2011/12/31/489C36A6-33D7-11E1-AC36-1AE57F33923B.php Blackburn stun United, Spurs and Chelsea slip up] Reuters, 31 December 2011</ref> This win lifted Blackburn off the bottom of the table.<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/16324998.stm Man Utd 2–3 Blackburn] ''BBC Sport'', 31 December 2011</ref> On 14 April 2012, in a Premier League fixture against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] at the [[Liberty Stadium]], he suffered an ankle ligament injury.{{citation needed|date=February 2016}} Hanley made 28 appearances and scored one goal in all competitions for Rovers, but the club was relegated into the [[Football League Championship|Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/league-table.html |title=Premier League Table |publisher=Premier League |access-date=30 August 2017 |archive-date=16 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160516065708/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/league-table.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the beginning of the [[2012–13 Blackburn Rovers F.C. season|2012–13 season]], Hanley maintained his first team spot in defense and formed a partnership with teammate [[Scott Dann]]. At the end of the season, he signed a new five-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Transfer news: Blackburn give Grant Hanley long-term contract at Ewood Park |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12691/8754287/Transfer-news-Blackburn-give-Grant-Hanley-long-term-contract-at-Ewood-Park |website=Sky Sports |date=4 June 2013 |access-date=16 June 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Grant Hanley.JPG|thumb|right|200px|Hanley as a Blackburn Rovers captain in 2015.]]

After Dann left for [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in January 2014, Hanley was appointed as the new [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the club.<ref>{{cite web |title=Delighted for the captain |url=http://www.rovers.co.uk/news/article/delighted-for-the-captain-1336772.aspx |publisher=Blackburn Rovers F.C. |date=3 February 2014 |access-date=25 February 2014}}</ref>

===Newcastle United===
On 21 July 2016, Hanley signed for newly relegated Championship club [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] on a five-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news |title=Grant Hanley: Newcastle United sign Blackburn Rovers captain |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36857862 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 July 2016 |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> He was handed the number 5 shirt, previously worn by [[Georginio Wijnaldum]]. He scored his first goal for the club in the 79th minute in a 6–0 win versus [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] at [[Loftus Road]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37282510 |title=Queens Park Rangers 0-6 Newcastle United |date=14 September 2016 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Norwich City===
====2017–18====
On 30 August 2017, Hanley joined [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on a four-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news|title=Grant Hanley joins Norwich City|url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2017/august/grant-hanley-joins-norwich-city/|publisher=Norwich City F.C.|date=30 August 2017}}</ref> He made his debut on 9 September 2017, coming on as a substitute in a 1–0 win over [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] at [[Carrow Road]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41132799 |title=Norwich City 1-0 Birmingham City |date=9 September 2017 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=9 September 2017 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Although he had been something of an emergency buy, with Norwich having started the season with a number of injuries and playing inexperienced centre-backs, Hanley soon became a regular in the team, often being deployed as one of three centre halves alongside [[Timm Klose]] and [[Christoph Zimmermann]]. He ultimately made 32 league appearances for Norwich during the 2017–18 season, plus two in the FA Cup. One of his most memorable contributions came in the derby game against [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] on 18 February. Ipswich had gone 1–0 up in the 89th minute and seemed set for a first win over Norwich in nine years. However, deep into added time, Hanley chased a ball to the byline and crossed it back into the goal area, allowing Klose to head it home for an equaliser.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43020998 |title=Norwich City 1-1 Ipswich Town |date=18 February 2018 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=15 January 2019 }}</ref> The following month, on 17 March, Hanley scored his first goal for Norwich, the second in a 3–2 win over [[Reading F.C.|Reading]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43353592 |title=Norwich City 3-2 Reading |date=17 March 2018 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=15 January 2019 }}</ref>

====2018–19====
[[File:Grant Hanley 2018.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Hanley playing for [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] in 2018.]]

At the beginning of the 2018–19 season, with [[Russell Martin (footballer)|Russell Martin]] leaving the club, Hanley was appointed Norwich's new club captain<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2018/august/grant-hanley-birmingham/ |title=Grant Hanley: Being named captain is a huge honour |date=1 August 2018 |publisher=Norwich City F.C. |access-date=6 May 2019 }}</ref> ahead of [[Ivo Pinto]], who had deputised for Martin for much of the previous season. He played in Norwich's opening six league games, getting his second goal for the club in a 4–3 defeat against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]];<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45066581 |title=Norwich City 3-4 West Bromwich Albion: Jay Rodriguez efforts please Baggies boss |date=11 August 2018 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 May 2019 }}</ref> however, he was then injured in training.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45522509 |title=Grant Hanley: Norwich defender out for six weeks with quad injury |date=14 September 2018 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 May 2019 }}</ref> During his absence, Klose and Zimmermann established themselves at centre-back, with [[Ben Godfrey]] also becoming a regular choice, and Hanley was restricted to a few appearances as substitute on his return. When he finally started a game, an [[FA Cup]] tie against [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]], he was sent off in the first fifteen minutes for a professional foul on [[Ronan Curtis]] and Norwich went on to lose 1–0.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46707005 |title=Norwich City 0-1 Portsmouth in FA Cup third round |date=5 January 2019 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 May 2019 }}</ref> Despite his lack of game time, Hanley remained club captain as Norwich gained promotion to the [[Premier League]]. In the final game of the season, as Norwich defeated [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] 2–1, winning the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] title, Hanley was brought on as an 89th minute substitute for [[Onel Hernandez]]<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48081773 |title=Aston Villa 1-2 Norwich City: Canaries win to seal Championship title |date=5 May 2019 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 May 2019 }}</ref> and lifted the Championship trophy alongside team captain Zimmermann.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/47713270 |title=Relieve the final day of the Championship season as it happened |date=5 May 2019 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 May 2019 }}</ref><ref name=trophymedal19>{{Cite news |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2834759-championship-table-2019-football-results-final-standings-and-play-off-fixtures |title=Championship Table 2019: Football Results, Final Standings and Play-Off Fixtures |website=Bleacher Report |date=5 May 2019 |access-date=6 May 2019}}</ref>

====2019–20====
Hanley scored an [[own goal]] in a 4–1 defeat against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on 9 August, which was the first goal of the [[2019–20 Premier League]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49201578 |title=Liverpool 4–1 Norwich City |first=Neil |last=Johnston |website=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2019 |access-date=10 August 2019}}</ref> Despite this, he retained his place for the next two Premier League games until he was once more injured in training.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edp24.co.uk/sport/norwich-city/canaries-timm-klose-grant-hanley-injury-latest-1-6244813 |title=Klose set for long layoff; Hanley also out for West Ham |first=Paddy|last=Davit|website=EDP|date=30 August 2019 |access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref> He would later admit he had been injured at the start of the season. Norwich suffered several injuries at centre-back throughout the season, with midfielders [[Alexander Tettey]] and [[Ibrahim Amadou]] both being deployed as makeshift centre-halves at various points. As a result, despite not being an automatic choice, Hanley made 15 appearances in the season's first 29 league games, as well as helping Norwich reach their first FA Cup quarter-final in over 20 years with a goal in a 2–1 win over [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51208465 |title=Burnley 1–2 Norwich |first=Phil|last=Dawkes|website=bbc.co.uk|date=25 January 2020 |access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref> However, at that stage, the season was suspended because of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. When it resumed after three months, Hanley was again injured.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edp24.co.uk/sport/norwich-city/hanley-injury-blow-for-canaries-1-67043636244813|title=Hanley injury blow for Canaries ahead of restart|first=David|last=Freezer|website=EDP|date=17 June 2020|access-date=26 July 2020}}{{Dead link|date=June 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He played no further part in the season as Norwich finished bottom of the Premier League and were relegated back to the Championship.

====2020–21====
With the new season starting only two months later, Hanley would again start a season injured.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pinkun.com/sport/norwich-city/city-skipper-targets-injury-return-1843172 |title=Norwich skipper Hanley keen to lead Championship recovery as he targets injury return|first=David|last=Freezer|website=Pink Un|date=21 July 2020 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> He would make his first appearance of the season on 17 October in Norwich's fifth game, a 2–1 win over [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54488894 |title=Rotherham United 1–2 Norwich City|website=BBC Sport|date=17 October 2020 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> However, from then on, he would not miss a game, making 42 league appearances and 2 FA Cup appearances, as well as contributing a goal in a 2–1 win over [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edp24.co.uk/sport/norwich-city/cardiff-1-norwich-2-hanley-reaction-6910356|title=Cardiff 1 Norwich City 2: Grant Hanley reaction|first=David|last=Freezer|website=EDP|date=17 January 2021 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> With Godfrey having left the club, Klose absent on loan and Zimmermann absent through injury, Hanley spent most of the season partnered with [[Ben Gibson]], as Norwich won the Football League Championship for the second time in three seasons. He came second behind [[Emi Buendia]] in Norwich's Player of the Season vote<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edp24.co.uk/sport/norwich-city/grant-hanley-player-of-the-season-7934352|title=Hanley named as runner-up in Player of the Season vote|first=Connor|last=Southwell|website=EDP|date=29 April 2021 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> and, after Norwich finished the season with a 2–2 draw with [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]], he lifted the trophy alongside outgoing teammate Tettey, who had been made captain for the game but had handed the armband back to Hanley when he was substituted in the 87th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eveningnews24.co.uk/sport/norwich-city/norwich-city-championship-title-winners-7957820|title='Worthy champions' - City fans celebrate trophy lift|first=Connor|last=Southwell|website=Evening News|date=8 May 2021 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref>

====2021–22====
Ahead of Norwich's return to the Premier League, Hanley signed a new four-year contract deal, extending his stay with the club until 30 June 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grant Hanley signs contract extension at Norwich City|url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2021/july/grant-hanley-signs-contract-extension-at-norwich-city/|access-date=2021-08-05|website=www.canaries.co.uk|language=en-gb}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season on 20 November in Norwich's 2–1 win against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], the first game in charge for new manager [[Dean Smith]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59271460|title=Norwich City 2–1 Southampton|publisher=BBC Sport|date=20 November 2021|accessdate=27 March 2022}}</ref> Hanley suffered an injury, his second of the season, early on in the game with Manchester United on 11 December, having to be replaced by [[Jacob Sørensen (footballer, born 1998)|Jacob Sørensen]], with Norwich going on to lose the match 1–0.,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59529643|title=Norwich City 0–1 Manchester United|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 December 2021|accessdate=28 May 2022}}</ref> but returned to the starting line-up in January.

Hanley would make a total of 33 Premier League appearances in the season, usually partnered with Gibson, as well as two appearances in the FA Cup and one in the Carabao Cup.<ref name="GH21"/> However, it would be another disappointing season for Norwich, as they finished bottom and were once again relegated back to the Championship after only one season. Hanley was one of the few Norwich players to come in for any praise: He again came second in the club's Player of the Season vote, this time losing out to [[Teemu Pukki]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pukki wins War Paint for Men Player of the Season award|url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/content/pukki-wins-war-paint-for-men-player-of-the-season-award|access-date=2022-05-28|website=www.canaries.co.uk|language=en-gb}}</ref>

====2022–23====
Hanley received a red card in the first league game of the season, a 1–0 defeat at [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardiff City 1-0 Norwich City: Romaine Sawyers scores winner for Bluebirds |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12660534/cardiff-city-1-0-norwich-city-romaine-sawyers-scores-winner-for-bluebirds |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season in a 1–1 draw at [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] in early October.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Reading 1-1 Norwich City: Jeff Hendrick earns point for Royals |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12708988/reading-1-1-norwich-city-jeff-hendrick-earns-point-for-royals |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> He would again be a regular for Norwich throughout the season, usually partnered with either Gibson or [[Andrew Omobamidele]], making 39 Championship appearances plus one in each of the cups.<ref name="GH22" /> However, he would suffer an injury during a 2–0 win over former club Blackburn Rovers,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grant Hanley: Norwich centre-half set for surgery on 'serious' Achilles injury|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65235001 |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=bbc.co.uk |date=10 April 2023 |language=en}}</ref> which caused him to miss the last five games of the season as Norwich finished 13th.

====2023–24====
Hanley's injury continued into the next season and he would not appear until December, when he was brought on as a half-time substitute for [[Jonathan Rowe (footballer, born 2003)|Jonathan Rowe]] in a 1–0 defeat to West Bromwich Albion, following the sending off of [[Borja Sainz]] late in the first half.<ref>{{Cite web |title=West Bromwich Albion 1–0 Norwich City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67756830 |access-date=2024-06-19 |website=bbc.co.uk |date=26 December 2023 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Grant Hanley: "You miss struggling to swallow porridge"|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cek5x1nrpr4o|access-date=2024-06-19 |website=bbc.co.uk |date=28 December 2023 |language=en}}</ref> He would subsequently start the New Year's Day game against  Southampton, where he was replaced by [[Adam Idah]] after 74 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Norwich City v Southampton|url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/en/match/norwich-city-vs-southampton-english-football-league--championship-2024-01-01|access-date=2024-06-19 |website=southamptonfc.com |language=en}}</ref> He was picked for Norwich's third round FA Cup tie, a 1–1 draw against [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]], but exited the field during injury time with a back problem.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Norwich City: David Wagner on Hwang and Hanley injuries|url=https://www.pinkun.com/sport/norwich-city/24032722.norwich-city-david-wagner-hwang-hanley-injuries/|access-date=2024-06-19 |website=www.pinkun.com |date=7 January 2024 |language=en}}</ref> He finally played a full game for Norwich in February, a 2–2 draw against Queens Park Rangers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=QPR 2–2 Norwich|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/queens-park-rangers-vs-norwich-city/report/485069|access-date=2024-06-19 |website=www.skysports.com |language=en}}</ref>

By now, Norwich had signed both [[Shane Duffy]] and [[Danny Batth]] as options at centre-half alongside Gibson, and Hanley found his opportunities limited: He started only 6 league games and 2 FA Cup games, the last of them in March.<ref name="GH23" /> He made a rare appearance as an 82nd minute substitute for Gibson in the last game of the regulation season, a 1–0 defeat against Birmingham.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Birm'ham 1–0 Norwich|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/birmingham-city-vs-norwich-city/report/485242|access-date=2024-06-19 |website=www.skysports.com |language=en}}</ref> This saw Norwich finish 6th and qualify for the play-offs, which Hanley played no part in as the club were quickly eliminated by [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] in the semi-finals.

====2024–25====
With both Gibson and Batth leaving the club over the summer, Hanley was selected alongside Duffy in defense for Norwich's first game of the [[2024–25 Norwich City F.C. season|2024–25 season]] and first under new manager [[Johannes Hoff Thorup]]. The game, against newly promoted [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]], ended in a 2–0 defeat. Hanley failed to clear the ball for Oxford's first goal and was substituted off after 61 minutes for Sørenson.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oxford United 2–0 Norwich City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn9ldl2q3dxt|access-date=2025-02-07 |website=www.bbc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> He was subsequently removed from the starting lineup, with new signings [[Callum Doyle]] and [[José Córdoba]] both being preferred at centre half ahead of him and Duffy. He would make one further start in a Carabao Cup match against Crystal Palace.<ref>{{Cite web |title=C Palace 4–0 Norwich|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/c-palace-vs-norwich/teams/521189|access-date=2025-02-07 |website=www.skysports.com |language=en}}</ref> His remaining two appearances would be as a second-half substitute in Championship matches, with him making his last appearance for Norwich when he replaced Sørenson in the 75th minute of a match with Cardiff City on 2 November.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardiff 2–1 Norwich: Bluebirds earn win after stunning late turnaround|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11688/13245483/cardiff-2-1-norwich-bluebirds-earn-win-after-stunning-late-turnaround|access-date=2025-02-07 |website=www.skysports.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Birmingham City===
On 17 January 2025, Hanley left Norwich, joining [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on a short-term deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.com/pages/en/media-article/blues-sign-grant-hanley|title=Blues sign Grant Hanley!|publisher=[[Birmingham City F.C.]]|date=17 January 2025|accessdate=17 January 2025}}</ref> On 20 May 2025, the club announced he would be leaving in June when his contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Grant Hanley: Birmingham City defender one of two players released |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cx2rrnpnvneo |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
Hanley signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 5 August 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c70xz87rykko |title=Hibs sign Scotland's Hanley on two-year deal |website=BBC Sport |date=5 August 2025 |accessdate=5 August 2025}}</ref> It marked the first time in his professional career that he had played for a Scottish team. On 25 October 2026 he was brought on in the 82nd minute, against league leaders Celtic, to play as a striker, marking Hanley’s debut in that position.

==International career==
[[File:Grant Hanley Scotland v Bolivia 6 June 2026-70.jpg|thumb|upright|Hanley with Scotland in 2026]]
Hanley captained [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland at under-19 level]].<ref name=NewCH/> On 17 November 2010, he played for [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21s]] when aged 18 in a 3–1 win against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland]] at [[Firhill]].<ref>[http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=128&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=6832 Under-21s defeat Northern Ireland] Scottish Football Association, 17 November 2010</ref>

On 1 February 2011, Hanley was called up to the [[Scotland national football team|senior Scotland squad]] for the first time ahead of the game against [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]] in the [[Nations Cup (football)|Nations Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/scotland/9383384.stm |website=BBC Sport |title=Hanley nets first Scots call-up |date=1 February 2011}}</ref> He made his full international debut as an 84th-minute substitute on 25 May 2011 coming on for [[Gary Caldwell]] against [[Wales national football team|Wales]] in the Nations Cup in [[Dublin]].<ref name=qosintl>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120613072303/http://qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=674 Doonhamer internationalists] Queen of the South F.C., 25 May 2011</ref> His first Scotland goal was in his fifth full international when he opened the scoring in a [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2014 FIFA World Cup qualifier]] at home against [[Wales national football team|Wales]] on 22 March 2013 at [[Hampden Park]].<ref name=Wales/>

In May 2021, Hanley was named in [[Steve Clarke]]'s 26-man squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Skinner|first=Andy|date=19 May 2021|title=Steve Clarke's 26-man Scotland squad for Euro 2020 announced|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish/3156085/steve-clarkes-26-man-scotland-squad-for-euro-2020-announced/|access-date=10 October 2021|website=The Press and Journal|language=en-GB}}</ref> appearing in all three matches against the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]], [[England national football team|England]] and [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]].

On 7 June 2024, Hanley was named in Scotland's squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2024]] finals in Germany,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/record-breaking-goalkeeper-gordon-out-scotland-euro-2024-squad-2024-06-07/|title=Record-breaking goalkeeper Gordon out of Scotland's Euro 2024 squad|date=7 June 2024|access-date=15 June 2024|website=Reuters}}</ref> and on the same day made his [[Scotland Men's International Roll of Honour|50th international appearance]] in a friendly against [[Finland national football team|Finland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eveningnews24.co.uk/sport/24375567.norwich-city-grant-hanley-interview-50th-scotland-cap/|title=Norwich City: Grant Hanley interview on 50th Scotland cap|website=Norwich Evening News |author= Samuel Seaman|access-date= 6 September 2024|date=9 June 2024}}</ref> Hanley appeared as a half-time substitute for [[Ché Adams]] after [[Ryan Porteous]] was sent off in 45th minute during the team's 5–1 loss to hosts [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in the opening match of the tournament on 15 June,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c844x4y3ee3t|title=Ruthless Germany humble 10-man Scotland in Euro 2024 opener|website=BBC Sport|access-date=15 June 2024|date=15 June 2024}}</ref> and went on to start in place of the suspended Porteous in both of the other group fixtures against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] and [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] as Scotland finished bottom of [[UEFA Euro 2024 Group A|Group A]] with one point from three matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028e-1b2c127c5b92-e020507872a2-1000--scotland-1-1-switzerland-clarke-s-men-keep-group-a-hopes-/|title=Scotland 1-1 Switzerland: Clarke's men keep Group A hopes alive|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA|date=19 June 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/match/2036186--scotland-vs-hungary/lineups/|title=Scotland vs Hungary: Line-ups|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA|date=23 June 2024}}</ref>

On 19 May 2026, Hanley was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/scotland-squad-announced-steve-clarke|title=Veteran Gordon and youngster Curtis named in Scotland squad|date=19 May 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|language=en}}</ref> In the second group stage game against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]], he and teammate [[Ryan Christie]] became only the 11th and 12th players to reach 70 caps for the men's team.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=ScotlandNT|author=Scotland National Team|number=2068071043000885678|title=Ryan Christie and Grant Hanley both win their 70th Scotland caps this evening!<br/>#SCOMAR #FIFAWorldCup|access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Jordan John Obita''' (born 8 December 1993) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as [[Left back (association football)|left-back]] or [[winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Hibernia}} club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], and the [[Uganda national football team]].

He has previously played for [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], [[Barnet F.C.|Barnet]], [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]], [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]], [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]], [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]], and [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]]. Born in England, Obita represented England in youth internationals up to the [[England national under-20 football team|under-20]] level and made his full international debut for [[Uganda national football team|Uganda Cranes]] in June 2025.

==== First team breakthrough and departure ====
He made his first Reading appearance for two years in their heavy 6–0 League Cup defeat to [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] in August 2013 before making his league debut a month later at [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/posh-team-news-270813-1017931.aspx |title=Adkins shuffles pack for Peterborough clash |publisher=Reading F.C |access-date=28 August 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23763986 |title=Peterborough United 6–0 Reading |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=28 August 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/team-news-derby-210913-1067254.aspx |title=Obita and Baird start |publisher=Reading F.C |access-date=22 September 2013}}</ref> After securing his place in first team squad for the following games he expressed his desire to play in a central midfield role, a position he played in during his formative Academy years.<ref name="Down the middle" /> In November, he scored his first goal for the club with the winner in a 3–2 victory away at [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and the following month signed a new contract until the summer of 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11673/9049430/ |title=Nigel Adkins delighted as Jordan Obita's first goal for Reading seals victory over Forest |publisher=Sky Sports |access-date=8 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/obita-new-contract-101213-1228091.aspx |title=Obita puts pen to paper |publisher=Reading F.C |access-date=11 December 2013}}</ref> In the second half of the season, the absence of [[Wayne Bridge]] through long-term injury,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/wayne-bridge-injury-sean-morrison-060314-1401807.aspx |title=Bridge & Morro injury update |publisher=Reading F.C |access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref> and the inability of [[Stephen Kelly (Irish footballer)|Stephen Kelly]] and [[Shaun Cummings]] to cement their place in his stead,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Anthony |url=http://www.readingchronicle.co.uk/sport/football/articles/2013/11/16/95057-reading-fc-defender-kelly-aims-to-bridge-the-defensive-gap/ |title=Reading FC defender Kelly aims to Bridge the defensive gap |date=16 November 2013 |work=Reading Chronicle |access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Soccerbase season|49403|2013|name=Shaun Cummings|access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref> saw Obita move to left-back for the game against [[Watford F.C.|Watford]]. He helped the team keep a clean sheet in a 1–0 win and provided the assist for [[Kaspars Gorkšs]]' early winner.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/fixtures-results/match-report/index.aspx?matchid=3632026 |title=Watford 0–1 Reading |publisher=Reading F.C |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201222100/http://www.readingfc.co.uk/fixtures-results/match-report/index.aspx?matchid=3632026 |archive-date=1 February 2014 |access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref> He retained his place for the next game, a 7–1 win against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], and from then on was a regular in the team, making 22 of his 36 appearances after his move to full-back.<ref>{{Soccerbase season|55856|2013|name=Jordan Obita|access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref> He was praised by club captain [[Jobi McAnuff]] who described his adaptation to the left-back role as "fantastic",<ref>{{Cite news |last=Watts |first=Charles |url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/reading-fc-skipper-hails-scary-6645513 |title=Reading FC skipper hails the 'scary' form of Jordan Obita |date=29 January 2014 |work=Reading Post |access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref> and was voted as the club's [[Reading F.C. Player of the Season|Player of the Season]] for 2013–14 by the fans.<ref name="Player of the Season">{{Cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/player-of-the-season-1524766.aspx |title=Obita wins Player of the Season |publisher=Reading F.C |access-date=4 May 2014}}</ref> Obita signed a new contract, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2018, on 30 July 2015.<ref name="Obita signs new Royals contract">{{Cite web |url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/jordan-obita-reading-contract-extension-2582443.aspx |title=Obita signs new Royals contract |date=30 July 2015 |website=readingfc.co.uk |publisher=Reading F.C. |access-date=30 July 2015}}</ref> On 30 August 2017, Reading announced that Obita had signed a new three-year contract, keeping him at the club until 2020.<ref name="Obita signs new three-year deal">{{Cite web |url=https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2017/august/obita-signs-new-three-year-deal/ |title=Obita signs new three-year deal |date=30 August 2017 |website=readingfc.co.uk |publisher=Reading F.C. |access-date=30 August 2017}}</ref>

With his contract with Reading due to expire on 30 June 2020, and due to the effects of the [[2019–20 EFL Championship#Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]] on the [[2019–20 Reading F.C. season|2019–20]] season, Obita signed a short-term extension with Reading until the end of the season on 26 June 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Adam, Blackett, Gunter, McCleary, Obita and Osho all agree contract extensions to the end of July |url=https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2020/june/adam-blackett-gunter-mccleary-obita-and-osho-all-agree-contract-extensions-to-the-end-of-july/ |website=readingfc.co.uk |publisher=Reading F.C. |access-date=26 June 2020 |date=26 June 2020}}</ref> Following the completion of the 2019–20 season, Reading announced that Obita would leave the club at the end of July 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Royals bid farewell to five first team players out of contract |url=https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2020/july/royals-bid-farewell-to-five-first-team-players-out-of-contract/ |website=readingfc.co.uk |publisher=Reading F.C. |access-date=25 July 2020 |date=25 July 2020}}</ref>

===Oxford United===
On 9 November, he signed for [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]], his hometown club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oufc.co.uk/news/2020/november/jordan-obita-joins-oxford-united/|title=Jordan Obita Joins Oxford United|website=www.oufc.co.uk|date=9 November 2020|access-date=9 November 2020}}</ref>

===Wycombe Wanderers===
On 29 January 2021, Obita joined [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] on a two-and-a-half-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55860910 |title=Jordan Obita: Wycombe Wanderers sign Oxford United's ex-Reading man |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 January 2021 |access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref> He left Wycombe during the 2023 close season after rejecting a new contract offer.<ref name = hibs>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65991780 |title=Jordan Obita: Hibernian sign wide man after he rejects Wycombe Wanderers extension |website=BBC Sport |date=22 June 2023 |accessdate=22 June 2023}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
On 22 June 2023, [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] announced the signing of Obita to a two-year contract, with the option for a third year.<ref name = hibs/><ref>{{cite web |title=Jordan Obita Signs For Hibs! |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/jordan-obita-signs-for-hibs |website=hibernianfc.co.uk |publisher=Hibernian F.C. |access-date=22 June 2023 |date=22 June 2023}}</ref> On 19 March 2024 Hibernian announced that Obita had signed a new contract with the club until 30 June 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=JORDAN OBITA SIGNS NEW DEAL! |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2024/march/19/jordan-obita-signs-new-deal-/ |website=hibernianfc.co.uk |publisher=Hibernian F.C. |access-date=19 March 2024 |date=19 March 2024}}</ref> He extended that contract by another year in July 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c628d99dpz7o |title=Hibs continue defensive continuity as Obita extends stay |website=BBC Sport |date=14 July 2025 |accessdate=15 July 2025}}</ref>

== International career ==
Obita was born in England and is of Ugandan descent.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://twitter.com/jordanobita/status/298186952526663680 |title=Jordan Obita on Twitter}}</ref>

Obita represented England at [[England national under-18 football team|under-18]] and [[England national under-19 football team|under-19]] level.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/England/All-Teams/Players/O/Jordan%20Obita |title=Jordan Obita |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=23 October 2013}}</ref> In May 2014 he was called up by the England [[England national under-20 football team|under-20s]] and [[England national under-21 football team|under-21s]] for the [[Toulon Tournament]] and a game against [[Wales national under-21 football team|Wales]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Watts |first=May |url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/reading-fc-star-jordan-obita-7074485 |title=Reading FC star Jordan Obita to receive England call-up |date=6 May 2014 |work=Reading Post |access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref> He was an unused substitute for the game against Wales, but started the first game of the Toulon Tournament and scored the opening goal in a 3–0 win over [[Qatar national under-20 football team|Qatar]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/england/under-21/2014/may/england-qatar-report-220514 |title=England U21s breeze past Qatar to start Toulon in style |last=Veevers |first=Nicholas |date=22 May 2014 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=24 May 2014}}</ref>

In May 2025, Obita was called up to the [[Uganda national football team|Uganda]] squad for the first time for their matches against [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] and [[Gambia national football team|Gambia]] on 6 and 9 June.<ref>{{cite web |title=Paul Put Names 28-Man Uganda Cranes Squad for International Friendlies in Morocco |url=https://www.fufa.co.ug/paul-put-names-28-man-uganda-cranes-squad-for-international-friendlies-in-morocco/ |website=fufa.co.ug |publisher=Federation of Uganda Football Associations |access-date=20 May 2025 |date=20 May 2025}}</ref>

'''Stuart Armstrong''' (born 30 March 1992) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] team [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]. He also plays for the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

Armstrong began his professional career with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], making his debut in 2010 and went on to make almost 150 appearances. Armstrong moved to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in February 2015, and helped them win four [[list of Scottish football champions|Scottish league championships]] and consecutive domestic trebles. He then moved to [[Premier League]] club [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in June 2018. Armstrong joined Canadian club [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC|Vancouver Whitecaps]] in September 2024 before he moved to [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] in January 2025. He returned to Scotland with Aberdeen in September 2025.

Armstrong represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level, then made his [[Scotland national football team|full international]] debut in 2017, representing the side at [[UEFA Euro 2020]]. He was voted as the [[SFWA Young Player of the Year]] in 2013 and has been named in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year]] for the [[Scottish Premiership]] three times. He was also nominated twice for the [[PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Inverness]], Armstrong attended [[Hazlehead Academy]] in [[Aberdeen]],<ref>{{cite news |url = https://www.tes.com/magazine/archived/scotland-players-old-schools-send-good-luck-messages|last1=Hepburn |first1=Henry |title=Scotland players' old schools send good luck messages |access-date=27 December 2021 |work=[[TES (magazine)|TES]] |date=11 June 2021}}</ref> alongside fellow footballer [[Fraser Fyvie]].<ref name="Dundee United starlet Stuart Armstrong: I want last laugh on school pal Fraser Fyvie"/> Armstrong grew up idolizing [[Gianfranco Zola]].<ref name="Arabs youngster Stuart Armstrong in no rush to seek dream move to English top-flight">{{cite news |title=Arabs youngster Stuart Armstrong in no rush to seek dream move to English top-flight |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/arabs-youngster-stuart-armstrong-no-2290936 |newspaper=Daily Record |date=22 September 2013 |access-date=3 April 2014}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Armstrong played for Dyce Boys Club and the [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] youth team, before signing professionally with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in July 2009.<ref name="1st Team">{{cite news |title=Stuart Armstrong Dundee United Profile |url=http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=124&ID=361 |publisher=Dundee United Official Website |access-date=22 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130705042324/http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=124&ID=361 |archive-date=5 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45508561 |title=Stuart Armstrong: Southampton to Celtic cash share leaves boys club in 'shock' |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 September 2018 |access-date=13 September 2018}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
====2010–11====
Armstrong made his first team debut for Dundee United in November 2010, coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 1–0 win over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=46&ID=361 |title=Welcome to Tannadice – Dundee United Football Club|access-date=26 February 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120928170127/http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=46&ID=361|archive-date=28 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Towards the end of the season, manager [[Peter Houston]] praised Armstrong on his substitute role.<ref>{{cite news |title=Peter Houston happy at impact of Dundee United subs |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/d/dundee_utd/9411250.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 March 2011 |access-date=22 May 2013}}</ref>

====2011–12====
Armstrong then scored his first goal for United in a 2–2 draw against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in December 2011.<ref name="St Mirren">{{cite web |title=St Mirren 2–2 Dundee United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/16281327 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=14 February 2012 |date=28 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127055627/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/16281327|archive-date=27 January 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> After the match, Armstrong said that "I got a deflected goal in Inverness last month but my first proper strike came against St Mirren in the 2–2 draw last week and that has filled me with confidence".<ref name="Dundee United starlet Stuart Armstrong: I want last laugh on school pal Fraser Fyvie">{{cite news |title=Dundee United starlet Stuart Armstrong: I want last laugh on school pal Fraser Fyvie |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united-starlet-stuart-armstrong-1112644 |newspaper=Daily Record |date=2 January 2012 |access-date=22 May 2013}}</ref>

====2012–13====
[[File:Stuart Armstrong.jpg|thumb|upright|Armstrong training with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in 2012]]

After making six appearances this season, Armstrong agreed a three-year contract with Dundee United in September 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dundee United extend contracts for Armstrong and Watson |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19704009 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=24 September 2012 |date=24 September 2012}}</ref> Armstrong then signed another new contract with United in October 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee United boss Peter Houston tips Stuart Armstrong to be next big thing |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dundee-united-boss-peter-houston-1395806 |newspaper=Daily Record |date=24 October 2012 |access-date=22 May 2013}}</ref> Armstrong scored his first goal of the season on 24 November, in a 2–1 win over [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee United goal hero Stuart Armstrong apologises to Jon Daly for nicking winner |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dundee-united-goal-hero-stuart-1455985 |newspaper=Daily Record |date=25 November 2012 |access-date=22 May 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite collect February SPL awards">{{cite news |title=Stuart Armstrong and Derek Adams collect February SPL awards |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/stuart-armstrong-derek-adams-win-1748447 |newspaper=Daily Record |date=7 March 2013 |access-date=22 May 2013}}</ref> Armstrong was ====2013–14====

interested in some of Dundee United's other youngsters.<ref>{{cite news |title=Celtic boss Neil Lennon eyes up move for Dundee United superkids as he looks to the future |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/celtic-boss-neil-lennon-ready-2976425 |newspaper=Daily Record |date=1 January 2014 |access-date=3 April 2014}}</ref> This was |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was also selected to the 2013–14 Premiership [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].<ref name=2014PremTofY>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27080030 |title=Celtic and Dundee United trios in SPFL Premiership team of year |date=18 April 2014 |access-date=18 April 2014 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

====2014–15====
His last match for Dundee United came in a [[New Firm (Scotland)|New Firm]] derby defeat of [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in a [[2014–15 Scottish League Cup]] semi-final on 31 January 2015.<ref name=SAandGMSleave>{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/spfl/celtic-sign-stuart-armstrong-gary-mackay-steven-1-3677908 |title=Celtic sign Stuart Armstrong & Gary Mackay-Steven |newspaper=The Scotsman |date=3 February 2015 |access-date=5 May 2015}}</ref> Armstrong made 150 appearances, starting 109 matches, and scored 22 goals in all competitions for Dundee United before joining Celtic.<ref name=SAandGMSleave/><ref name=arabarchive>[http://www.arabarchive.co.uk/player.php?id=422 Stuart Armstrong profile] Arab Arachive. Retrieved 5 May 2015.</ref>

===Celtic===
====2014–15====
In January 2015, Dundee United turned down two transfer offers from [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] for Armstrong,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31044217 |title=Stuart Armstrong: Dundee United reject Celtic and Burnley bids |date=29 January 2015 |access-date=2 February 2015 |author=Jim Spence |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> however the transfer was completed on 2 February 2015, alongside fellow Dundee United player [[Gary Mackay-Steven]].<ref name=duojoinup>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31088504 |title=Stuart Armstrong & Gary Mackay-Steven join Celtic |date=2 February 2015 |access-date=3 February 2015 |first=Jim |last=Spence |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Armstrong denied requesting the transfer.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31118674 |title=Celtic: Stuart Armstrong denies Dundee United exit request |date=3 February 2015 |access-date=3 February 2015 |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Both players would be ineligible for the remaining [[Scottish Cup]] and [[Scottish League Cup]] ties as Celtic chased a domestic treble.<ref name=duojoinup/> Armstrong and Mackay-Steven were later given the nickname [[Zig and Zag (puppets)|Zig and Zag]] by the staff at Celtic.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/spfl/stuart-armstrong-settles-in-with-celtic-nickname-1-3690250 |title=Stuart Armstrong settles in with Celtic nickname |newspaper=The Scotsman |date=14 February 2015 |access-date=5 May 2015}}</ref>

[[File:20170701 SK Rapid Wien vs Celtic FC 1329.jpg|thumb|upright|Armstrong playing for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2017]]

Armstrong scored on his Celtic debut in a 3–0 league victory at [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on 11 February 2015.<ref name=3v0partick>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/partick-thistle-0-celtic-3-5149660 |title=Partick Thistle 0 Celtic 3 |newspaper=Daily Record |date=12 February 2015 |access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref> He gave Celtic a 2–0 lead after fellow debutant Gary Mackay-Steven opened the scoring.<ref name=3v0partick/> Armstrong made his [[Celtic Park]] and European debut in a 3–3 draw with [[Inter Milan]] in the [[2014-15 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]] on 19 February 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtics-stuart-armstrong-inter-fightback-5202850 |title=Celtic's Stuart Armstrong: Inter fightback was incredible but title is still top priority |newspaper=Daily Record |date=21 February 2015 |access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/celtic/311007-gary-mackay-steven-and-stuart-armstrong-make-euro-debuts-for-hoops/ |title=Gary Mackay-Steven and Stuart Armstrong make Euro debuts for Hoops |publisher=STV Sport |date=19 February 2015 |access-date=3 May 2015 |archive-date=3 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303232741/http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/celtic/311007-gary-mackay-steven-and-stuart-armstrong-make-euro-debuts-for-hoops/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2015–16====
Armstrong made his first appearance of the [[2015–16 Celtic F.C. season|2015–16]] season in the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] second qualifying round first leg tie against [[Stjarnan]], assisting the second goal in a 2–0 home win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33500135 |title=Celtic 2:0 Stjarnan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 July 2015 |access-date=17 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="SoccerBase 201516">{{Soccerbase season|57797|2015|access-date=24 January 2016}}</ref> He scored his first goals of the season with a second-half brace, in a 4–2 league win against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 15 August.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33832093 |title=Celtic 4:2 Inverness CT |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 August 2015 |access-date=24 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/celtic-vs-inverness/342088 |title=Celtic 4–2 Inverness: Armstrong double seals Hoops win |publisher=Sky Sports |date=16 August 2015 |access-date=24 January 2016}}</ref>

====2016–17====
Armstrong scored 17 goals in all competitions as Celtic won a domestic treble.<ref name = "southampton">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44584238 |title=Stuart Armstrong: Celtic & Southampton agree terms for Scotland midfielder |first=Kenny |last=Macintyre |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 June 2018 |access-date=23 June 2018}}</ref>

====2017–18====
Celtic won a second successive domestic treble in 2017–18, but Armstrong's season was interrupted by injuries.<ref name = "southampton"/><ref name = "oct 17 injury"/> In June 2018, Celtic agreed a £7 million transfer fee for Armstrong with [[Premier League]] club [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref name = "southampton"/>

===Southampton===

==== 2018–19 ====
Armstrong signed a four-year contract with [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in June 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/14535 |title=Stuart Armstrong signs for Southampton on a four-year deal |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=26 June 2018 |access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Stuart Armstrong: Southampton sign Celtic midfielder on four-year deal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44619120 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=26 June 2018 |date=26 June 2018}}</ref> He said he wanted to "hit the ground running" at the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44626200 |title=Stuart Armstrong: Southampton signing from Celtic aims to 'hit ground running' |date=27 June 2018 |access-date=27 June 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 12 August 2018, Armstrong made his debut in a 0–0 draw against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] in the [[Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Southampton 0–0 Burnley: Alex McCarthy and Joe Hart shine in stalemate|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11470927/southampton-0-0-burnley-alex-mccarthy-and-joe-hart-shine-in-stalemate|access-date=6 March 2021|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> In November 2018, he stated that he did not miss Scottish football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46205972|title=Stuart Armstrong: Southampton's ex-Celtic midfielder doesn't miss Scottish game|date=14 November 2018|access-date=14 November 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 24 November 2018, Armstrong scored his first two goals for Southampton in a 3–2 defeat against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] in the league.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Mitrovic double earns Ranieri first win|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46244414|access-date=6 March 2021}}</ref>

==== 2019–20 ====
On 17 August 2019, Armstrong made his first league appearance of the season in a 1–2 defeat to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], replacing [[Ché Adams]] in the second half.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnston |first=Neil |date=17 August 2019 |title=Southampton 1–2 Liverpool |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49302580 |access-date=29 July 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 2 November 2019, Armstrong made his first league start of the season in a 2–1 defeat to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bevan |first=Chris |date=2 November 2019 |title=Manchester City 2–1 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50191002 |access-date=29 July 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 11 January 2020, Armstrong scored his first goal of the season in Southampton's 1–2 victory against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] at the [[King Power Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bullin |first=Matt |date=11 January 2020 |title=Leicester City 1–2 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50990601 |access-date=29 July 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 13 March 2020, the [[Premier League]] was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacInnes |first=Paul |date=13 March 2020 |title=Premier League, Football League and WSL suspended until April |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/mar/13/premier-league-and-football-league-suspended-until-4-april-coronavirus |access-date=29 July 2022 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> This meant that Armstrong and Southampton would not play again until 19 June 2020, where Armstrong scored in a 0–3 victory against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich]] at [[Carrow Road]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanders |first=Emma |date=19 June 2020 |title=Norwich 0–3 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51779559 |access-date=29 July 2020 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==== 2020–21 ====
It was announced on 1 January 2021 that Armstrong had signed a new three-and-a-half-year contract with Southampton, which will run to the summer of 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/news/2021-01-01/announcement-stuart-armstrong-new-southampton-contract-2024|title=New deal for Armstrong|website=Southampton FC|access-date=1 January 2021|archive-date=21 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210721222826/https://www.southamptonfc.com/news/2021-01-01/announcement-stuart-armstrong-new-southampton-contract-2024|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==== 2021–22 ====
On 5 February 2022, Armstrong scored in a 2–1 victory against [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in the [[FA Cup]] which was voted as goal of the fourth round.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 February 2021 |title=Southampton 2–1 Coventry: Kyle Walker-Peters strikes in extra-time but Lyanco and Armando Broja suffer injuries |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12533347/southampton-2-1-coventry-kyle-walker-peters-strikes-in-extra-time-as-saints-advance-to-fifth-round |access-date=1 October 2023 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 February 2022 |title=FA Cup: Stuart Armstrong strike voted goal of the fourth round |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60283136 |access-date=1 October 2021 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> His first league goal of the season came on 19 February 2022 in a 2–0 victory against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sutcliffe |first=Steve |date=19 February 2022 |title=Southampton 2–0 Everton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60357461 |access-date=1 October 2023 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==== 2022–23 ====
On 23 October 2022, Armstrong scored his first goal of the season in a 1–1 draw with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howarth |first=Matthew |date=23 October 2022 |title=Southampton 1–1 Arsenal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63274131 |access-date=1 October 2023 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> His only other goal of the 2022–23 season came on 30 April 2023 in a 3–1 defeat to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rose |first=Gary |date=30 April 2023 |title=Newcastle United 3–1 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65363992 |access-date=1 October 2023 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==== 2023–24 ====
Armstrong made his first appearance of the season on 4 August 2023 in a 1–2 victory against [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodcock |first=Ian |date=4 August 2023 |title=Sheffield Wednesday 1–2 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66333585 |access-date=21 April 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 3 October 2023, he scored his first goal of the campaign in a 0–1 victory against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 October 2023 |title=Stoke City 0–1 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66920480 |access-date=21 April 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> During a 2–1 defeat to [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] on 20 April 2024, he suffered an injury and was expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rees-Julian |first=George |date=20 April 2024 |title=Southampton's Stuart Armstrong sidelined until the end of season |url=https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/sport/24267221.southamptons-ross-stewart-sidelined-end-season/ |access-date=21 April 2024 |website=Southern Daily Echo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=20 April 2024 |title=Stuart Armstrong: Scotland and Southampton midfielder out for season and a doubt for Euro 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68861708 |access-date=21 April 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Armstrong was released by Southampton at the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Men's retained list published for 2024 |url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/en/news/article/mens-retained-list-published-for-2024 |access-date=4 June 2024 |work=Southampton F.C. |date=4 June 2024}}</ref>

=== Vancouver Whitecaps ===
On 3 September 2024, Armstrong joined [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] side [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC|Vancouver Whitecaps]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 September 2024 |title=Whitecaps FC sign Scottish international midfielder Stuart Armstrong to Designated Player contract |url=https://www.whitecapsfc.com/news/vwfc-sign-armstrong |access-date=3 September 2024 |website=Vancouver Whitecaps FC}}</ref> He made his Whitecaps debut in a 0–0 draw with [[FC Dallas]] on 7 September,<ref>{{cite web |title=Points split |url=https://www.whitecapsfc.com/news/points-split |website=Whitecaps FC |access-date=17 September 2024 |date=8 September 2024 |quote=Newly signed Designated Player Stuart Armstrong made his Vancouver Whitecaps FC and MLS debut}}</ref> and scored his first goal a week later in a 2–0 victory against [[San Jose Earthquakes]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Shutout streak continues, Armstrong off the mark as 'Caps serve up dominant display against San Jose |url=https://www.whitecapsfc.com/news/shutout-streak-continues-armstrong-off-the-mark-as-caps-serve-up-dominant-display-against-san-jose |website=Whitecaps FC |access-date=17 September 2024 |date=15 September 2024}}</ref>

=== Sheffield Wednesday ===
On 31 January 2025, Armstrong returned to England, joining [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Stuart Armstrong signs for Wednesday!|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2025/january/31/stuart-armstrong-signs-for-wednesday-/|access-date=31 January 2025 |publisher=Sheffield Wednesday FC |date=31 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cde9644r344o|title=Stuart Armstrong: Sheffield Wednesday sign Vancouver Whitecaps midfielder|date=31 January 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his debut the following day, coming off the bench against [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Report: Wednesday 1–1 Luton|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2025/february/01/report--wednesday-1-1-luton/|access-date=1 February 2025 |publisher=Sheffield Wednesday FC |date=1 February 2025}}</ref> He was released from his contract following the end of the [[2024–25 Sheffield Wednesday F.C. season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Owls confirm retained list|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2025/may/15/owls-confirm-/|access-date=15 May 2025 |publisher=Sheffield Wednesday FC |date=15 May 2025}}</ref>

=== Aberdeen ===
On 2 September 2025, Armstrong returned to Scotland, joining [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a 2 year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-02 |title=Scotland cap Armstrong signs for Aberdeen |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cx23243049mo |access-date=3 September 2025|website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Armstrong represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=105&playerID=51419&squadID=9 |title=Scottish Football Association – Under-19 squad |publisher=SFA}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=105&playerID=51419&squadID=5 |title=Scottish Football Association – Under-21 squad |publisher=SFA}}</ref> On 21 May 2013, Armstrong was called up for the [[Scotland national football team|senior team]], along with his Dundee United teammate [[Gary Mackay-Steven]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee United's Stuart Armstrong called up to Scotland squad |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united-s-stuart-armstrong-called-up-to-scotland-squad-1.95265 |newspaper=The Courier |date=21 May 2013 |access-date=22 May 2013}}</ref> He was called up again by the national team in August 2015,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34040001 |title=Celtic's Stuart Armstrong given Scotland call-up |work=BBC Sport |date=24 August 2015 }}</ref> and again in March 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39253748 |title=Scotland: Stuart Armstrong, Ryan Fraser & Tom Cairney called up |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 March 2017 |access-date=26 March 2017}}</ref> Armstrong made his full international debut on 26 March 2017, in a 1–0 win against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39302192 |title=Scotland 1–0 Slovenia |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 March 2017 |access-date=26 March 2017}}</ref> National team manager [[Gordon Strachan]] called it "the best Scotland debut I have ever seen."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39401778 |title=Scotland 1–0 Slovenia: Gordon Strachan hails match-winner Chris Martin |date=26 March 2017 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In September 2017 he was ruled out of two 2018 World Cup qualifying games through injury.<ref name = "oct 17 injury">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41445004 |title=World Cup 2018: Scotland duo Scott Brown and Stuart Armstrong ruled out through injury |date=29 September 2017 |access-date=23 June 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In October 2020 he pulled out of the Scotland squad for a [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] play-off semi-final against [[Israel national football team|Israel]] after testing positive for [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54453593|title=Scotland trio out after positive test|website=BBC Sport|date=7 October 2020}}</ref>

In May 2021, he was selected in the Scotland squad for the delayed [[UEFA Euro 2020]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57171330|title=Gilmour & Turnbull make Scotland squad|work=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2021 }}</ref> He played in all three of the team's [[UEFA Euro 2020 Group D|Group D]] matches, starting against both [[Czech Republic national football team|Czechia]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/match/2024452--scotland-vs-czechia/|title=Scotland vs Czechia|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref> and [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/match/2024472--croatia-vs-scotland/lineups/|title=Croatia vs Scotland: Line-ups|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref> at [[Hampden Park]] and appearing as a substitute against [[England national football team|England]] at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/026a-128d451ae1fc-603204881652-1000--england-0-0-scotland-honours-even-at-wembley/|title=England 0–0 Scotland: Honours even at Wembley|date=18 June 2021|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref>

On 26 March 2024, Armstrong won his 50th cap for Scotland in a 1–0 friendly loss to [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/match-report-scotland-v-northern-ireland/|title=Match Report: Scotland v Northern Ireland|access-date=24 June 2024|website=Scottish FA}}</ref>

On 7 June 2024, Armstrong was named in Scotland's squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2024]] finals in Germany.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/record-breaking-goalkeeper-gordon-out-scotland-euro-2024-squad-2024-06-07/|title=Record-breaking goalkeeper Gordon out of Scotland's Euro 2024 squad|date=7 June 2024|access-date=15 June 2024|website=Reuters}}</ref> He made one appearance at the tournament, coming on as a 76th minute substitute for [[John McGinn]] against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] as Scotland finished bottom of [[UEFA Euro 2024 Group A|Group A]] with one point from three matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/match/2036186--scotland-vs-hungary/lineups/|title=Scotland vs Hungary: Line-ups|access-date=24 June 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2014, Armstrong was studying for a law degree through the [[Open University]] in his spare time.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united/dundee-united-s-stuart-armstrong-favours-law-course-over-golf-course-1.298237 |title=Dundee United's Stuart Armstrong favours law course over golf course |last=Robertson |first=Neil |newspaper=The Courier |access-date=3 April 2014 |date=3 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140403181310/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united/dundee-united-s-stuart-armstrong-favours-law-course-over-golf-course-1.298237 |archive-date=3 April 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dundee-uniteds-stuart-armstrong-reveals-3338131 |title=Dundee United's Stuart Armstrong reveals he's studying for a law degree to stave off boredom |last=McDermott |first=Scott |newspaper=Daily Record |access-date=3 April 2014 |date=3 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140403182815/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dundee-uniteds-stuart-armstrong-reveals-3338131 |archive-date=3 April 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Joseph Peter Newell''' (born 15 March 1993) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Hibernia}} club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] as a [[midfielder]], where he is [[captain (association football)|captain]] and current longest-serving player, having signed for the club in 2019. Newell has previously played for [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]], [[St Albans City F.C.|St Albans City]] and [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]].

==Career==

===Peterborough United===

Newell made his debut for [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] on 25 April 2011, in a 2–2 draw at home to [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13112105 "Peterborough 2–2 Yeovil"] BBC Sport. 25 April 2011. Retrieved 2 December 2012.</ref> He made his second appearance in a 5–0 win against [[Dagenham & Redbridge F.C.|Dagenham & Redbridge]] on 7 May 2011.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13247270 "Peterborough 5–0 Dag & Red"] BBC Sport. 7 May 2011. Retrieved 2 December 2012.</ref> He began to establish himself in the team during the 2011–12 season, and scored his first goal for the club in an away match against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 14 April 2012.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17643317 "Leeds 4–1 Peterborough"] BBC Sport. 14 April 2012. Retrieved 2 December 2012.</ref> He scored his second goal for the club on 14 August 2012, helping Peterborough to a 4–0 win against [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]] in the first round of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19159760 "Peterborough 4–0 Southend"] BBC Sport. 14 August 2012. Retrieved 2 December 2012.</ref> Newell picked up the Peterborough United FC, BBC radio Cambridgeshire and away supporters player of the year awards for the 2014–15 season.

===Rotherham United===

On 5 August 2015, Newell joined [[The Football League Championship|Championship]] side [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] on a three-year deal. After four years at the club, which included a Wembley play-off final win, he left at the end of the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.themillers.co.uk/news/2019/june/read--newell-thanks-millers-for-four-memorable-years/|title=READ {{!}} Newell thanks Millers for 'four memorable years'|publisher=Rotherham United Official Site|date=5 June 2019}}</ref>

===Hibernian===

Newell signed a two-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in June 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48575308 |title=Joe Newell: Midfielder 'really excited' to join Hibs after rejecting new Rotherham contract |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 June 2019 |access-date=9 June 2019}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a [[Scottish League Cup]] tie against [[Elgin City]] on 26 July 2019.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48998287|title=Elgin 0-2 Hibernian |website=BBC Sport |date=26 July 2019 |access-date=26 January 2022}}</ref> Newell initially struggled playing in a wide-left position, but his form improved after he was moved into a central midfield role.<ref name = hibs>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-announce-new-two-year-deal-for-star-midfielder-joe-newell-3144500 |title=Hibs announce new two-year deal for star midfielder Joe Newell |first=Joel |last=Sked |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=23 February 2021 |accessdate=24 February 2021}}</ref> On 23 February 2021, Newell signed a new two-and-a-half-year deal with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], with the option to extend a further year.<ref name = hibs/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/joe-newell-to-stay-a-hibee|title=Joe Newell to stay a hibee|publisher=Hibernian FC|date=23 February 2021|access-date=23 February 2021}}</ref> He signed another new contract in March 2022, which is due to run until the end of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-news-joe-newell-pens-new-deal-tying-him-to-easter-road-until-summer-of-2025-3635793 |title=Hibs news: Joe Newell pens new deal tying him to Easter Road until summer of 2025 |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=31 March 2022 |accessdate=8 May 2023}}</ref> Newell won both the Players' Player and Supporters' Player of the year awards for the 2022–23 season.{{citation needed|date=September 2023}}
