'''Martin Callie Boyle''' (born on 25 April 1993) is a professional [[association football]] player who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Hibernia}} club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]. Born in Scotland, he represents the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia national team]]. He is a right sided [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] who is also capable of playing as a [[forward (association football)|forward]].

Boyle has previously played for [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], and Saudi club [[Al Faisaly FC|Al Faisaly]].

==Club career==
===Montrose===
Born in [[Aberdeen]], Boyle started his career with [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]]. He made his first senior appearance in a [[2009–10 Scottish Cup]] tie against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], aged 16.<ref name = "dundee signs"/>

Boyle signed a senior contract in August 2010 and scored his first goal for the first team in a victory over [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] soon after.<ref>{{cite web|title=Martin Boyle|url=http://www.montrosefc.co.uk/Players/Martin%20Boyle.html|publisher=Montrose FC|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111214085823/http://www.montrosefc.co.uk/Players/Martin%20Boyle.html|archive-date=14 December 2011}}</ref> He followed that up by scoring the winner against [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in the [[Scottish Cup]] and ended the season with four goals. Boyle signed a new deal in 2011 and made nine starts and sixteen further substitute appearances in his first season, scoring three goals. In the 2011–12 season, he claimed a starting role and made 41 appearances in all competitions, scoring 22 goals. In the final game of the season, he scored his first senior hat-trick in a 5–0 win over Clyde.<ref>{{cite web|title=Montrose 5 – 0 Clyde : Saturday, 5th May 2012 |url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/football/third/results/3409869/ |publisher=Scottish Football League |date=5 May 2012 |access-date=21 April 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130625171703/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/football/third/results/3409869/ |archive-date=25 June 2013 }}</ref>

He received an award for scoring most goals in the [[Scottish Football League]].<ref name="THE IRN-BRU SFL PHENOMENAL AWARDS SUMMARY">{{cite news|title=The Irn-Bru SFL Phenomenal Awards Summary|url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/irn-bru-sfl-end-of-season-awards-201112/ |publisher=Scottish Football League |date=25 May 2012 |access-date=21 April 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130512200207/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/irn-bru-sfl-end-of-season-awards-201112/ |archive-date=12 May 2013 }}</ref> Boyle trained with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the summer of 2012,<ref name = "dundee signs"/> but returned for pre-season training with Montrose, playing in their 2–0 defeat to Stenhousemuir on 7 July.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stenhousemuir v Montrose 07/07/12|url=http://www.montrosefc.co.uk/Match%20Reports%2012-13/StenhousemuirvMontrose070712.html|publisher=Montrose FC |date=7 July 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120728194823/http://www.montrosefc.co.uk/Match%20Reports%2012-13/StenhousemuirvMontrose070712.html|archive-date=28 July 2012 }}</ref> He made four appearances (one in the league, two in the [[Challenge Cup]] and one in the [[Scottish League Cup]]) at the outset of the new season.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Dundee===
Boyle signed for [[Scottish Premier League]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in August 2012.<ref name = "dundee signs">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19281762|title=Dundee: Martin Boyle signs from Montrose|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 August 2012|access-date=27 August 2012|archive-date=18 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120818191158/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19281762|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut coming on as a substitute for [[Jim McAlister (Scottish footballer)|Jim McAlister]] in the [[Dundee derby]] on 19 August 2012, which Dundee lost 3–0. However, he only made ten appearances in total for the club, being an unused substitute on several occasions.

In January 2013, Boyle was linked with a move to [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] on loan, but the move was cancelled due to a rule which prohibits players from playing for three clubs in one season, having already featured for Dundee and Montrose.<ref>{{cite news|title=Martin Boyle's Wasps move stung by SFL|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/martin-boyle-s-wasps-move-stung-by-sfl-1.64454|publisher=DC Thomson|work=The Courier|date=11 January 2013|access-date=21 April 2013|archive-date=7 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307032543/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/martin-boyle-s-wasps-move-stung-by-sfl-1.64454|url-status=live}}</ref> Instead, Boyle signed for his former club Montrose on loan for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/2013/02/25/martin-boyle-gets-four-for-montrose/ |title=Martin Boyle gets four for Montrose  | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191117164204/https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/2013/02/25/martin-boyle-gets-four-for-montrose/ | archive-date=17 November 2019 | date=25 February 2013 | website=Evening Telegraph }}</ref> He made his second debut for the club in a 1–1 draw against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. On the next matchday, 2 February 2013, he scored his first goal since returning in a 4–1 win over [[East Stirlingshire F.C.|East Stirlingshire]], which was the start of a run of goalscoring form. On 23 February he scored four goals in a 5–1 win over [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=SFL3 round-up: Queen's Park maintain their play-off push with first victory at Peterhead|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/sfl3-round-up-queens-park-record-1728712|work=Daily Record|date=24 February 2013|access-date=21 April 2013|archive-date=16 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016173624/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/sfl3-round-up-queens-park-record-1728712|url-status=live}}</ref> Because of his goalscoring form, Boyle was awarded February's ''Irn-Bru SFL Young Player of the Month'' award.<ref>{{cite web|title=Irn-Bru Phenomenal Young Player of the Month|url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/irn-bru-phenomenal-young-player-of-the-month/|publisher=Scottish Football League|date=15 March 2013|access-date=21 April 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130430151939/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/irn-bru-phenomenal-young-player-of-the-month/|archive-date=30 April 2013}}</ref>

Following his impressive displays at Montrose, Dundee manager [[John Brown (footballer, born 1962)|John Brown]] confirmed that Boyle would stay at the club in the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Young Dee strike duo is backed by Bomber |url=http://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/sport/dundee-fc/young-dee-strike-duo-is-backed-by-bomber-1.92781|publisher=DC Thomson |work=Evening Telegraph |date=14 May 2013|access-date=13 February 2014}}</ref> Boyle scored his first goal for the ''Dee'' in a 1–0 win over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], which was also [[Paul Hartley]]'s first match as the new Dundee manager.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dundee 1 – 0 Hamilton Academical|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/search/sport/?q=Martin%20Boyle&video=on&audio=on&text=on |publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 February 2014|access-date=13 February 2014}}{{dead link|date=September 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> After the match, Hartley praised Boyle's performance and was unaware that it was his first goal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Martin Boyle's display impresses new boss Hartley|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/martin-boyle-s-display-impresses-new-boss-hartley-1.217452|publisher=DC Thomson|work=The Courier|date=12 February 2014|access-date=13 February 2014|archive-date=22 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222141937/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/martin-boyle-s-display-impresses-new-boss-hartley-1.217452|url-status=live}}</ref> Dundee were promoted to the [[Scottish Premiership]] by winning the [[2013–14 Scottish Championship]]. [https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4960478/dundee-fc-win-league-championship-2014/ How Dundee Won The League]

Boyle made his first [[Scottish Premiership]] appearance in the 2014–15 season, coming on as a substitute for [[Greg Stewart (footballer)|Greg Stewart]] in the 62nd minute of a goalless draw with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 13 August 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle 0–0 Dundee|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28670241|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 August 2014|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season in the second round of the League Cup, in a 4–0 win over [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on 26 August.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee 4 – 0 Raith Rovers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28847745|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 August 2014|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref> Despite featuring in the first team, Boyle struggled to score his first league goal of the season, and was loaned to second-tier [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] for the second half of the 2014–15 season.<ref name ="harris / boyle"/> He was offered a new contract by Dundee after the loan was completed,<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee boss Paul Hartley offers Martin Boyle chance to resurrect career at Dens |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/dundee-boss-paul-hartley-offers-martin-boyle-chance-to-resurrect-career-at-dens-1.879706 |publisher=DC Thomson |work=The Courier |date=30 May 2015 |access-date=26 June 2015 |archive-date=26 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626190929/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/dundee-boss-paul-hartley-offers-martin-boyle-chance-to-resurrect-career-at-dens-1.879706 |url-status=live }}</ref> but he decided to sign permanently with Hibernian.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Hibernian===
Boyle moved to Hibernian in January 2015, in a loan exchange for [[Alex Harris (Scottish footballer)|Alex Harris]].<ref name="harris / boyle">{{cite news |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/dundee-sign-hibs-winger-on-loan-1.767701 |title=Dundee sign Hibs winger on loan |first=Eric |last=Nicolson |newspaper=The Courier |publisher=DC Thomson |date=3 January 2015 |access-date=3 January 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150103154326/http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-fc/dundee-sign-hibs-winger-on-loan-1.767701 |archive-date=3 January 2015 }}</ref> He made his debut on 3 January 2015 in the [[Scottish Championship]], as Hibs drew 1–1 with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in the [[Edinburgh derby]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Hearts 1 Hibernian 1|url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/5075|publisher=Hibernian F.C.|date=3 January 2015|access-date=3 January 2015|archive-date=4 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150104025145/http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/5075|url-status=live}}</ref> and scored his first goal for the club on 31 January 2015, in a 1–1 draw against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hibernian 1–1 Raith Rovers|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30963706|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 January 2015|access-date=1 February 2015}}</ref> He later scored two goals in the last two games of the season against Alloa Athletic<ref>{{cite web|title=Hibernian 4–1 Alloa Athletic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32363349|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 April 2015|access-date=26 June 2015|archive-date=29 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150429000115/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/32363349|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Falkirk 0 – 3 Hibernian |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32448139|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 May 2015|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref> but suffered a knee injury that caused him to miss the end of season play-offs.<ref>{{cite news|title=Knee injury rules Martin Boyle out of play-offs|url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/knee-injury-rules-martin-boyle-out-of-play-offs-1-3764135|newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News|date=6 May 2015|access-date=26 June 2015|archive-date=27 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150627075204/http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/knee-injury-rules-martin-boyle-out-of-play-offs-1-3764135|url-status=live}}</ref>

Boyle moved to Hibs on a permanent basis in June 2015, signing a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hibernian: Martin Boyle agrees two-year deal at Easter Road |first=Kenny |last=Crawford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33128308 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 June 2015 |access-date=14 June 2015 |archive-date=20 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920170201/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/33128308 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was an unused substitute as the club won the [[2016 Scottish Cup Final]].<ref name = "cup unused">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36292302|title=Scottish Cup final: Rangers 2–3 Hibernian – BBC Sport|date=21 May 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=21 May 2016|archive-date=5 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805010507/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36292302|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored nine goals during the 2016–17 season, as Hibs won promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership|Premiership]].<ref name = "2017 contract"/>

Boyle signed a new two-year contract with Hibernian in June 2017.<ref name = "2017 contract">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40132459 |title=Hibernian: New contracts for Martin Boyle and Liam Fontaine |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 June 2017 |access-date=2 June 2017 |archive-date=22 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222140908/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40132459 |url-status=live }}</ref> After a productive start to the 2017–18 season, this was extended to 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-winger-martin-boyle-agrees-contract-extension-1-4633938 |title=Hibs winger Martin Boyle agrees contract extension |first=David |last=Hardie |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=7 December 2017 |access-date=8 December 2017 |archive-date=18 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918054252/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-winger-martin-boyle-agrees-contract-extension-1-4633938 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Having made 25 appearances in the first part of the 2018–19 season, Boyle underwent surgery on a knee injury sustained on international duty in January 2019,<ref name = "oman injury"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46813343 |title=Martin Boyle: Hibs winger likely to miss rest of the season |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 January 2019 |access-date=10 January 2019}}</ref> which prevented him playing any further part in the campaign.

Boyle returned to first team action in July 2019, but suffered a recurrence of the knee injury during a League Cup match at [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]].<ref name = elgin/> He was not expected to return to playing until 2020,<ref name = elgin>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49172332 |title=Hibernian: Martin Boyle set to be out until 2020 with knee injury |first=Richard |last=Winton |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 July 2019 |access-date=30 July 2019 |archive-date=30 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730210516/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49172332 |url-status=live }}</ref> but he returned sooner than expected and made his comeback on 30 October.<ref name = Livi/> Boyle scored an injury-time equaliser to earn Hibs a 2–2 draw with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]],<ref name = Livi>{{cite web|title=Hibernian 2–2 Livingston|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50148208|publisher=BBC Sport|last=McLauchlin|first=Brian|date=30 October 2019|access-date=31 October 2019|archive-date=30 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191030220540/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50148208|url-status=live}}</ref> following this up in December with doubles against [[Aberdeen]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Hibernian 3–0 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50611280|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Southwick|first=Andrew|date=7 December 2019}}</ref> and in the [[Edinburgh derby]] against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Heart of Midlothian 0–2 Hibernian|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50847215|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Moffat|first=Colin|date=26 December 2019|access-date=27 December 2019|archive-date=27 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191227120706/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50847215|url-status=live}}</ref> These performances led to Boyle being named as Premiership [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|player of the month]] for December 2019.<ref name = "dec 2019"/>

In August 2020, Boyle and Hibs agreed a new contract, which is due to run until the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53923371 |title=Martin Boyle: Hibs extend contract until 2023 a day after wife's new deal |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=26 August 2020 |access-date=26 August 2020 |archive-date=6 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306115234/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53923371 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name = afcbid>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58241478 |title=Martin Boyle: Hibs winger signs new deal after Aberdeen's £500,000 bid rejected |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |website=BBC Sport |date=18 August 2021 |accessdate=17 August 2021 |archive-date=17 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817085950/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58241478 |url-status=live }}</ref> During March 2021 Boyle was criticised by [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] manager [[John Hughes (footballer, born 1964)|John Hughes]] for "conning the referee" to win a [[penalty kick (association football)|penalty]].<ref name = simulation>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56729984 |title=Martin Boyle: Hibs winger says he is 'most fouled player', not a diver |website=BBC Sport |date=13 April 2021 |accessdate=13 April 2021}}</ref> A few weeks later Boyle was booked for [[Diving (association football)|simulation]] during a match with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], after which Boyle argued that he needed protection from referees because he was one of the most fouled players in the Scottish league.<ref name = simulation/>

Hibs rejected an offer of £500,000 from [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] for Boyle in August 2021.<ref name = afcbid/> Later that month, Boyle signed a new contract with Hibs that was due to run until the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref name = afcbid/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/martin-boyle-stays-with-hibernian-after-signing-extended-deal?top |title=Martin Boyle stays with Hibernian after signing extended deal |first=Jamie |last=Borthwick |website=STV Sport |date=18 August 2021 |accessdate=18 August 2021 |archive-date=18 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818124927/https://news.stv.tv/sport/martin-boyle-stays-with-hibernian-after-signing-extended-deal?top |url-status=live }}</ref> Boyle won the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners#2021–22 season|Scottish Premiership Player of the Month]] for August 2021, having scored four goals in four league games that month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-martin-boyle-talks-big-ambitions-after-winning-premiership-player-of-the-month-3378775|title=Hibs: Martin Boyle talks 'big ambitions' after winning Premiership Player of the Month|work=www.edinburghnews.com|first=Matthew|last=Elder|date=10 September 2021|access-date=10 September 2021|archive-date=10 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210910133545/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-martin-boyle-talks-big-ambitions-after-winning-premiership-player-of-the-month-3378775|url-status=live}}</ref> A first-half hat-trick against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] earned Hibs a place in the [[2021 Scottish League Cup Final (December)|League Cup final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58479245 |title=Martin Boyle: From chasing pigeons to Hampden hat-tricks - the rise and rise of Hibs & Australia forward |first=Nick |last=McPheat |website=BBC Sport |date=21 November 2021 |accessdate=21 November 2021 |archive-date=21 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211121201635/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58479245 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59373810 |title=Hibs beat Rangers: Globe-trotting Martin Boyle cleans up at Hampden |first=Tom |last=English |website=BBC Sport |date=22 November 2021 |accessdate=22 November 2021 |archive-date=22 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122113503/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59373810 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Al-Faisaly ===
On 21 January 2022, Boyle left Hibs for an "undisclosed seven-figure sum" to join [[Saudi Professional League]] club [[Al Faisaly FC|Al-Faisaly]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Martin Boyle Joins Al-Faisaly|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/transfer-martin-boyle-joins-al-faisaly|access-date=21 January 2022|website=Hibernian FC|language=en-US|archive-date=21 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121094845/https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/transfer-martin-boyle-joins-al-faisaly|url-status=live}}</ref> The club were relegated at the end of the [[2021–22 Saudi Professional League|2021–22]] season, which led to speculation that Boyle would return to Scotland.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.scottishdailyexpress.co.uk/sport/football/martin-boyle-stay-saudi-despite-27353030 |title=Martin Boyle to stay in Saudi despite relegation with Hibs return now off the table |newspaper=Scottish Daily Express |first=Scott |last=Burns |date=29 June 2022 |accessdate=8 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2022/august/hibernian-boss-lee-johnson-interested-in-re-signing-martin-boyle |title=Hibernian boss Lee Johnson interested in re-signing Martin Boyle |website=BT Sport |date=3 August 2022 |accessdate=8 August 2022 |archive-date=19 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220819145358/https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2022/august/hibernian-boss-lee-johnson-interested-in-re-signing-martin-boyle |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Hibernian (second spell) ===
On 6 August 2022, [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] announced that an agreement had been reached with [[Al-Faisaly FC|Al-Faisaly]] on the transfer and subsequent re-signing of Boyle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/update-martin-boyle|title=Update: Martin Boyle|publisher=Hibernian FC|date=6 August 2022|access-date=19 May 2024 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817015431/https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/update-martin-boyle |archivedate=17 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62448714|title=Martin Boyle returns to Hibernian after brief stint in Saudi Arabia|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Brian|last=McLauchlin|date=6 August 2022|access-date=6 August 2022|archive-date=6 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806142300/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62448714|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored on his second debut for Hibs a day later, a late equaliser in an [[Edinburgh derby]] with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62366370 |first=Andrew |last=Petrie |title=Hibernian 1-1 Heart of Midlothian: Boyle earns hosts dramatic draw |website=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2022 |accessdate=7 August 2022 |archive-date=7 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807140716/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62366370 |url-status=live }}</ref> Boyle suffered a knee injury during a match with [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 29 October that eventually forced him to withdraw from the Australia squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]].<ref name = withdraw>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63693807 |title=World Cup 2022: Hibs' Martin Boyle forced out of Australia's finals squad through injury |website=BBC Sport |date=20 November 2022 |accessdate=27 December 2022}}</ref> When he underwent surgery on his knee, a much more serious tear to his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) was detected.<ref name = acl/> The recovery from that operation took several months,<ref name = acl/> with Boyle making his return to competitive action in August 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66383942 |title=Hibernian 6-1 Inter Club D'Escaldes (agg 7-3): Scottish side through in Europa Conference League |website=BBC Sport |date=3 August 2023 |accessdate=1 September 2023 |first=Amy |last=Canavan}}</ref>

After a 2024–25 season in which Boyle's goals and assists helped the team qualify for European competition, Hibs exercised an option to extend his contract by one year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cq69g6ndq13o |title=Hibs trigger extension to keep Boyle |website=BBC Sport |date=16 May 2025 |accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref> He scored his 100th competitive goal for Hibs during a 2–0 win against [[FK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] in August 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/czjm4r0nm1go |title=Dad advice helps Boyle break 100 as Chaiwa signs |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |date=8 August 2025 |accessdate=8 August 2025 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Hibs manager [[David Gray (footballer, born 1988)|David Gray]] said Boyle would leave the club at the end of the 2025–26, following the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c62dedk4qnlo  |title=Gray confirms Boyle exit and says star should 'go out on a high' |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |website=BBC Sport |date=13 March 2026 |accessdate=9 April 2026}}</ref> On 16 May 2026 however, shortly before the final match of the season kicked off, he signed a new one-year contract.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2026/may/16/test/|title=Martin Boyle Pens One-Year Contract Extension|website=www.hibernianfc.co.uk|date=16 May 2026|accessdate=16 May 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
===Scotland youth===
Boyle played for the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland under-16 team]].<ref name = "aussie"/>

===Australia===
Boyle was eligible to play for Scotland, the land of his birth, and [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia national team]], as his father Graeme was born in Sydney.<ref name = "aussie"/> He currently holds dual citizenship in both Australia and the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sundaypost.com/fp/video-hibs-star-martin-boyle-nets-his-first-international-goals-for-australia/ |title=Hibs star Martin Boyle nets his first international goals for Australia |publisher=The Sunday Post |date=20 November 2018 |access-date=10 November 2022}}</ref> In March 2018, Boyle said that he had applied for an Australian passport.<ref name = "aussie">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43597570 |title=Martin Boyle: Hibernian winger considers representing Australia |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 March 2018 |access-date=1 April 2018 |archive-date=2 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181102192450/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43597570 |url-status=live }}</ref> Australia manager [[Graham Arnold]] had a meeting with Boyle in September 2018, with a view to selecting him in their next squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45686013 |title=Martin Boyle may choose to play for Scotland or Australia - Neil Lennon |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 September 2018 |access-date=30 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/worldcup/qatar2022/news/boyle-looking-for-more-glory-with-high-flying-socceroos |title=Boyle looking for more glory with high-flying Socceroos |date=6 October 2021 |accessdate=7 October 2021 |website=www.fifa.com |publisher=FIFA |archive-date=7 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007200524/https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/worldcup/qatar2022/news/boyle-looking-for-more-glory-with-high-flying-socceroos |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] manager [[Alex McLeish]] said that he had considered Boyle for selection in May 2018, but he had missed out due to injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45707466 |title=Scotland recall Scott McKenna, Jack Hendry, Jon McLaughlin & Oli McBurnie for Israel & Portugal games |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 October 2018 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001134845/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45707466 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Boyle was selected for the Australia squad in October 2018, but was unable to play in their match with [[Kuwait national football team|Kuwait]] as he did not yet have an Australian passport.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ftbl.com.au/news/martin-boyle-arnold-meeting-wooed-me-513823 |title=MARTIN BOYLE: ARNOLD MEETING WOOED ME |first=Ben |last=Somerford |work=ftbl.com.au |date=11 October 2018 |access-date=11 October 2018 |archive-date=11 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011133732/https://www.ftbl.com.au/news/martin-boyle-arnold-meeting-wooed-me-513823 |url-status=live }}</ref> Boyle made his international debut for Australia on 17 November, coming on as a substitute for striker and club teammate [[Jamie Maclaren]] in a friendly match against [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] at [[Lang Park]], [[Brisbane]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/martin-boyle-makes-debut-as-hibs-trio-feature-for-australia-against-south-korea-1-4831347 |title=Martin Boyle makes debut as Hibs trio feature for Australia against South Korea |work=Edinburgh Evening News |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=17 November 2018 |access-date=17 November 2018 |archive-date=17 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181117193127/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/martin-boyle-makes-debut-as-hibs-trio-feature-for-australia-against-south-korea-1-4831347 |url-status=live }}</ref> In his first start for Australia, Boyle scored two goals and set up the other in a 3–0 win against [[Lebanon national football team|Lebanon]] on 20 November.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/nov/20/martin-boyle-states-socceroos-case-with-brace-as-tim-cahill-bids-farewell?CMP=twt_gu |title=Martin Boyle states Socceroos case with brace as Tim Cahill bids farewell |first=Mike |last=Hytner |work=The Guardian |date=20 November 2018 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref> He was selected for the [[2019 AFC Asian Cup]] squad,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46630908 |title=Celtic and Hibs face derby absences after Australia call-ups for Asia Cup |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 December 2018 |access-date=20 December 2018 |archive-date=20 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220140024/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46630908 |url-status=live }}</ref> but had to withdraw due to a knee injury sustained in a warm-up match against [[Oman national football team|Oman]].<ref name = "oman injury">{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-martin-boyle-out-for-indefinite-period-after-suffering-knee-injury-with-australia-1-4850852 |title=Hibs' Martin Boyle out for 'indefinite' period after suffering knee injury with Australia |first=Mark |last=Atkinson |work=Edinburgh Evening News |date=1 January 2019 |access-date=1 January 2019 |archive-date=2 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190102154855/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-martin-boyle-out-for-indefinite-period-after-suffering-knee-injury-with-australia-1-4850852 |url-status=live }}</ref>

He was recalled to the Australia squad in November 2019, soon after recovering from a knee operation.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/sport/football/tom-rogic-and-martin-boyle-give-socceroos-more-firepower-for-jordan/news-story/5bc31bdee86409a6643b05bdc7d0035a |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191108130806/https://www.theaustralian.com.au/sport/football/tom-rogic-and-martin-boyle-give-socceroos-more-firepower-for-jordan/news-story/5bc31bdee86409a6643b05bdc7d0035a |url-status=live |archive-date=8 November 2019 |title=Tom Rogic and Martin Boyle give Socceroos more firepower for Jordan |newspaper=The Australian |first=Tom |last=Smithies |date=8 November 2019 |access-date=8 November 2019}}</ref>

Boyle was named in Australia's squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in November 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 November 2022 |title=SOCCEROOS SQUAD ANNOUNCED: FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022™ |url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/socceroos-squad-announced-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022tm |access-date=9 November 2022 |website=Socceroos |language=en |archive-date=8 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108050206/https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/socceroos-squad-announced-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022tm |url-status=live }}</ref> However, he was ruled out of the tournament on 20 November 2022 after succumbing to a knee injury; he was replaced in the squad by [[Marco Tilio]].<ref name = withdraw/><ref>{{cite web |title=Martin Boyle withdrawn from Socceroos' FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022™ squad |url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/martin-boyle-withdrawn-socceroos-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022tm-squad |website=Socceroos |date=20 November 2022 |access-date=20 November 2022 |archive-date=20 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221120110303/https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/martin-boyle-withdrawn-socceroos-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022tm-squad |url-status=live }}</ref> Despite being unable to take part, he stayed with the squad in Qatar to show support for his teammates, as Australia reached the last sixteen for the second time.<ref name = acl>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63791861 |title=Martin Boyle: Hibs & Australia forward might have had knee issue for seven years |website=BBC Sport |date=29 November 2022 |accessdate=27 December 2022 |archive-date=27 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221227114249/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63791861 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pirie |first=Mark |date=2022-11-26 |title=Martin Boyle shows Australia support at the World Cup amid injury nightmare |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/martin-boyle-ultimate-show-australia-28588940 |access-date=2022-12-05 |newspaper=Daily Record |language=en |archive-date=5 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205153335/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/martin-boyle-ultimate-show-australia-28588940 |url-status=live }}</ref>

After regaining fitness following his knee injury, Boyle was recalled to the squad in September 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/sep/01/socceroos-australia-vs-mexico-friendly-squad |title=Graham Arnold adds new faces to Socceroos squad for Mexico friendly |newspaper=The Guardian |date=1 September 2023 |accessdate=1 September 2023 |first=Mike |last=Hytner |archive-date=1 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230901101711/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/sep/01/socceroos-australia-vs-mexico-friendly-squad |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored a [[penalty kick|penalty]] and assisted the other Australia goal for another Scottish-born footballer, [[Harry Souttar]], in his first international since returning from injury, a 2–2 draw with [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] on 9 September.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-09-10/socceroos-draw-2-2-with-mexico-in-dallas-texas/102837846 |title=Socceroos draw 2-2 with Mexico in Dallas, with Jackson Irvine suffering ankle injury |website=ABC News |date=10 September 2023 |accessdate=10 September 2023 |archive-date=10 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230910090119/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-09-10/socceroos-draw-2-2-with-mexico-in-dallas-texas/102837846 |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Boyle helped the ''Socceroos'' qualify for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026 World Cup]], setting up the winning goal in a 2–1 victory against [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]] that clinched a place in the finals,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cgkd5p1802po |title=Hibs: Martin Boyle and Lewis Miller help Australia qualify for World Cup |website=BBC Sport |date=10 June 2025 |accessdate=11 June 2025}}</ref> but was one of four players cut from the squad selected for the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cdxp53k7qv1o |title=World Cup 2026: Uncapped Tete Yengi and Cristian Volpato make Australia squad |website=BBC Sport |date=31 May 2026 |accessdate=1 June 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2012, Boyle began a relationship with Aberdonian [[Scotland women's national football team|Scotland women's international]] footballer [[Rachael Boyle|Rachael Small]]; they had known each other since their schooldays at [[Northfield Academy]]. They were engaged in 2016, with Rachael moving to [[Edinburgh]] to play for [[Hibernian W.F.C.|Hibernian Women]]. Their daughter Amelia was born in 2018, and they married in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/news/people/hibs-winger-martin-boyle-ties-the-knot-with-fellow-easter-road-star-rachael-small-1-4948987/amp |title=Hibs winger Martin Boyle ties the knot with fellow Easter Road star Rachael Small |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=18 June 2019 |access-date=18 June 2019 |archive-date=18 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190618215535/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/news/people/hibs-winger-martin-boyle-ties-the-knot-with-fellow-easter-road-star-rachael-small-1-4948987/amp |url-status=live }}</ref> Due to the upheaval it would cause to their daughter, Rachael opted to stay in Edinburgh when Martin left Hibs to play in Saudi Arabia in January 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/rachael-boyle-staying-at-hibs-as-husband-martin-goes-to-saudi-arabia-3537672 |title=Rachael Boyle staying at Hibs as husband Martin Boyle goes to Saudi Arabia to set family up for life |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=21 January 2022 |access-date=7 April 2022 |archive-date=25 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220425011813/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/rachael-boyle-staying-at-hibs-as-husband-martin-goes-to-saudi-arabia-3537672 |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Christopher Cadden''' (born 19 September 1996) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right-back]] for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]. Cadden, who is a product of the [[Motherwell F.C. Reserve and Youth squads|Motherwell Academy]], has previously played for Motherwell, [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]], [[Columbus Crew SC|Columbus Crew]], [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]], and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]. He made two full international appearance for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in May 2018.

==Club career==
=== Motherwell ===
Cadden made his Motherwell debut as a substitute in a 4–1 win against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] on 1 March 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26300976|title=Motherwell 4–1 Hearts|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=1 March 2014|access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref> On 6 March 2015, Cadden joined [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2015/03/06/cadden-joins-rovers-on-loan/|title=Cadden joins Rovers on loan|publisher=[[Motherwell F.C.]]|date=6 March 2014|accessdate=7 March 2014}}</ref> Cadden scored his first career goal on 4 April 2015, as Albion Rovers beat [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]] 2–0,<ref>{{cite web|title=Albion 2–0 Berwick|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32088119|work=BBC Sport|date=4 April 2015|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref> and another in Albion Rovers' league-winning match against [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]]. His loan spell concluded with the club being [[2014–15 Scottish League Two|promoted as divisional winners]].<ref name="youthcup" /> On 30 January 2016, Cadden scored his first goal for Motherwell in a 2–2 draw away to [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee 2–2 Motherwell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35389624|work=BBC Sport|last=Davie|first=Scott|date=30 January 2016|accessdate=1 August 2016}}</ref> In March 2016, he signed a new contract with the club to run until the summer of 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mark McGhee: Motherwell starlet Chris Cadden has a bright future |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/14343455.Mark_McGhee__Motherwell_starlet_Chris_Cadden_has_a_bright_future/|work=Evening Times|date=14 March 2016|accessdate=19 May 2016}}</ref> By now establishing himself in the first team, he also contributed to Motherwell's Under-20s winning the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] for the first time.<ref name="youthcup">{{cite web|title=Chris Cadden: Dad lost Youth Cup final with Motherwell – I'm out to go one better|url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/news/14454811.amp/|work=Evening Times|date=27 April 2016|accessdate=30 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/14463034.Dom_Thomas_looks_to_Motherwell_future_after_cup_success/ |title=Dom Thomas looks to Motherwell future after cup success |work=[[The Evening Times]] |date=29 April 2016 |accessdate=30 May 2018}}</ref> Cadden signed another contract with Motherwell in November 2016, extending its term by another year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/cadden-signs-new-deal-with-motherwell/ |title=Cadden signs new deal with Motherwell |publisher=SPFL |date=4 November 2016 |accessdate=5 November 2016}}</ref> He played in the finals of the [[2017–18 Scottish League Cup|2017–18]]<ref name="lc1718">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42056522 |title=Motherwell 0 – 2 Celtic|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC |accessdate=30 May 2018 |date=26 November 2017}}</ref> League Cup and the [[2017–18 Scottish Cup]],<ref name="sc1718">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44091573 |title=Celtic 2 – 0 Motherwell |work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=BBC |accessdate=19 May 2018|date=30 May 2018}}</ref> both of which resulted in 2–0 defeats for Motherwell at the hands of [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].

=== Columbus Crew SC ===
On 23 July 2019, [[free agent]] Cadden signed for [[Major League Soccer]] side [[Columbus Crew SC]]; it was announced that he would be immediately loaned to English club [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] and would join the Crew in advance of the 2020 season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Murphy|first=Pat|url=https://www.massivereport.com/2019/7/23/20707321/columbus-crew-sign-midfielder-chris-cadden-loan-him-for-remainder-of-2019-motherwall-oxford-united|title=Crew sign midfielder Chris Cadden; loan him for remainder of 2019|website=MassiveReport.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|accessdate=23 July 2019|date=23 July 2019|archive-date=11 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811232817/https://www.massivereport.com/2019/7/23/20707321/columbus-crew-sign-midfielder-chris-cadden-loan-him-for-remainder-of-2019-motherwall-oxford-united|url-status=dead}}</ref> Motherwell stated they would negotiate for a training compensation fee, due to no formal arrangement being in place with MLS in respect of clubs which had developed a young player receiving a payment when they left out of contract.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49070898 Motherwell: Chris Cadden move to MLS could cost club 280,000 euros], BBC Sport, 22 July 2019</ref>

==== Loan to Oxford United ====
Cadden made his Oxford debut in a 1–1 draw at [[Sunderland F.C.|Sunderland]] on the opening day of the [[2019–20 Oxford United F.C. season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oufc.co.uk/matches/fixtures/first-team/201920/august/sunderland-vs-oxford-united-on-03-aug-19/ |title=REPORT Sunderland 1 Oxford United 1 |publisher=Oxford United F.C. |first=Chris |last=Williams |date=3 August 2019 |accessdate=3 August 2019}}</ref> During Cadden's loan spell, he made 21 appearances for Oxford and was widely considered one of the best right backs in [[EFL League One]].<ref name=sw/> Oxford manager [[Karl Robinson]] looked to make the loan permanent, but had its advances rejected by the Crew.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/sport/18133627.chris-cadden-bids-farewell-oxford-united/|title=Chris Cadden bids farewell to Oxford United as Columbus Crew trigger recall|website=Oxford Mail|date=2 January 2020 |language=en|access-date=2 March 2020}}</ref>

==== Return to Columbus ====
Cadden started the 2020 season as depth at both the wing and wing-back positions, but was widely considered the successor to 33-year-old Ghanaian [[Harrison Afful]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Myers|first=Jacob|title=Crew's Chris Cadden pushing himself in reserve role|url=https://www.dispatch.com/sports/20200226/crewrsquos-chris-cadden-pushing-himself-in-reserve-role|access-date=2 March 2020|website=The Columbus Dispatch|language=en|archive-date=2 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302164644/https://www.dispatch.com/sports/20200226/crewrsquos-chris-cadden-pushing-himself-in-reserve-role|url-status=dead}}</ref> Cadden made his debut for the Crew against [[New York City FC]] in the first game of the season.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Columbus Crew vs. New York City|url=https://matchcenter.mlssoccer.com/matchcenter/2020-03-01-columbus-crew-sc-vs-new-york-city-fc/feed|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302004526/https://matchcenter.mlssoccer.com/matchcenter/2020-03-01-columbus-crew-sc-vs-new-york-city-fc/feed |archive-date=2 March 2020 |access-date=|website=MLS}}</ref> He came on in the 87th minute for fellow debutant [[Lucas Zelarayán]].<ref name=":0" /> In December 2020 he was part of the squad that won the [[MLS Cup 2020|MLS Cup]]. In January, it was reported that Cadden would likely leave the club in a bid to gain more playing time; it was noted that his transition to America was made difficult by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Guldan|first=Patrick|date=5 January 2021|title=Chris Cadden likely to depart the Crew as reports of Scottish transfer intensify|url=https://www.massivereport.com/2021/1/5/22213164/chris-cadden-likely-to-depart-the-columbus-crew-as-reports-of-scottish-transfer-intensify|access-date=15 January 2021|website=Massive Report|language=en|archive-date=9 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809070023/https://www.massivereport.com/2021/1/5/22213164/chris-cadden-likely-to-depart-the-columbus-crew-as-reports-of-scottish-transfer-intensify|url-status=dead}}</ref> Cadden was linked with a return to Great Britain with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], and [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibs set to complete signing of former Motherwell starlet Chris Cadden|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/soccer/hibs-set-to-complete-signing-of-former-motherwell-starlet-chris-cadden/ar-BB1cr6ld?ocid=uxbndlbing|access-date=15 January 2021|website=www.msn.com}}</ref>

=== Hibernian ===
On 15 January 2021, Cadden returned home to Scotland, signing for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on a two-and-a-half-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/chris-cadden-is-a-hibee|title=Chris Cadden is a Hibee!|publisher=Hibernian FC|date=15 January 2021|access-date=15 January 2021}}</ref> He signed a new contract with Hibs in August 2022, which is due to run until the end of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c72zqvwdvd6o |title=Chris Cadden signs new Hibs contract until summer of 2025 |website=BBC Sport |date=5 August 2022 |accessdate=8 May 2023}}</ref> Cadden suffered an [[achilles tendon]] injury during the last game of the 2022–23 season, which prevented him from playing for several months.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/chris-cadden-ruled-out-for-months-after-achilles-surgery |first=Jamie |last=Borthwick |title=Chris Cadden ruled out for months after Achilles surgery |website=STV News |date=1 June 2023 |accessdate=10 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/chris-cadden-eyes-coaching-move-as-hibs-defender-reveals-he-missed-his-own-stag-do-through-injury-4225802 |title=Chris Cadden eyes coaching move as Hibs defender reveals he missed his own stag-do through injury |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date= 20 July 2023 |accessdate=10 September 2023 |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin}}</ref> He made his first appearance since the injury on 10 February 2024, in a [[2023–24 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] tie against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/it-was-emotional-returning-hibs-star-wowed-by-team-mates-show-of-support-4513646 |title='It was emotional' - returning Hibs star wowed by team-mates' show of support |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=11 February 2024 |accessdate=12 February 2024 |first=John |last=Greechan}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
Cadden signed a two-year contract with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 31 July 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cd0xdnmgxpxo |title=Aberdeen by Chris Cadden from Hibs as right-back seeks game time |website=BBC Sport |date=31 July 2026 |accessdate=31 July 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Украина U-21 - Шотландия U-21 4-0. 6 сентября 2016 года — 708159.jpg|thumb|Cadden (No 18) with [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21s]] in Ukraine, 2016]]
In August 2016, Cadden was named in the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad for the first time ahead of the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification Group 3|European Under-21 Championship qualifiers]] against [[Macedonia national under-21 football team|Macedonia]] and [[Ukraine national under-21 football team|Ukraine]], receiving the call having initially been left out the squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Scotland U21s: Cadden & Hendrie replace Macleod & McFadzean|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37206416|work=BBC Sport|date=28 August 2016|accessdate= 10 September 2016}}</ref> He made his debut against Ukraine on 6 September 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ukraine U21 4 – 0 Scotland U21: Hearts' John Souttar sent off|url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/scotland/ukraine-u21-4-0-scotland-u21-hearts-john-souttar-sent-off-1-4222815|work=The Scotsman|date=6 September 2016|accessdate=10 September 2016}}</ref>

On 17 May 2018, Cadden was called up to the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad for the first time ahead of their friendlies against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] and [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]];<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Cadden gets Scotland call|url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2018/05/17/chris-cadden-gets-scotland-call/|website=motherwellfc.co.uk|publisher=Motherwell F.C.|accessdate=17 May 2018|date=17 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44159498 |title=Chris Cadden: Scotland add Motherwell midfielder to squad for friendlies |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=17 May 2018 |accessdate=17 May 2018}}</ref> he made his full Scotland debut on 29 May, in a 2–0 defeat to Peru.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44219810 |title=Peru 2–0 Scotland |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=30 May 2018 |accessdate=30 May 2018}}</ref>

'''Marius Müller''' (born 12 July 1993) is a German professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref name="soccerway">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/marius--muller/232583/|title=Germany - M. Mûller - Profile with news, career statistics and history - Soccerway|publisher=soccerway.com|accessdate=5 June 2023}}</ref>

==Club career==

===1 FC Kaiserslautern===
Müller joined [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]] in 2002 from TV 1883 Lampertheim. He made his [[2. Bundesliga]] debut at 11 May 2014 against [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] in a 4–2 away loss.<ref name="soccerway2">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/05/11/germany/2-bundesliga/dusseldorfer-tus-fortuna-1895-ev/1-fc-kaiserslautern/1487011/|title=Fortuna Düsseldorf vs. Kaiserslautern - Soccerway|publisher=soccerway.com|accessdate=18 August 2014}}</ref>

===RB Leipzig===
In June 2016, he moved to [[RB Leipzig]] agreeing to a three-contract. The transfer fee paid to Kaiserslautern was reported as about €1.7 million.<ref>{{cite news|title=Leipzig verpflichtet FCK-Keeper Müller|url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-verpflichtet-fck-keeper-mueller-653868/artikel|access-date=7 July 2017|work=kicker Online|date=14 June 2016|language=German}}</ref> In July 2017, Müller returned to 1. FC Kaiserslautern from RB Leipzig, on a one-year loan.<ref>{{cite news|title=Keeper Müller kehrt nach Kaiserslautern zurück|url=https://www.kicker.de/ein-jahr-leihe_keeper-mueller-zurueck-in-kaiserslautern-701166/artikel|access-date=7 July 2017|work=kicker Online|date=7 July 2017|language=German}}</ref>

===Luzern===
On 5 July 2019, Müller signed for [[Swiss Super League]] club [[FC Luzern]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Marius Müller per sofort zum FCL |url=https://fcl.ch/publication/neuer-torhueter-fuer-den-fcl/ |website=FC Luzern |access-date=22 June 2023 |language=German}}</ref>

===Schalke 04===
On 22 June 2023, Müller signed a two-year contract with recently relegated [[2. Bundesliga]] club [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]].<ref>{{cite web |title=S04 sign goalkeeper Marius Müller |url=https://schalke04.de/en/team/marius-muller-transfer/ |website=FC Schalke 04 |access-date=22 June 2023 }}</ref>

===VfL Wolfsburg===
On 4 June 2024, Müller joined [[Bundesliga]] club [[VfL Wolfsburg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vfl-wolfsburg.de/en/newsdetails/news-detail/detail/news/goalkeeper-joins-wolves|title=Goalkeeper joins Wolves|website=VfL Wolfsburg|date=4 June 2024}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
On 15 July 2026, Müller signed a two-year contract with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in Scotland.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/en/news/marius-mueller-joins-the-dons|title=Marius Müller joins The Dons|date=15 July 2026|access-date=17 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Felix Passlack''' (born 29 May 1998) is a German professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] or [[right wing-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].

==Club career==
===Borussia Dortmund===
On 2 March 2016, Passlack made his professional debut in the [[Bundesliga]] in a 2–0 win against [[SV Darmstadt 98|Darmstadt 98]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Ramos und Durm grooven sich auf Bayern ein|url=https://www.kicker.de/darmstadt-gegen-dortmund-2016-bundesliga-2855148/analyse|access-date=29 May 2016|publisher=kicker|date=20 March 2016|language=de}}</ref> He also played in a 3–1 win against [[FC Augsburg]] and a 3–0 win during the [[2015–16 Borussia Dortmund season|2015–16 season]].<ref name="2015–16 season">{{cite web|title=Felix Passlack|url=https://www.kicker.de/felix-passlack/spieler/bundesliga/2024-25/vfl-bochum|website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|publisher=kicker|access-date=29 May 2016|language=de}}</ref>

==== Loan to TSG Hoffenheim ====
On 30 August 2017, Passlack extended his contract with [[Borussia Dortmund]] and was loaned out to [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|TSG Hoffenheim]] for two years. The loan spell at TSG Hoffenheim was terminated early in July 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2018-19/1/tm-news--24501-8760-.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702150808/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2018-19/1/tm-news--24501-8760-.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 July 2018 |title=Dortmunds Passlack löst Leihvertrag bei Hoffenheim auf |publisher=Kicker |language=de |access-date=July 2, 2018}}</ref>

==== Loan to Norwich City ====
On 2 July 2018, Passlack signed for [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2018/july/passlack-signs/|title=City sign Felix Passlack on season loan}}</ref> He only made one league appearance as Norwich were promoted to the [[Premier League]] as winners of the [[2018–19 EFL Championship]].<ref>{{Soccerbase season|87933|2018|name=Felix Passlack|access-date=2019-05-14}}</ref>

==== Loan to Fortuna Sittard ====
On 2 July 2019, Passlack signed for [[Eredivisie]] side [[Fortuna Sittard]] on a season-long loan.<ref name="Loan">{{cite web|url=https://www.bvb.de/eng/News/Overview/Felix-Passlack-joins-Fortuna-Sittard-on-loan|title=Felix Passlack joins Fortuna Sittard on loan|publisher=Borussia Dortmund|access-date=July 2, 2019}}</ref>

===VfL Bochum===
On 20 April 2023, Passlack joined [[Bundesliga]] club [[VfL Bochum]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 April 2023 |language=de |publisher=VfL Bochum |title=VfL verpflichtet Felix Passlack |url=https://www.vfl-bochum.de/de/news/2023/april/20/vfl-verpflichtet-felix-passlack |access-date=29 June 2023}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
Passlack moved to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 2 February 2026, signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cvgxy9x5535o  |title=Felix Passlack: Hibs sign Bochum wing-back on three-and-a-half year deal |website=BBC Sport |date=2 February 2026 |accessdate=2 February 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
In 2014, Passlack made six appearances for Germany at [[Germany national under-16 football team|under-16 level]] and in the same year he debuted for the [[Germany national under-17 football team|Germany U17 team]]. In May 2015, Passlack was selected to [[Captain (association football)|captain]] the Germany squad at the [[2015 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]] in [[Bulgaria]], he played every single minute of the tournament, scoring three goals and helping Germany reach the final where they lost 4–1 to [[France national under-17 football team|France]].<ref name="U17 runner-up">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under17/news/0252-0cdbb5257619-d0909441b152-1000--edouard-treble-gives-france-second-u17-title/|title=Édouard treble gives France second U17 title|last=Harrison|first=Wayne|publisher=UEFA|date=22 May 2015|access-date=27 July 2016}}</ref> In October 2015, Passlack captained Germany at the [[2015 FIFA U-17 World Cup]] in [[Chile]], appearing in all four of Germany's matches and scoring two goals as Germany were eliminated in the round of 16 in a 2–0 loss to [[Croatia national under-17 football team|Croatia]]. In total, Passlack has scored seven goals in 20 appearances for the Germany U17 team. In March 2016, Passlack was called up to the [[Germany national under-18 football team|Germany U18 team]] for the first time and later that year, received his first call to the [[Germany national under-19 football team|Germany U19 team]].

'''Olutoyosi Tajudeen Oludamilola Olusanya''' (born 14 October 1997), known as '''Toyosi Olusanya''', is an English [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

He started his professional career at [[AFC Wimbledon]] and scored on his debut. After a loan spell at [[Kingstonian F.C.|Kingstonian]] in late 2016, Olusanya trialled with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] and [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] before joining [[Walton Casuals F.C.|Walton Casuals]]. He joined [[Fleet Town F.C.|Fleet Town]] in February 2018 before a move to [[Gosport Borough F.C.|Gosport Borough]] a month later.

==Club career==

=== Youth ===
Olusanya started his youth career with Mass between the ages of 11 and 14, before a year-long spell at Palace Guard. He later joined 10 Coaching as part of a college scheme, and was spotted by AFC Wimbledon while looking at a teammate.<ref name=":0">{{Citation|last=AFC Wimbledon TV|title=Rapid rise earns AFC Wimbledon pro deal for Toyosi|date=2016-02-06|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YHCY76AKgUo|accessdate=2016-05-10}}</ref>

=== AFC Wimbledon ===
In 2015, Olusanya joined [[AFC Wimbledon]].<ref name=":0" /> He was a key member of the club's [[2015–16 FA Youth Cup]] run that saw them reach the fifth Round.

Having featured in a 4–0 victory over [[Woking F.C.|Woking]] in the first round, he netted both goals in the club's 2–0 victory over [[Ebbsfleet United F.C.|Ebbsfleet United]] in the second round. Olusanya also played against [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], [[Newcastle United F.C. Reserves and Academy|Newcastle United]] and Chelsea in the ensuing rounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/article/toyosi-nets-debut-winner-3100407.aspx|title=Toyosi nets debut winner|last=Slavin|first=Chris|website=www.afcwimbledon.co.uk|accessdate=2016-05-10}}</ref> He was rewarded with a professional deal in February 2016.<ref name=":0" />

On 7 May 2016, he made his [[The Football League|Football League]] debut as a 73rd minute substitute against [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]]. Olusanya scored his first goal for the club seven minutes later, being bought down in the box before converting the penalty. With the game ending 1-0, Olusanya managed to secure the win for the Dons <ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36176364|title=AFC Wimbledon 1-0 Newport County|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=2016-05-10}}</ref>

==== Kingstonian (loan) ====
In November 2016, he joined [[Isthmian League]] Premier Division club [[Kingstonian F.C.|Kingstonian]] on a one-month loan.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.kingstonian.com/teams/72292/player/toyosi-olusanya-1793464/39138|title=Toyosi Olusanya - First Team - Kingstonian FC|website=www.kingstonian.com|language=en|access-date=2017-12-02}}</ref> He made his debut in a 1–1 [[FA Trophy]] draw with [[Tonbridge Angels F.C.|Tonbridge Angels]] on 12 November, and marked his league debut a week later.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kingstonian.com/teams/72292/match-centre/2-38861|title=Kingstonian 1 vs. 1 Tonbridge Angels - 12 November 2016 - First Team - Kingstonian FC|website=www.kingstonian.com|language=en|access-date=2017-12-02}}</ref> He made seven appearances for the club, the majority coming from the bench, before his return to AFC Wimbledon in December.<ref name=":1" />

==== Trials ====
In April 2017, Olusanya joined [[Premier League]] side [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on trial, having impressed in their previous [[FA Youth Cup]] meeting. Reports suggested [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] also took an interest in the forward after his cup performances.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/chelsea-been-granted-permission-take-10292369|title=Chelsea given permission to take AFC Wimbledon winger Toyosi Olusanya on trial|last=Cross|first=John|date=2017-04-25|work=mirror|access-date=2017-12-02}}</ref>

In July 2017, Olusanya was listed as a member of the [[Reading F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Reading Under-23]] squad.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.readingfc.co.uk/teams/u23-team/forward/toyosi-olusanya/|title=Toyosi Olusanya - Forward - Under-23s - Reading FC|website=www.readingfc.co.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=2017-12-02}}</ref> A month later he joined [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on trial.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=894884150448095232|user=AndrewDHipkins|title=Former @AFCWimbledon Winger/Forward Toyosi Olusanya who's been on trial with Wolves U23s for a few weeks is again i…<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=2017-12-02|language=en|date=8 August 2017}}</ref> In October 2017, he joined [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] on trial.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=917734591489806337|user=JonPalmerSport|title=Trialist Toyosi Olusanya leaves the field at half-time #ctfc<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=2017-12-02|language=en|date=10 October 2017}}</ref>

=== Walton Casuals ===
On 2 December 2017, he joined [[Isthmian League]] South Division club [[Walton Casuals F.C.|Walton Casuals]] with the club out of striking options due to injuries.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://waltoncasuals.com/transfers/stags-sign-toyosi-olusanya/|title=Stags sign Toyosi Olusanya - Walton Casuals FC|date=2017-12-02|work=Walton Casuals FC|access-date=2017-12-02|language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his debut in the same day in a league fixture at [[South Park F.C.|South Park]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://waltoncasuals.com/match/021217/|title=South Park vs Walton Casuals - Walton Casuals FC|work=Walton Casuals FC|access-date=2017-12-02|language=en-GB}}</ref> On 5 December, he scored his first goal for the club in a 3–0 victory against [[Sittingbourne F.C.|Sittingbourne]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://waltoncasuals.com/event/051217/|title=Walton Casuals 3-0 Sittingbourne - Walton Casuals FC|work=Walton Casuals FC|access-date=2018-03-24|language=en-GB}}</ref> He made a further five appearances for the club before falling out of favour.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://waltoncasuals.com/player/toyosi-olusanya|title=Toyosi Olusanya - Walton Casuals FC|work=Walton Casuals FC|access-date=2018-03-24|language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Fleet Town ===

In February 2018, Olusanya joined [[Southern Football League|Southern League]] Division One East club [[Fleet Town F.C.|Fleet Town]]. On 3 February, he made his debut in a 3–2 defeat at [[Uxbridge F.C.|Uxbridge]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://fleettownfc.co.uk/uxbridge-3-fleet-town-2/|title=Uxbridge 3 Fleet Town 2 - Fleet Town FC|date=2018-02-03|work=Fleet Town FC|access-date=2018-03-24|language=en-US}}</ref> Olusanya scored his first goal for the club in an 8–1 North Hants Cup win against [[Tadley Calleva F.C.|Tadley Calleva Reserves]] on 20 February.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://fleettownfc.co.uk/fleet-town-progress-north-hants-cup/|title=Fleet Town Progress in North Hants Cup - Fleet Town FC|date=2018-02-21|work=Fleet Town FC|access-date=2018-03-24|language=en-US}}</ref> Two weeks later, he scored his first league goal in defeat to [[Ashford Town (Middlesex) F.C.|Ashford Town]] and was named Man of the Match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://fleettownfc.co.uk/fleet-town-1-ashford-town-mx-2/|title=Fleet Town 1 Ashford Town (Mx) 2 - Fleet Town FC|date=2018-03-10|work=Fleet Town FC|access-date=2018-03-24|language=en-US}}</ref> Olusanya also scored on his final appearance for the club in a 4–2 victory against Thame United on 17 March.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://fleettownfc.co.uk/fleet-town-4-thame-united-2/|title=Fleet Town 4 Thame United 2 - Fleet Town FC|date=2018-03-17|work=Fleet Town FC|access-date=2018-03-24|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Gosport Borough ===

On 23 March 2018, Olusanya joined [[Southern Football League|Southern League]] Premier Division club [[Gosport Borough F.C.|Gosport Borough]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gosportboroughfc.co.uk/news/the-boro-sign-toyosi-olusanya-2228988.html|title=The Boro' sign Toyosi Olusanya - News - Gosport Borough Football Club|website=www.gosportboroughfc.co.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-03-24}}</ref> He made his début for Gosport as a second-half substitute in a 5–1 defeat at [[Hereford F.C.|Hereford]] the following day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/GosportBFC/status/977581672253272065|title=Gosport Borough FC on Twitter: "Gosport sub: Wright off, Olusanya on. (63 mins)"<!-- Bot generated title -->}}</ref>

=== Billericay Town FC ===
Prior to joining Middlesbrough for an undisclosed fee, Olusanya had an amazing pre season with National league side Billericay Town, where he managed to score 8 goals in 3 games. He scored a hat-trick in a 4-1 win against Canvey Island, followed by a second hat-trick in a 5-0 win against Needham Market.
 
=== Middlesbrough ===
Olusanya joined [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] in August 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boro Sign Toyosi Olusanya {{!}} Middlesbrough FC|url=https://www.mfc.co.uk/news/boro-sign-toyosi-olusanya|access-date=2021-08-30|website=www.mfc.co.uk|language=en}}</ref> On 25 August 2021, he made his debut in the 1–1 draw against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] at the [[Riverside Stadium]], coming on from the bench after 67 minutes. He featured regularly for the Under 23s before being out of action for four months due to a broken metatarsal.<ref>{{Cite web|title=28/08/2021 15:00 v Blackburn Rovers {{!}} Official Website of the Boro- Middlesbrough FC latest news, photos and videos|url=https://www.mfc.co.uk/fixture/18b50841-c06a-4ee8-a7e4-a9e8b72755fa|access-date=2021-08-30|website=www.mfc.co.uk|language=en}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 17 June 2022, Olusanya joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4465-toyosi-olusanya-joins-st-mirren|title=Toyosi Olusanya joins St Mirren|website=St Mirren|date=17 June 2022|accessdate=17 June 2022}}</ref>

On 25 January 2023, he joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on loan until the end of the season. On 1 March 2024, it was confirmed that Olusanya had signed a one-year extension on his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5339-toyosi-olusanya-agrees-one-year-contract-extension#:~:text=St%20Mirren%20Football%20Club%20is,at%20Saints%20until%20summer%202025.|title=TOYOSI OLUSANYA AGREES ONE-YEAR CONTRACT EXTENSION|website=St Mirren|date=1 March 2024|accessdate=8 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cp3015yyk06o|title=Olusanya signs new St Mirren deal|website=BBC|date=1 March 2024|accessdate=8 October 2024}}</ref>

===Houston Dynamo===
[[File:Austin vs Houston Dynamo (2025 US Open Cup) 06.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Olusanya in 2025.]]

On 23 April 2025, Olusanya signed for [[Major League Soccer]] side [[Houston Dynamo FC|Houston Dynamo]] for an undisclosed six-figure fee, signing a contract until June 2026 with the option to extend for a further two years.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.houstondynamofc.com/news/houston-dynamo-fc-sign-forward-toyosi-olusanya-from-st-mirren-fc|title=Houston Dynamo FC sign forward Toyosi Olusanya from St. Mirren FC|website=www.houstondynamofc.com|date=23 April 2025|accessdate=23 April 2025}}</ref><ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/5826-toyosi-olusanya-joins-houston-dynamo-in-permanent-move|title=Toyosi Olusanya joins Houston Dynamo in permanent move|website=www.stmirren.com|date=23 April 2025|accessdate=23 April 2025}}</ref>

==== Loans to Doncaster Rovers and Aberdeen ====
On 30 August 2025, Olusanya joined League One club [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] on loan until 6 January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 August 2025 |title=Doncaster sign forward Toyosi Olusanya on loan until January |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cly700x3qq5o |access-date=30 August 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Olusanya was again sent out on loan on 23 January 2026, returning to the Scottish Premiership to join [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 January 2026 |title=Aberdeen FC - Striker Secures Loan Deal with the Dons |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2026/01/23/striker-secures-loan-deal-with-the-dons/ |access-date=23 January 2026 |website=Aberdeen F.C. |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in England, Olusanya is of Nigerian descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.allnigeriasoccer.com/read_news.php?nid=54988|title=Rangers eye move for 27yo Nigerian forward as potential replacement for Cyriel Dessers | All Nigeria Soccer|website=www.allnigeriasoccer.com}}</ref>
