'''Jamie Terence McGrath''' (born 30 September 1996) is an Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], and the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland national team]]. He started his career with [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]] and has since played for [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]], [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
A native of [[Athboy]], [[County Meath]], McGrath played youth football for his local club Athboy Celtic before joining top [[Dublin]] youth side [[Cherry Orchard F.C.|Cherry Orchard]]. He played for [[University College Dublin A.F.C.|UCD]] under 19's before joining [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]] under 19 side on their scholarship scheme with [[Maynooth University|NUI Maynooth]]. He played for Pats under 19's for two seasons, including a league winning campaign in which McGrath scored two goals against [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]] under 19's in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=6722|title=Club News : St Patrick's Athletic Win Sse Airtricity U19 League|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|date=25 April 2015|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Duffy|first=Arthur|url=http://www.derryjournal.com/sport/football/derry-city/heartbreak-as-derry-city-lose-out-in-dramatic-u19-elite-league-final-1-6710193|title=Heartbreak as Derry City lose out in dramatic U19 Elite League Final|publisher=Derry Journal|date=25 April 2015|access-date=14 November 2016|archive-date=14 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114233102/http://www.derryjournal.com/sport/football/derry-city/heartbreak-as-derry-city-lose-out-in-dramatic-u19-elite-league-final-1-6710193|url-status=dead}}</ref> He progressed into the first team in 2014 whilst still playing for the club's under 19 side.

===St Patrick's Athletic===
====2014 season====
McGrath made his senior debut with the first team on 9 September 2014 as he played the full 90 minutes in a 2–1 win over [[Longford Town F.C.|Longford Town]] in the [[2014 Leinster Senior Cup Final]] at [[Strokestown Road|City Calling Stadium]]. McGrath impressed Saints fans with his display, including an excellent through ball to set up Jack Bayly's winning goal in the 64th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ie/news/3942/ireland/2014/09/09/5094211/longford-town-1-2-st-patricks-athletic-saints-lift-leinster?CMPID=TWIRE_140909_LONSTP|title=Longford Town 1-2 St Patrick's Athletic: Saints lift Leinster Senior Cup|publisher=Goal.com|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stpatsfc.com/report.php?report=661|title=Longford Town (1) – St Patrick's Athletic (2)|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> His [[League of Ireland]] debut came on 17 October 2014 when he started against [[Athlone Town F.C.|Athlone Town]] in a 2–0 loss at [[Richmond Park (football ground)|Richmond Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://extratime.ie/fixtures/detail/20424/2/|title=Report – League of Ireland Premier Division – St. Patrick's Athletic -v- Athlone Town|publisher=Extratime.ie|date=18 March 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref>

====2015 season====
He was named as a first team player ahead of the [[2015 St Patrick's Athletic F.C. season|2015 season]], with number 19 being assigned to McGrath as his squad number.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=6600|title=Club News : 2015 Squad No's Announced|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|date=15 January 2015|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> Mid season when first choice striker [[Christy Fagan]] picked up a knee injury, McGrath had an extended run in the starting 11 as a striker and scored his first goals away to [[Drogheda United F.C.|Drogheda United]] and [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] in consecutive away games to secure 2–0 and 3–0 wins respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=6843|title=Club News : Saints Win And Extend Winning Streak To 5|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|date=17 July 2015|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stpatsfc.com/report.php?report=688|title=Sligo Rovers (0) – St Patrick's Athletic (3)|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|date=24 July 2015|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> McGrath made his first appearances in [[UEFA]] competition when he came on from the bench both away and at home against [[Latvia]]n side [[Skonto FC|Skonto Riga]] in the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=6819|title=Club News : Result: Skonto 2 – Saints 1|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|date=2 July 2015|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://extratime.ie/fixtures/detail/27919/2/|title=Report – Europa League – St. Patrick's Athletic -v- Skonto Riga|publisher=Extratime.ie|date=18 March 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> McGrath came on at the start of extra time in the [[2015 League of Ireland Cup Final]] as Pats drew 0–0 with [[Galway United F.C.|Galway United]] before winning 4–3 on penalties to win the League Cup at [[Eamonn Deacy Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://extratime.ie/fixtures/detail/27944/2/|title=Report – EA Sports Cup – Galway United FC -v- St. Patrick's Athletic|publisher=Extratime.ie|date=18 March 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> McGrath received rave reviews from fans, pundits and the media alike for his breakthrough season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sseairtricityleague.ie/news/6119-rising-stars-jamie-mcgrath|title=Rising Stars – Jamie McGrath|publisher=Sseairtricityleague.ie|date=3 June 2015|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> coming in a second behind [[Lee Desmond]] in the club's Young Player of the Year awards.

====2016 season====
Although he struggled with shin splints that kept him out of games at the beginning of the [[2016 St Patrick's Athletic F.C. season|2016 season]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Season|first=The|url=http://seasonticketsite.com/2016/05/05/rising-star-jamie-mcgrath/|title=Rising Star: Jamie McGrath – THE SEASON TICKET|publisher=Seasonticketsite.com|access-date=14 November 2016|archive-date=14 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114083931/http://seasonticketsite.com/2016/05/05/rising-star-jamie-mcgrath/|url-status=dead}}</ref> his importance to the team increased in a season where the team struggled to deal with the midfield losses of [[Christopher Forrester|Chris Forrester]], [[Greg Bolger]], [[Killian Brennan]] and [[James Chambers (Irish footballer)|James Chambers]]. Those losses however, created an opportunity for McGrath to play a lot of games in the role of attacking midfielder throughout the season. His first goal of the season was an 89th-minute strike to rescue a point at home to relegation fighting [[Longford Town F.C.|Longford Town]] live on [[Eir Sport]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://extratime.ie/matches/detail/28454/2/|title=Report – League of Ireland Premier Division – St. Patrick's Athletic -v- Longford Town|publisher=Extratime.ie|date=18 March 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> His only appearance in Europe for the season came against [[FC Dinamo Minsk|Dinamo Minsk]] of Belarus as Pats lost 1–0 at home and were knocked out of the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] in the second qualifying round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2020111--st-patrick-s-vs-dinamo-minsk/|title=UEFA Europa League 2017 – St Patrick's-Dinamo Minsk –|publisher=[[UEFA]]|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> McGrath played a huge part in the Saints retaining their League Cup trophy as he played in every game, scoring away from home against [[Bray Wanderers F.C.|Bray Wanderers]] in the quarter-finals,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://extratime.ie/matches/detail/29208/2/|title=Report – EA Sports Cup – Bray Wanderers -v- St. Patrick's Athletic|publisher=Extratime.ie|date=18 March 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]] in the semi's<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/jamiemcgrath-the-mastermind-asst-patricks-athletic-reachea-sports-cup-final-414856.html|title=Jamie McGrath the mastermind as St Patrick's Athletic reach EA Sports Cup final|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=9 August 2016|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://extratime.ie/matches/detail/29298/2/|title=Report – EA Sports Cup – Shamrock Rovers -v- St. Patrick's Athletic|publisher=Extratime.ie|date=18 March 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> and [[Limerick F.C.|Limerick]] in the Final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fai.ie/domestic/news/st-pats-retain-ea-sports-cup-after-thrilling-final|title=St Pat's retain EA SPORTS Cup after thrilling final | Football Association of Ireland|publisher=Fai.ie|date=18 September 2016|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://extratime.ie/matches/detail/29421/2/|title=Report – EA Sports Cup – Limerick FC -v- St. Patrick's Athletic|publisher=Extratime.ie|date=18 March 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> Following a good season for McGrath, he was voted [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]] Young Player of the Season by the club's supporters.<ref name="auto1">{{cite web|url=http://stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=7388|title=Club News: 2016 Awards Night Winners|publisher=stpatsfc.com|date=19 November 2016|access-date=20 November 2016}}</ref>

===Dundalk===
McGrath moved from [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]] to [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] for an undisclosed transfer fee on 15 January 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dundalkfc.com/duo-join-champions/|title=Duo Join The Champions|publisher=dundalkfc.com|date=15 January 2017|access-date=15 January 2017}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
After winning back-to-back [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] titles with Dundalk, McGrath signed a {{frac|2|1|2}}-year deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 7 January 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=St Mirren sign Irish pair Conor McCarthy and Jamie McGrath |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51021616 |access-date=7 January 2020 |work=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2020}}</ref> He was named as the club's Player of the Year for the [[2020–21 St Mirren F.C. season|2020–21 season]] by the club's supporters after scoring and impressive 17 goals in 45 appearances in all competitions from midfield.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3987-st-mirren-player-of-the-year-awards-2020-21|title=St Mirren Player of the Year Awards 2020/21|website=www.stmirren.com}}</ref>

===Wigan Athletic===
On 31 January 2022, transfer deadline day, McGrath signed for [[EFL League One]] club [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2022/january/31/new-signing-latics-complete-signing-of-jamie-mcgrath-from-st-mirren/|title=New Signing - Latics complete signing of Jamie McGrath from St Mirren|publisher=Wigan Athletic FC|date=31 January 2022 }}</ref> After making four appearances for the club, he spent the 2022–23 season on loan at [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], before on 26 July 2023, making the decision to terminate his contract due to repeated contractual breaches by the previous owners of Wigan, despite the club's efforts to retain him.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2023/july/26/club-statement-jack-whatmough-and-jamie-mcgrath/|title=Jack Whatmough and Jamie McGrath leave Wigan Athletic|date=26 July 2023|publisher=Wigan Athletic FC}}</ref>

====Dundee United loan====
On 3 August 2022, he joined Dundee United on loan until the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jamie McGrath Joins Dundee United On Loan |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7417/JAMIE-MCGRATH-JOINS-DUNDEE-UNITED-ON-LOAN.html |publisher=Dundee United Football Club |access-date=3 August 2022}}</ref> He made his debut the following day, providing the assist for [[Glenn Middleton]]'s goal in a 1–0 win over [[AZ Alkmaar]] in the [[UEFA Europa Conference League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/glenn-middleton-strike-earns-dundee-united-a-stirring-victory-against-az-alkmaar-1659647567000|title=Glenn Middleton strike earns Dundee United a stirring victory against AZ Alkmaar|author1=PA Staff|date=4 August 2022|website=fourfourtwo.com}}</ref> McGrath made 32 appearances in all competitions over the course of the season, scoring 7 goals, but this was not enough to help his side avoid relegation to the [[Scottish Championship]] as they finished bottom of the table.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65685480|title=Where did it go wrong for Dundee Utd?|date=28 May 2023|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
After leaving Wigan, McGrath returned to the [[Scottish Premiership]] by signing a two-year contract with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 22 August 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/aberdeen-delight-at-capture-of-irish-player-jamie-mcgrath-he-has-the-right-mentality-to-fit-into-our-squad/a1182207793.html|title=Aberdeen delight at capture of Irish player Jamie McGrath – He has the right mentality to fit into our squad|date=22 August 2023|website=Independent.ie}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66586989 |title=Jamie McGrath: Ex-St Mirren & Dundee Utd midfielder joins Aberdeen after Wigan contract termination |website=BBC Sport |date=22 August 2023 |accessdate=22 August 2023}}</ref> He made his debut two days later, coming off the bench in the 70th minute away to [[BK Häcken]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]], helping his side to comeback from two goals down to earn a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66573722|title=Aberdeen recover from two down to draw with Hacken|work=BBC Sport |date=23 August 2023 }}</ref> On 30 September 2023, McGrath scored in a 3–1 win over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at [[Ibrox Stadium]] on his 27th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/jamie-mcgrath-scores-vital-goal-31073472|title=Jamie McGrath scores vital goal on birthday as Aberdeen beat Rangers|first=Darragh|last=Culhane|date=30 September 2023|website=Irish Mirror}}</ref> On 9 November 2023, he scored his first career European goal when he found the bottom corner with a 30-yard free kick away to [[P.A.O.K.|PAOK]] to level the scores at 2–2 in his sides [[UEFA Europa Conference League]] draw at the [[Toumba Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67290895|title=Aberdeen eliminated from Europe after PAOK thriller|work=BBC Sport |date=8 November 2023 }}</ref> In January 2025, he sustained a shoulder injury that required surgery, with the intensive rehabilitation period keeping him out of action for several months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2025/01/24/injury-update-jamie-mcgrath/|title=Aberdeen FC - Injury update | Jamie McGrath|website=Aberdeen FC}}</ref> McGrath signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in February 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/czdnl4rr2n9o  |title=Hibernian transfers: Midfielder Jamie McGrath to join when Aberdeen deal expires |website=BBC Sport |date=25 February 2025 |accessdate=25 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2025/0225/1498782-mcgrath-signs-pre-contract-agreement-with-hibernian/|title=McGrath signs pre-contract agreement with Hibernian|date=25 February 2025|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
McGrath joined [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in June 2025, having agreed a four-year contract with the club earlier that year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cx230wy0x9yo |title='Club's on an upward trajectory' - Jamie McGrath on joining Hibs |website=BBC Sport |date=25 June 2025 |accessdate=26 June 2025}}</ref>
On 24 July 2025, he scored within seven minutes of his debut against Danish side [[FC Midtjylland]] in the first leg of the second round of the [[2025–26 UEFA Europa League qualifying]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25339968.midtjylland-1-hibs-1-mcgrath-scores-debut-first-leg-draw/ |title='Midtjylland 1 Hibs 1: McGrath scores on debut in first-leg draw |website=The herald |date=24 July 2025 |accessdate=25 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/jamie-mcgrath-scores-on-hibs-debut-in-europa-league-with-troy-parrott-also-on-mark-for-alkmaar-in-conference-league/a483156664.html|title=Jamie McGrath scores on Hibs debut in Europa League with Troy Parrott also on mark for Alkmaar in Conference League|date=24 July 2025|website=www.independent.ie}}</ref> McGrath scored 9 goals in 41 appearances in all competitions in an impressive debut season with Hibs that saw him voted the club's Men's Player of the Year and Player's Player of the Year awards.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |date=2026-05-17 |title=Jamie McGrath has been named Hibernian FC Player of the Year in his debut season for the 2025/26 campaign! |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2026/may/17/2025-26-end-of-season-award-winners-/ |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=www.hibernianfc.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==
McGrath's first taste of under-19's international football came when he was called up to the [[Republic of Ireland national under-19 football team|Republic of Ireland under-19s]] by [[Paul Doolin]] for their November 2014 games against [[Malta national under-19 football team|Malta]] and Gibraltar. His first appearance came against Malta in a 1–0 win in [[Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=6554|title=Club News : Mcgrath Gets Irish U19 Cap|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|date=13 November 2014|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> He went on to make a total of six appearances for the 19's, scoring twice vs [[Azerbaijan national under-19 football team|Azerbaijan]] at [[Tallaght Stadium]]. McGrath was called up to the [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland under-21]] squad for the first time by manager [[Noel King (footballer)|Noel King]] on 8 November 2016, for their games against [[Czech Republic national under-21 football team|Czech Republic]] and [[Slovakia national under-21 football team|Slovakia]] in [[La Manga Club]], Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=7381|title=Club News : Mcgrath Named In Ireland U21 Squad|publisher=Stpatsfc.com|date=8 November 2016|access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref>

On 24 May 2021, McGrath received his first call up to the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] senior squad by his former [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] manager [[Stephen Kenny (football manager)|Stephen Kenny]] for the summer friendlies against [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] and [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/ireland/news/kenny-names-27-man-squad-for-andorra-hungary|title=Kenny names 27-man squad for Andorra & Hungary | Football Association of Ireland|website=www.fai.ie}}</ref> making his full international debut in the away fixture in [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] on 3 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/ireland-andorra-2-5457011-Jun2021/|title= Troy Parrott brace rescues Ireland from humiliating defeat to Andorra|date=3 June 2021|work=The 42|accessdate= 4 June 2021}}</ref> His first senior start for Ireland came in a 2–1 loss in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group A|2022 World Cup qualifier]] against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] on 1 September 2021 at the [[Estádio Algarve]] in [[Faro, Portugal|Faro]], in which he provided the assist for [[John Egan (footballer, born 1992)|John Egan]]'s opening goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/sep/01/portugal-republic-ireland-world-cup-2022-qualifier-match-report/|title=Record-breaker Cristiano Ronaldo's late goals for Portugal break Ireland's hearts|last=Doyle|first=Paul|date=1 September 2021|work=The Guardian|access-date=1 September 2021}}</ref>

After 18 months out of the squad, McGrath was recalled in May 2026 for end-of-season friendlies against [[Qatar national football team|Qatar]] and [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2026/0529/1575865-mcgrath-happy-to-cut-holiday-short-for-ireland-call-up/ |title=McGrath happy to cut holiday short for Ireland call-up |website=RTE Sport |date=29 May 2026 |accessdate=29 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Connor Patrick Ronan''' (born 6 March 1998) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premier League]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]. Born in [[Rochdale]], England, he plays for the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland national team]].

==Club career==
Ronan started his career with Copperpot JFC<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rochdaleonline.co.uk/sites/copperpot-jfc/under-11s-win-bowlee-tournament|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111124091722/http://rochdaleonline.co.uk/sites/copperpot-jfc/under-11s-win-bowlee-tournament|url-status=usurped|archive-date=24 November 2011|title=Copperpot JFC|work=Rochdale Online}}</ref> and attended [[St Cuthbert's RC High School]] in Rochdale with whom he reached the final of the English National Schools Cup as a Year 7 in 2009 with a team that also included [[Axel Tuanzebe]], Kisimba Kisimba and [[Johny Diba]], who all went on to become professional.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manchester-united-youngster-axel-tuanzebe-10396435|title=Manchester United youngster Axel Tuanzebe 'born for greatness'|first=Samuel|last=Luckhurst|date=11 November 2015|work=Manchester Evening News}}</ref> He then joined [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]], his boyhood club in which he stayed until he joined [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] at the age of 16.<ref>{{cite news|title=Five Things We Have Learned About Connor Ronan|url=http://www.wolves.co.uk/news/article/five-things-we-have-learned-about-connor-ronan-2279740.aspx|publisher=Wolverhampton Wanderers FC|date=2 February 2015|accessdate=17 December 2016}}</ref> Ronan made three appearances for the team's [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. Development Squad and Academy|development squad]] in the [[2016–17 EFL Trophy]], scoring a goal in their 4–0 win over [[EFL League Two]] team [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Youngsters Make Progress In Cup|url=http://www.wolves.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/report-youngsters-make-progress-in-cup-3406677.aspx|date=8 November 2016|publisher=Wolverhampton Wanderers FC|accessdate=17 December 2016}}</ref> With [[Paul Lambert]] as manager, Ronan was part of the first-team squad for the first time on 26 November 2016,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/wolverhampton-wanderers-fc/2016/11/26/wolves-vs-sheffield-wednesday-live/|title=Wolves 0 Sheffield Wednesday 2 - As it happened|date=26 November 2016|accessdate=17 December 2016|work=Express & Star|publisher=MNA Media}}</ref> as an unused substitute in the 2–0 defeat to [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]]. Ronan made his debut on 17 December 2016, replacing [[Hélder Costa (footballer)|Hélder Costa]] for the final nine minutes of the team's 2–0 win over [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38271717|title=Nottingham Forest 0-2 Wolverhampton Wanderers|date=17 December 2016|accessdate=17 December 2016|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/wolverhampton-wanderers-fc/2016/12/17/nottingham-forest-0-wolves-2-report/soccer-sky-bet-championship-nottingham-forest-v-wolverhampton-wanderers-41/|title=Nottingham Forest 0 Wolves 2 - Report and pictures|date=17 December 2016|accessdate=17 December 2016|work=Express & Star|publisher=MNA Media|quote=Lambert did too. He sent on youngster Connor Ronan for his professional debut in place of Costa}}</ref>

On 31 August 2018, Ronan joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]] on loan until January 2019 along with team-mate Connor Johnson.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45375788 |title=Connor Johnson and Connor Ronan: Wolves duo join Walsall on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2018 |accessdate=1 September 2018 }}</ref>
Ronan returned to Wolves at the conclusion of his loan spell, making 15 appearances in all competitions for Walsall.<ref name="CR18"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.saddlers.co.uk/news/2019/january/ronan-returns-to-wolves|title=Ronan Returns to Wolves|publisher=Walsall FC|date=2 January 2019}}</ref>

He signed for League One club [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] on a six-month loan deal on 17 January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51150133 |title=Connor Ronan: Blackpool sign Wolves midfielder on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 January 2020 |accessdate=17 January 2020 }}</ref> His playing time was however restricted to ten games after the League One clubs voted to curtail the season owing to the COVID-19 outbreak.

In August 2020, he signed a new contract – lasting until 2024 – with Wolves before again being sent out on loan, this time joining Swiss side [[Grasshopper Club Zürich|Grasshoppers]] for the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wolves.co.uk/news/under-23/20200916-ronan-agrees-new-contract/|title=Ronan agrees new contract|publisher=Wolverhampton Wanderers FC|date=16 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=GC Holt Dadashov und Ronan |url=https://www.gcz.ch/news/news/artikel/gc-holt-dadashov-und-ronan/ |publisher=Grasshopper Club Zurich |date=23 August 2020|language=de}}</ref> His would make his first appearance coming on as a substitute in the second half, in a 3–0 victory against [[FC Wil]]. Ronan's first goal for the Swiss club came in a 3–0 home win against [[Neuchâtel Xamax FCS|Neuchâtel Xamax]], when he scored the second goal in the 91st minute.

In May 2020, Ronan returned to his parent club for treatment, after breaking his [[metatarsal bone]], ruling him out for up to four to five months.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/football/wolverhampton-wanderers-fc/2021/05/13/connor-ronan-to-return-to-wolves-for-treatment-after-breaking-metatarsal/ |title=Connor Ronan to return to Wolves for treatment after breaking metatarsal |work=Express & Star |date=13 May 2021|publisher=MNA Media |accessdate=15 May 2021 }}</ref>

On 31 August 2021, Ronan sealed a season long loan to [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4089-jim-goodwin-aiming-to-bring-one-more-in-ahead-of-transfer-deadline|title=Jim Goodwin aiming to bring one more in ahead of transfer deadline|publisher=St Mirren FC}}</ref> He made his debut in a 0–0 draw at home to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in September.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58444922|title=St Mirren still winless after stalemate|date=11 September 2021|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made a habit of scoring sensational long range goals throughout his spell at St. Mirren, including a 30-yard strike in the [[2021-22 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] quarter-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/60724676|title='Oh my goodness... that is outstanding' - St Mirren's Ronan scores 30-yard wonder goal|date=13 March 2022|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 23 January 2023, Ronan signed a four-year deal with the [[Colorado Rapids]] in [[Denver]]. It will see him play through to the 2026 [[Major League Soccer]] season, with an additional club option for 2027.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/colorado-rapids-sign-connor-ronan-from-epl-s-wolverhampton-wanderers|title=Colorado Rapids sign Connor Ronan from EPL's Wolverhampton Wanderers|publisher=MLSsoccer|date=23 January 2023|access-date=23 January 2023}}</ref>

On 18 June 2026, Ronan signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Premier League]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/en/news/connor-ronan-joins-aberdeen|title=Connor Ronan Joins Aberdeen - Aberdeen FC|website=www.afc.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==
Ronan has played at under 17, under 19 and under 21 level for the Republic of Ireland. Ronan was selected for the [[2019 Toulon Tournament]] where he played in every match.

He was called up to the senior [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] squad for the [[Exhibition game|friendlies]] against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] and [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]] on 26 and 29 March 2022 respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/ireland/news/kenny-names-25-man-squad-for-belgium-lithuania|title=Kenny names 25-man squad for Belgium & Lithuania|publisher=[[Football Association of Ireland]]|date=18 March 2022|access-date=24 March 2022}}</ref>

'''Afeez Aremu Olalekan'''{{audio|LL-Q34311 (yor)-Abike25-Afeez Aremu Olalekan.wav|listen}}(born 3 October 1999) is a Nigerian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sportstalkafrica.com/npfl-transfer-sunshine-lose-afeez-aremu-to-akwa/|title=NPFL Transfer: Sunshine lose Afeez Aremu to Akwa|website=sportstalkafrica.com|accessdate=4 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportlineng.com/2017/01/18/psftebs86471-2/|title=EXCLUSIVE: I can't wait to put one past Rivers United – Aremu Afeez|date=18 January 2017|website=sportlineng.com|accessdate=4 March 2017}}</ref> He has also played for the [[Nigeria national under-20 football team|Nigeria national under-20 team]].<ref name="Premium">{{Cite news|url=http://www.premiumtimesng.com/sports/156342-12-uninvited-players-progress-flying-eagles-trial.html|title=12 uninvited players progress in Flying Eagles trial|date=7 March 2014|accessdate=4 March 2017|newspaper=[[Premium Times]]}}</ref>

==Career==
Aremu was born in [[Ibadan]], Nigeria. He made his league debut with [[Remo Stars F.C.]]<ref name=Premium/> at the age of 14 in 2013–14 Nigeria National Pro League season during their terrain in the Nigerian Second Division League. He has played for several [[Nigeria Premier League]] teams, such as [[Sharks F.C.]] from where he played against [[Sunshine Stars F.C.]] and this made Sunshine Stars sign him.<ref name="supportthenpfl">{{cite web|url=http://www.supportthenpfl.com/news/aremu-afeez-delighted-sunshine-stars-move/|publisher=supportthenpfl.com|title=www.supportthenpfl.com/news/aremu-afeez-delighted-sunshine-stars-move/|accessdate=4 March 2017}}{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He got stronger interest from [[Rivers United F.C.]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://thenationonlineng.net/afeez-praises-rivers-utds-mentality/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Afeez praises Rivers Utd's mentality|date=6 October 2016|accessdate=4 March 2017|language=en-US|newspaper=[[The Nation (Nigeria)|The Nation]]}}</ref> after he played against them during the first leg of 2015–16 Nigeria Premier League season and was signed during the mid season. He won the man of the match again towards two games to the end of 2015–16 Nigeria Premier League season when Rivers United played against [[Akwa United F.C.]] and this also made Akwa United sign him in the 2017 Nigeria Premier League season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ng/news/4111/npfl/2016/03/06/21037132/sunshine-stars-afeez-aremu-looking-to-arrest-poor-form|title=Sunshine Stars' Afeez Aremu looking to arrest poor form against Ifeanyi Ubah FC|date=6 March 2016|work=Goal.com|accessdate=4 March 2017|language=en-NG}}</ref>

In August 2020, Aremu joined [[2. Bundesliga]] side [[FC St. Pauli]] from [[Eliteserien]] club [[IK Start]] on a three-year contract. The transfer fee paid to IK Start was undisclosed.<ref>{{cite web |title=FC St. Pauli verpflichtet Afeez Aremu |url=https://www.kicker.de/schultz_bekommt_wunschspieler_aremu_unterschreibt_bei_st_pauli-782718/artikel |website=kicker |access-date=24 August 2020 |language=German |date=24 August 2020}}</ref>

Having featured less since the arrival of manager [[Fabian Hürzeler]], Aremu moved to league rivals [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]] in August 2023.<ref name="fck">{{cite web |title=Aremu wechselt nach Kaiserslautern |trans-title=Aremu moves to Kaiserslautern |url=https://www.kicker.de/aremu-wechselt-nach-kaiserslautern-965030/artikel |website=kicker |access-date=24 August 2023 |language=German |date=23 August 2023}}</ref> The transfer was reported as being in the mid-six-figure range.<ref name="fck"/>

On 29 January 2026, Aremu moved to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in Scotland on a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2026/01/29/nigerian-midfielder-completes-move-to-dons/|title=Nigerian Midfielder Completes Move to Dons|date=29 January 2026|access-date=29 January 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Aremu has [[Yoruba tribal marks]] on his face, he had them since he was a baby.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=FC St Pauli|url=https://www.fcstpauli.com/en/news/published/afeez-aremu-speaks-to-the-media-ahead-of-hannover-away/|title=AREMU: "I THOUGHT, WOW, THIS IS GREAT!|date=8 September 2021|access-date=24 August 2023}}</ref>

'''Panutche Amadu Pereira Camará''' (born 28 February 1997) is a Bissau-Guinean professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] and [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for Scottish club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and the [[Guinea-Bissau national football team|Guinea-Bissau national team]].<ref name="SW">{{soccerway|panutche-camara/476242|accessdate=11 June 2017}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
After playing youth football for [[GS Loures|Loures]] and [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lopes |first=Gervásio |date=8 August 2020 |title=Inglaterra: Panutche Camará é reforço de Plymouth Argyle FC |url=http://www.soudjurtu.com/2020/08/inglaterra-panutche-camara-e-reforco-do.html |access-date=30 December 2021 |website=Sou Djurtu |language=pt}}</ref> Camará joined the under-23 setup at [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] before signing for [[Dulwich Hamlet F.C.|Dulwich Hamlet]] in 2017. He made 15 appearances for Hamlet, scoring four goals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dulwich Hamlet youngster Camara snapped up by Crawley Town |url=https://www.pitchero.com/clubs/dulwichhamlet/news/dulwich-hamlet-youngster-camara-snapped-up-by-craw-1836824.html |access-date=8 August 2019 |publisher=Dulwich Hamlet F.C. |language=en |via=pitchero.com}}</ref>

===Crawley Town===
Camará signed a two-year professional contract with [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] in June 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 June 2017 |title=Panutche Camara: Crawley Town sign Dulwich Hamlet forward |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40204552 |access-date=11 June 2017 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Crawley on his debut in a 5–1 [[EFL Cup]] defeat at [[Birmingham City]] on 8 August 2017.<ref name="2017-18" /> In 2017–18, he made 34 appearances in all competitions, scoring three goals.<ref name="2017-18" /> In 2018–19, he appeared regularly for the Reds, making 50 appearances in all competitions, also scoring three goals.<ref name="2018-19" /> In May 2019, Crawley extended his contract to the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Reds release two players |url=https://www.crawleytownfc.com/news/2019/may/10.05-contract-news/ |access-date=14 July 2019 |publisher=Crawley Town F.C. |language=en-gb}}</ref> He was offered a new contract by Crawley at the end of the 2019–20 season,<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 June 2020 |title=2020/21 retained list announced |url=https://www.crawleytownfc.com/news/2020/june/released-and-retained-list/ |website=crawleytownfc.com |publisher=Crawley Town F.C.}}</ref> though Camará rejected the offer and chose to leave the club.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Morton |first=Sam |date=7 August 2020 |title=Second Crawley Town player confirms departure with heartfelt message |language=en |work=Mid Sussex Times |url=https://www.midsussextimes.co.uk/sport/football/second-crawley-town-player-confirms-departure-heartfelt-message-2935846 |access-date=7 August 2020}}</ref>

===Plymouth Argyle===
On 7 August 2020, Camará signed for [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] on a free transfer following his release from Crawley.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 August 2020 |title=Pautche Camara: Promoted Plymouth sign former Crawley midfielder |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53698311 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Plymouth in an EFL Cup tie against [[Leyton Orient]] on 15 September 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 September 2020 |title=Leyton Orient 3–2 Plymouth |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54067072 |access-date=15 September 2020 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Plymouth exercised their option to extend Camará's contract at the end of the [[2021–22 Plymouth Argyle F.C. season|2021–22 season]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/retained-list|title=Retained List|website=www.pafc.co.uk|date=3 May 2022|accessdate=4 May 2022}}</ref> Despite this, Camará was made available for transfer with him showing no intent of signing a new improved contract with the club.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/camara-available-transfer|title=Camara Available for Transfer|website=www.pafc.co.uk|date=10 May 2022|accessdate=11 May 2022}}</ref>

===Ipswich Town===
Camará signed for [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] on 1 September 2022 on a two-year deal for a fee reported to be around £500,000.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.eadt.co.uk/sport/ipswich-town/itfc-complete-camara-deal-9248244 | work = [[East Anglian Daily Times]] | access-date = 1 September 2022 | date = 1 September 2022 | title = Camara becomes Town's ninth signing as midfielder joins from Plymouth| first = Andy | last = Warren}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62759467|title=Ipswich sign striker Ahadme and midfielder Camara|work=BBC Sport |date=September 2022 }}</ref> Having initially been sidelined with a groin injury early in the season, Camará made his Ipswich debut as a half-time substitute in a 0–1 [[EFL Trophy]] defeat away against [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]] on 18 October 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/cambridge-united-vs-ipswich-town/471715|title=Cambridge United 1 - 0 Ipswich Town|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=18 October 2022|accessdate=25 May 2023}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in his next appearance, coming off the bench to score in a 3–0 away win against [[Bracknell Town F.C.|Bracknell Town]] in an [[FA Cup]] first round tie on 7 November.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63461427|title=Bracknell Town 0 - 3 Ipswich Town|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=7 November 2022|accessdate=25 May 2023}}</ref> He made his league debut for Ipswich five days later, coming on as a second-half substitute in a 1–1 home draw against [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] at [[Portman Road]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63523619|title=Ipswich Town 1 - 1 Cheltenham Town|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=12 November 2022|accessdate=25 May 2023}}</ref> In December, Camará underwent surgery on the groin injury he had been suffering with during the season, ruling him out of action for a number of months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.twtd.co.uk/ipswich-town-news/43984/camara-facing-months-out-after-further-surgery|title=Camara Facing Months Out After Further Surgery|publisher=TWTD|date=22 December 2022|accessdate=25 May 2023}}</ref> He returned from injury in March, featuring for Ipswich's under-21 team during the remaining months of  the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.twtd.co.uk/ipswich-town-news/44494/camara-returns-as-u21s-host-charlton-u18s-at-cardiff|title=Camara Returns as U21s Host Charlton, U18s at Cardiff|publisher=TWTD|date=3 March 2023|accessdate=25 May 2023}}</ref> In total, he made 4 appearances during an injury hindered first season at Ipswich scoring once. Ipswich achieved promotion to the [[EFL Championship]] during his first season at the club following a second-placed finish in [[EFL League One]].<ref name=sb2223/>

On 18 July 2023, Camará joined [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on a season-long loan for the 2023–24 campaign.<ref>{{cite news |title=DONE DEAL: PANUTCHE CAMARÁ IS AN ADDICK |url=https://www.charltonafc.com/news/done-deal-panutche-camara-addick |access-date=18 July 2023 |publisher=Charlton Athletic F.C. |date=18 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66236011|title=Charlton sign Ipswich midfielder Camara on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2023 }}</ref> Camará was released by Ipswich at the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-03 |title=Retained list confirmed |url=https://www.itfc.co.uk/news/2024/june/03/ipswich-town-retained-list-summer-2024/ |access-date=2024-08-07 |publisher=Ipswich Town F.C. |language=en}}</ref>

===Return to Crawley Town===
On 6 August 2024, it was announced that Camará had rejoined former club [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]], now competing in League One, on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 August 2024 |title=Panutche Camara re-joins the Red Devils |url=https://www.crawleytownfc.com/news/2024/august/06/panutche-camara-re-joins-the-red-devils/ |access-date=2024-08-07 |publisher=Crawley Town F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-07 |title=Panutche Camara rejoins Crawley after Ipswich Town release |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cdjweden78po |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> His first appearance came as a substitute in a 2–1 League One victory over [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] on 10 August.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2024 |title=Crawley 2-1 Blackpool |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/crawley-town-vs-blackpool/report/508795 |access-date=11 August 2024 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
In June 2025 he transferred to Scottish club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], signing a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/8945/GUINEA-BISSAU-INTERNATIONAL-PANUTCHE-CAMAR-SNAPPED-UP-BY-DUNDEE-UNITED.html|title=GUINEA-BISSAU INTERNATIONAL PANUTCHE CAMARÁ SNAPPED UP BY DUNDEE UNITED|website=Dundee United Football Club}}</ref>

==International career==
In June 2021, Camará received his first international call-up from [[Guinea-Bissau national football team|Guinea-Bissau]] for a friendly against [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Errington |first=Chris |date=7 June 2021 |title=Argyle midfielder Panutche Camara poised for Guinea Bissau debut |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/plymouth-argyle-midfielder-panutche-camara-5498217 |website=PlymouthLive}}</ref> but the match was cancelled after a fault with the Cape Verde plane meant they could not get to the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Futebol: Cancelado particular entre Guiné-Bissau e Cabo Verde |url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/cabo-verde/artigos/cancelado-jogo-de-futebol-particular-entre-guine-bissau-e-cabo-verde |website=SAPO Desporto |language=pt}}</ref> He was named in Guinea-Bissau's 24-man squad for the [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 December 2021 |title=Panutche Camara: Plymouth's Guinea-Bissau midfielder has 'brilliant' Afcon opportunity |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59831924 |access-date=30 December 2021 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He debuted with them in a 0–0 [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations]] tie with [[Sudan national football team|Sudan]] on 11 January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cafonline.com/total-africa-cup-of-nations/matches/2021/2243269/match-report|title=CAFOnline.com|first=CAF-Confedération Africaine du|last=Football|website=CAFOnline.com}}</ref>

He scored his first international goal in a friendly match against Equatorial Guinea on 23 March 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/plymouth-argyle-midfielder-panutche-camara-6852532|title=Argyle midfielder Panutche Camara scores first international goal|first=Chris|last=Errington|date=24 March 2022|website=PlymouthLive}}</ref>

'''Mehdi Merghem''' ({{ langx|ar|مهدي مرغم}}; [[Berber languages|Tamazight]]: ⵎⴻⵀⴷⵉ ⵎⴻⵔⴳⵀⴻⵎ; born 19 July 1997) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|right winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. Born in France, he represents Algeria internationally.

==Career==
Merghem made his professional debut for [[LB Châteauroux|Châteauroux]] in a 3–2 [[Ligue 2]] win over [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]] on 27 July 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue2/feuille_match/83199|title=LFP.fr - Ligue de Football Professionnel - Domino's Ligue 2 - Saison 2017/2018 - 1ère journée - Stade Brestois 29 / Châteauroux|website=www.lfp.fr}}</ref>

On 28 August 2025, he signed a two-year contract with [[JS Kabylie]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.competition.dz/chrono/transferts-zinnbauer-annonce-larrivee-de-merghem-a-la-jsk.html|title=Zinnbauer annonce l'arrivée de Merghem à la JS Kabylie|website=Competition |date= 29 August 2025 |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref>

On 3 February 2026, he joined [[SC Bastia|Bastia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mediafootdz.dz/js-kabylie-le-sc-bastia-annonce-la-signature-de-mehdi-merghem/ |title=JS Kabylie : le SC Bastia annonce la signature de Mehdi Merghem |website=mediafootdz.dz |date=3 February 2026 |access-date=3 February 2026}}</ref>

On 12 July 2026, Merghem moved to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in Scotland on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Dundee United F.C.|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9424/Merghem-heads-to-Tannadice-.html|title=Merghem heads to Tannadice|date=12 July 2026|access-date=20 July 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in France, Merghem holds French and Algerian nationalities.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dzballon.com/2019/01/08/un-franco-algerien-de-ligue-2-proche-de-guingamp/|title=Un Franco-Algérien de ligue 2, proche de Guingamp|last=farid|date=8 January 2019|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mehdi MERGHEM |url=https://www.unfp.org/joueur/mehdi-merghem-20472/ |access-date=2024-01-08 |website=unfp.org}}</ref>

'''Raphael Lukas Sallinger''' (born 8 December 1995) is an Austrian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].

==Club career==
He made his [[Austrian Football Bundesliga]] debut for [[Wolfsberger AC]] on 29 April 2017 in a game against [[SV Mattersburg]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2017/04/29/austria/bundesliga/wolfsberger-athletik-club/sportverein-mattersburg/2241144/|title=Game Report by Soccerway|date=29 April 2017}}</ref>

After seven years with [[TSV Hartberg]], Sallinger signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c20n2l5nyeno |title=Hibs sign goalkeeper Sallinger from Austria |website=BBC Sport |date=5 June 2025 |accessdate=5 June 2025}}</ref> He was regarded to have established himself as a regular starter while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-raphael-sallinger-head-for-heights-mountain-climbing-5365003|title=Hibs star reveals head for heights as mountain-climbing No.1 plots route to summit during Easter Road stay|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=18 October 2025|access-date=14 July 2026}}</ref> He kept six [[Shutout|clean sheets]] in his first seventeen league appearances while playing for them.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kicker.at/sallinger-das-war-mit-abstand-das-beste-was-ich-als-profi-je-erlebt-habe-1181586/artikel|title=Sallinger: "Das war mit Abstand das Beste, was ich als Profi je erlebt habe"|trans-title=Sallinger: "That was by far the best thing I have ever experienced as a professional"|language=de|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|date=8 January 2026|access-date=14 July 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Sallinger is an Austria youth international. He played for the [[Austria national under-20 football team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theedinburghreporter.co.uk/2025/06/hibs-new-signing-raphael-sallingers-career-so-far/|title=Hibs new signing Raphael Sallinger’s career so far|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=The Edinburgh Reporter|date=7 June 2025|access-date=14 July 2026}}</ref>
.
==Personal life==
Sallinger has been in a relationship with Austria [[nutritionist]] Darinka Stock.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.90minuten.at/de/red/magazin/interview/sallinger--es-hat-schon-die-eine-oder-andere-frage-aus-graz-gegeben/|title=Sallinger: "Es hat schon die eine oder andere Frage aus Graz gegeben"|trans-title=Sallinger: "There have already been one or two questions from Graz"|language=de|publisher=90minuten.at|date=22 October 2025|access-date=14 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Rocky Bushiri Kisonga''' (born 30 November 1999) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Hibernia}} side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and the [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo national team]].

He has previously played for [[K.V. Oostende]] and [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], spending almost the entirety of his spell at Norwich on loan at other clubs.

Bushiri was born in DR Congo, his family moved to Belgium soon after.<ref name="nutmegmagazine.co.uk"/> He played for Belgian [[Belgium national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Belgium national under-21 football team|under-21]] teams. He switched his international allegiance to [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo]] in March 2023, and made his full international debut for them later that year.

==Club career==
===Oostende===
Bushiri joined the youth academy of [[K.V. Oostende]] in 2012 after impressing in a provincial tournament representing [[Walloon Brabant]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hln.be/de-krant/debutant-bushiri-18-werkt-ook-op-kvo-secretariaat~a6443fa5/|title=Debutant Bushiri (18) werkt ook op KVO-secretariaat|publisher=}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract with Oostende in June 2017, for two years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.standaard.be/cnt/dmf20170603_02910871|title=Herhaalt KV Oostende succesverhaal Dimata? Kustboys halen weer spits bij Standard|last=(belga)|date=3 June 2017 |publisher=}}</ref> He made his professional debut in a 1–0 [[Belgian First Division A]] loss to [[KV Mechelen]] on 9 December 2017, becoming the youngest-ever debutant for Oostende.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kvo.be/nieuws/jupiler-pro-league-speeldag-18-kv-oostende-kv-mechelen-0-1|title=Jupiler Pro League - speeldag 18: KV Oostende - KV Mechelen 0 - 1|website=www.kvo.be}}</ref>

===Norwich City===
On 3 July 2019, it was announced that Bushiri would join [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on a four-year deal, initially linking up with the U23 squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2019/july/rocky-bushiri/|title=Norwich City set to sign Belgium U21 international Rocky Bushiri |website=www.canaries.co.uk}}</ref> On 1 August 2019, Bushiri joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49199868|title=Rocky Bushiri: Blackpool sign Norwich City defender on season-long loan deal|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 August 2019|accessdate=2 August 2019}}</ref> Bushiri scored his first goal for the club in a 1–0 win against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. Development Squad and Academy|Wolverhampton Wanderers U21s]] in an [[EFL Trophy]] tie on 5 November 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/football/blackpool-fc/blackpool-1-0-wolves-u21s-rocky-bushiri-s-stoppage-time-winner-seals-efl-trophy-qualification-1-10087305 |title=Blackpool 1-0 Wolves' U21s: Rocky Bushiri's stoppage-time winner seals EFL Trophy qualification |date=5 November 2019 |website=blackpoolgazette.co.uk |accessdate=6 November 2019}}</ref>

On 30 June 2020, Bushiri went out on loan again, this time joining [[K.V. Mechelen|Mechelen]] on a season-long deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2020/june/rocky-bushiri-moves-to-kv-mechelen-on-season-long-loan/|title=Rocky Bushiri moves to KV Mechelen on season-long loan|publisher=[[Norwich City F.C.]]|date=30 June 2020|accessdate=28 July 2020}}</ref>

On 26 January 2021, Bushiri moved to Belgium side [[K.A.S. Eupen|KAS Eupen]], on a loan deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=January 26, 2021|title=Rocky Bushiri moves to KAS Eupen on loan|url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2021/january/rocky-bushiri-moves-to-kas-eupen-on-loan/|access-date=January 26, 2021|website=www.canaries.co.uk}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
On 10 January 2022, Bushiri joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on loan for the remainder of the season, with an option to buy in the summer.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rocky Bushiri Joins Hibs From Norwich City!|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/rocky-bushiri-joins-from-norwich-city|access-date=2022-01-10|website=Hibernian FC|language=en-US}}</ref> His number of appearances during the loan triggered that option, and he signed a three-year contract with Hibs in June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61740160 |title=Hibernian: Rocky Bushiri signs permanent deal & Momodou Bojang joins on loan |website=BBC Sport |date=9 June 2022 |accessdate=9 June 2022}}</ref>

After he played against [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Morton]], whilst he was supposed to be suspended for receiving two cautions in earlier ties, Morton were awarded a default 3–0 victory which led to Hibernian being knocked out of the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62252834|title=Hibernian out of Scottish League Cup after fielding suspended Rocky Bushiri against Morton|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=21 July 2022|accessdate=21 July 2022}}</ref> He played regularly during the first half of the [[2022–23 Hibernian F.C. season|2022–23 season]], but was then unavailable for more than three months due to an ankle injury.<ref name = ankle/>

Bushiri scored his first goal for the club on 26 November 2024, scoring a 97th-minute equaliser in a 3–3 draw with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cd9nw8q0822t |title=Three stoppage-time goals as Hibs and Aberdeen draw 3-3 |website=BBC Sport |date=27 November 2024 |accessdate=27 November 2024}}</ref> That goal started a club-record run of 17 league games without defeat, with Bushiri featuring regularly as the team finished third in the [[2024–25 Scottish Premiership|Premiership]].<ref name = 2025deal/>

His contract with Hibernian expired at the end of the [[2024–25 Hibernian F.C. season|2024–25 season]], but he signed a new three-year deal with the club in June 2025.<ref name = 2025deal>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvg8pgkg41vo |title='Real leader' Bushiri extends Hibs stay until 2028 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 June 2025 |accessdate=27 June 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Bushiri's grandfather, [[Rachel Albert Kisonga Mazakala|Albert Kisonga]], was an [[List of ambassadors of the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Belgium|ambassador to Belgium]].<ref name = ankle>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/rocky-bushiri-big-interview-derby-injury-hibs-comeback-and-congo-dr-decision-4123900 |title=Rocky Bushiri big interview: Derby injury, Hibs comeback, and Congo DR decision |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=29 April 2023 |accessdate=29 April 2023}}</ref> Bushiri represented Belgium in youth internationals up to and including the [[Belgium national under-21 football team|under-21]] level, but changed his international allegiance in March 2023 so that he could play for [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-defender-rocky-bushiri-makes-national-team-decision-following-belgium-under-21-caps-4056976 |title=Hibs defender Rocky Bushiri makes national team decision following Belgium Under-21 caps |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=9 March 2023 |accessdate=9 March 2023 |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News}}</ref> Bushiri was first selected by DR Congo in June 2023, for two [[2023 Africa Cup of Nations qualification Group I|Africa Cup of Nations qualifying]] matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cqv0552p81vo |title=Bushiri earns Congo call up |website=BBC Sport |date=29 May 2023 |accessdate=29 May 2023}}</ref> He made his full international debut in September 2023, playing in a [[friendly match|friendly]] against [[South Africa national soccer team|South Africa]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cd1zl80x039o |title=Bushiri's Congo DR debut ends in defeat |website=BBC Sport |date=12 September 2023 |accessdate=12 September 2023}}</ref>

Bushiri was selected in the Congolese squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], but was forced to withdraw after suffering an achilles tendon injury during the last match of the [[2025–26 Hibernian F.C. season|2025–26]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cgkp8de42gmo |title=Hibs: Rocky Bushiri to miss World Cup |website=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2026 |accessdate=20 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Jack Henry Stewart Iredale''' (born 2 May 1996) is a professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C|Hibernian]]. Born in Scotland, he represented Australia at youth level. 

==Early life==
Iredale was born in Scotland, before moving to New Zealand at the age of one. He lived in New Zealand, where his mother, [[Fiona Iredale|Fiona]] represented the country in [[judo]] at the [[2000 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carlisle Utd's Jack Iredale: ‘Mental resilience was ingrained in me. Everything else was just noise’ |website=News and Star |date=19 July 2019 |url=https://www.newsandstar.co.uk/sport/17781620.carlisle-utds-jack-iredale-mental-resilience-ingrained-everything-else-just-noise/ |language=en |access-date=3 September 2025 |last=Colman |first=Jon}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/nz-teams/132909172/darren-bazeley-eager-to-meet-dualnational-prospects-around-all-whites-match-in-london |title=Darren Bazeley eager to meet dual-national prospects around All Whites match in London |access-date=3 September 2025 |website=Stuff |last=Voerman |first=Andrew |date=17 September 2023}}</ref> He moved to Australia as a ten-year-old.<ref name="acls">{{cite news |url=https://ericksfootballblog.wordpress.com/2015/08/11/three-strikes-and-not-out-perth-glory-youths-jack-iredales-fight-against-knee-injury/ |author=Lopez, Erick |date=11 August 2015 |accessdate=26 April 2018 |title=Three strikes and not out – Perth Glory Youth's Jack Iredale's fight against knee injury}}</ref> He suffered three [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|anterior cruciate ligament injuries]] playing football between the ages of 15 and 18.<ref name=acls/>

==Career==
===Club===
Iredale signed with [[National Premier Leagues Western Australia]] side [[ECU Joondalup SC|ECU Joondalup]] in May 2017.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ecujoondalup.com.au/news/2017/jacks-sign-perth-glory-defender/|title=Jacks sign Perth Glory defender|accessdate=26 April 2018|publisher=[[ECU Joondalup SC]]|date=17 May 2015|archive-date=26 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180426145122/http://www.ecujoondalup.com.au/news/2017/jacks-sign-perth-glory-defender/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2017, Iredale signed with his hometown club, [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://gmfc.net/2017/07/27/signing-news-jack-iredale-joins-morton/|title=Signing news: Jack Iredale joins Morton|date=27 July 2017|accessdate=26 April 2018|author=Jonathan Mitchell|publisher=[[Greenock Morton F.C.]]|archive-date=26 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180426144537/https://gmfc.net/2017/07/27/signing-news-jack-iredale-joins-morton/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Iredale was nominated for SPFA Goal of the Season for a wonder-strike against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gmfc.net/player/jack-iredale/|title=Jack Iredale|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.|author=Jonathan Mitchell|accessdate=27 July 2018|archive-date=27 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180727145910/https://gmfc.net/player/jack-iredale/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He signed a one-year extension in May 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://gmfc.net/2018/05/01/jack-iredale-signs-one-year-contract-extension/|title=Jack Iredale signs one-year contract extension|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.|author=Jonathan Mitchell|date=1 May 2018|accessdate=1 May 2018|archive-date=2 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502064737/https://gmfc.net/2018/05/01/jack-iredale-signs-one-year-contract-extension/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 7 May 2019, English [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] announced that they had signed Iredale on a one-year contract for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48191977|title=Jack Iredale: Carlisle United sign Greenock Morton left-back|date=7 May 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 14 August 2020, Iredale signed for [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53785516 |title=Jack Iredale: Cambridge United sign former Carlisle United left-back |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 August 2020 |accessdate=14 August 2020}}</ref> On 4 May 2022, it was announced Iredale would be leaving the club after turning down a new contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cambridge-united.co.uk/news/2022/may/jack-iredale-leaves-cambridge-united-contract-sky-bet-league-one-efl-english-football-league-wednesday-4th-may-2022/ |title= Iredale set to leave U's|publisher=Cambridge United F.C. |date=4 May 2022 |accessdate=4 May 2022}}</ref>

On 9 May 2022, Iredale signed a three-year contract with [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], marking their first signing of the transfer window.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/bolton-iredale-transfer-confirmed-breaking-23906184|title=Bolton Wanderers confirm Jack Iredale Cambridge United free transfer capture and contract length|first=John|last=McDougall|newspaper=[[Manchester Evening News]]|date=9 May 2022}}</ref> In January 2023, he was ruled out for the rest of the season due to injury.<ref>[https://www.theboltonnews.co.uk/sport/23231419.ian-evatt-bolton-wanderers-signing-randell-williams-hull-city/ The Bolton News: "Ian Evatt on Bolton Wanderers' signing Randell Williams from Hull City: With Jack Iredale out for up to four months, Wanderers do have a decision to make at left wing-back for the visit of Plymouth on Saturday."]</ref>

Iredale moved to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in August 2024, signing a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c86ly628yy2o |title=Defender Jack Iredale joins Hibs on two-year deal from Bolton |website=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2024 |accessdate=11 March 2025}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Hibs on 2 March 2025, a match-winning goal in an [[Edinburgh derby]] against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c9q4j1nwjprt |title=Hibs beat Hearts in Scottish Premiership to jump to third after derby thriller |website=BBC Sport |first=George |last=O'Neill |date=2 March 2025 |accessdate=11 March 2025}}</ref> that won the [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year (lower leagues)|PFA Scotland goal of the season]] award for [[2024–25 in Scottish football|2024–25]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/every-pfa-scotland-award-winner-35169330  |title=Every PFA Scotland award winner as John McGlynn pips Brendan Rodgers to make it 2 in a row |newspaper=Daily Record |first=Fraser |last=Wilson |date=4 May 2025 |accessdate=5 May 2025}}</ref> He signed a new contract with Hibs in April 2025, which is due to expire in the summer of 2028.<ref>{{cite news |title=Iredale extends Hibs stay to 2028 |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cly1zyw99djo |date=24 April 2025 |accessdate=25 April 2025}}</ref>

===International===
Iredale was selected for a training camp of the full [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] squad in May 2025, ahead of [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (AFC)|2026 World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Japan national football team|Japan]] and [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/squad-notes-six-players-return-three-set-first-socceroos-training-camp-abu-dhabi |title=Squad Notes: Six players return, with three set for first Socceroos training camp in Abu Dhabi |website=www.socceroos.com |first=Taryn |last=Heddo |date=16 May 2025 |accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-world-cup-jack-iredale-socceroos-5131997 |title=Hibs boost international reputation with another World Cup call-up |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |first=John |last=Greechan |date=16 May 2025 |accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref>

'''Ante Palaversa''' (born 6 April 2000) is a Croatian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==Club career==

===Hajduk Split===
Born in [[Split, Croatia]], Palaversa started his youth career with the [[HNK Hajduk Split Reserves and Academy|Hajduk Split academy]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ante Palaversa: I'm glad that coach Kopic trusts young players |url=https://hajduk.hr/eng/article/ante-palaversa-i-m-glad-that-coach-kopic-trusts-young-players/6372 |publisher=HNK Hajduk Split |accessdate=18 August 2018 |date=17 July 2018}}</ref> At the end of the 2016–17 season, he won the Best Player of the Youth League award and was subsequently promoted to the reserve team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ante Palaversa: Nagradu posvećujem momčadi, nije bilo lako igrati po ovakvim vrućinama | trans-title = Ante Palaversa: I dedicate the team prize, it was not easy to play with this kind of heat |url=http://dalmatinskiportal.hr/sport/ante-palaversa--nagradu-posvecujem-momcadi--nije-bilo-lako-igrati-po-ovakvim-vrucinama/22806 |publisher=Dalmatinski Portal |accessdate=18 August 2018 |language=Croatian |date=26 June 2018}}</ref> After playing regularly for the reserve team in the second tier, he was promoted to the senior team in June 2018 by manager [[Željko Kopić]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Novi dijamant Hajduka Ante Palaversa blista na pripremama: Ovo je ispunjenje mojih snova | trans-title = New Hajduk's Diamond Ante Palavers Blinks on Preparations: This is the fulfillment of my dreams |url=https://www.slobodnadalmacija.hr/sport/hajduk/clanak/id/556710/novi-dijamant-hajduka-ante-palaversa-blista-na-pripremama-ovo-je-ispunjenje-mojih-snova |publisher=Slobodna Dalmacija |accessdate=18 August 2018 |language=Croatian |date=17 July 2018}}</ref>
On 26 July 2018, Palaversa made his first team debut, coming on as a substitute in a 1–0 victory over Bulgarian club [[PFC Slavia Sofia|Slavia Sofia]] in a [[UEFA Europa League]] qualifying match.<ref>{{cite web |title=Palaversa after the debut: This is my dream come true, thank you for applause |url=https://hajduk.hr/eng/article/palaversa-after-the-debut-this-is-my-dream-come-true-thank-you-for-applause/6393 |publisher=HNK Hajduk Split |accessdate=18 August 2018 |date=27 July 2018}}</ref> On 26 August, he scored his first goal for the club in a 2–2 draw against [[NK Inter Zaprešić|Inter Zaprešić]], scoring a volley from 21-metres.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prvijenac za pamćenje: Kada dam gol, onda je to obično ovakav nekakav | trans-title = Remember that when I get a shot, then this is usually something like this |url=https://slobodnadalmacija.hr/sport/hajduk/clanak/id/562728/prvijenac-za-pamcenje-kada-dam-gol-onda-je-to-obicno-ovakav-nekakav |publisher=Slobodan Dalmacija |accessdate=27 August 2018 |date=26 August 2018}}</ref>

===Manchester City===
On 28 January 2019, it was announced that Palaversa would be joining [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] for an eventual fee of €7 million, instantly returning to Hajduk on loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Palaversa leti u Manchester na potpis ugovora, sutra se očekuje konačna potvrda | trans-title = Palaversa flying off to Manchester to sign a contract.|url=https://slobodnadalmacija.hr/sport/hajduk/clanak/id/586426/palaversa-leti-u-manchester-na-potpis-ugovora-sutra-se-ocekuje-konacna-potvrda |publisher=Slobodan Dalmacija |accessdate=28 January 2019 |date=28 January 2019}}</ref> He completed the move on 31 January.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47073192|title=Ante Palaversa: Man City complete Hajduk Split signing|date=31 January 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref>

====Loan to Getafe====
On 31 August 2020, Palaversa joined [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pledgetimes.com/official-ante-palaversa-on-loan-to-getafe-for-one-season/ |title=Official: Ante Palaversa, on loan to Getafe for one season |website=Pledge Times |date=31 August 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==== Loan to KV Kortrijk ====
On 26 January 2021, Palaversa moved to Belgian club [[K.V. Kortrijk|KV Kortrijk]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=26 January 2021|title=Jupiler Pro League: Courtrai accueille Ante Palaversa (Manchester City)|trans-title=Jupiler Pro League: Kortrijk welcomes Ante Palaversa (Manchester City)|url=https://www.lavenir.net/cnt/dmf20210126_01549170/jupiler-pro-league-courtrai-accueille-ante-palaversa-manchester-city|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126220509/https://www.lavenir.net/cnt/dmf20210126_01549170/jupiler-pro-league-courtrai-accueille-ante-palaversa-manchester-city |archive-date=26 January 2021 |access-date=27 January 2021|website=Lavenir.net|language=fr}}</ref>

===Troyes===
On 31 August 2022, having never made an appearance for City, Palaversa joined [[ES Troyes AC|Troyes]], another club within the [[City Football Group]], on a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ante Palaversa joins ESTAC!|url=https://www.estac.fr/actualites/21687/ante-palaversa-rejoint-l-estac.html|publisher=[[ES Troyes AC|Troyes]]|date=31 August 2022|access-date=31 August 2022|archive-date=14 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014125959/https://www.estac.fr/actualites/21687/ante-palaversa-rejoint-l-estac.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
On 8 August 2024, Palaversa signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a one-year contract, with the Scottish Premiership club having the option of a further two years, which was exercised in January 2025 with the club extending his stay until summer 2027.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6666921/aberdeen-fc-ante-palaversa-new-deal/ |date=11 January 2025 |accessdate=11 January 2025 | title=Aberdeen midfielder Ante Palaversa signs long-term deal with the Dons }}</ref>

'''Jack James Walton''' (born 23 April 1998) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

==Club career==
Walton started his youth career with [[Bolton Wanderers F.C. Reserves and Academy|Bolton Wanderers' Academy]] before switching to [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] in 2013, where he was named Academy Player of the year for 2014–15. In August 2015, he signed his first professional contract with the club, of three years.<ref name=TurnsPro>{{cite news |title=Walton is future number one after signing first pro deal |url=https://www.barnsleychronicle.com/article/walton-is-future-number-one-after-signing-first-pro-deal |newspaper=Barnsley Chronicle |access-date=5 September 2018 |date=28 August 2015}}</ref>

On 25 January 2016, Walton was loaned out to [[Conference North]] club [[Stalybridge Celtic F.C.|Stalybridge Celtic]] on a 28-day youth loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Walton joins Stalybridge Celtic on loan |url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2016/January/walton-joins-stalybridge-celtic-on-loan/ |publisher=Barnsley F.C. |access-date=5 September 2018 |date=25 January 2016}}</ref> He made his debut the same day in a goalless draw with [[Curzon Ashton F.C.|Curzon Ashton]].<ref name=StalyProfile>{{cite web |title=Jack Walton |url=http://www.stalybridgeceltic.co.uk/play.php?code=WALTJ |publisher=Stalybridge Celtic F.C. |access-date=16 August 2019}}</ref>

Walton returned to Stalybridge Celtic on 22 September 2017 for one month,<ref>{{cite web |title=Jack Walton joins Stalybridge Celtic on loan |url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2017/september/walton-loan/ |publisher=Barnsley F.C. |access-date=5 September 2018 |date=22 September 2017}}</ref> during which he played eight times and kept three [[clean sheet]]s. Upon returning to his parent club, he said "I really enjoyed my time with Stalybridge and I can't thank them enough for taking the chance on me to play for them".<ref>{{cite web |title=Jack Walton returns to Oakwell |url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2017/october/walton-returns/ |publisher=Barnsley F.C. |access-date=5 September 2018 |date=24 October 2017}}</ref> In January 2018, he was reloaned to Stalybridge Celtic for the remainder of the season,<ref>{{cite web |title=Jack's the lad for Stalybridge |url=http://www.stalybridgecorrespondent.co.uk/2018/02/09/jacks-the-lad-for-stalybridge/ |newspaper=Stalybridge Correspondent |access-date=5 September 2018 |date=9 February 2018}}</ref> but was recalled in March and was named on the bench for a [[EFL Championship|Championship]] match at home to [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Reds equal club record after home defeat to Millwall |url=https://www.barnsleychronicle.com/article/reds-equal-club-record-after-home-defeat-to-millwall |newspaper=Barnsley Chronicle |access-date=5 September 2018 |date=17 March 2018}}</ref> He made a brief return to Stalybridge<ref>{{cite web |title=Jack Walton returns to Stalybridge |url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2018/march/walton-returns/ |publisher=Barnsley F.C. |access-date=5 September 2018 |date=21 March 2018}}</ref> before, on 24 April 2018, making his debut for Barnsley in a 3–0 league defeat against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]].<ref>{{cite news On 2 July 2018, Walton signed a two-year contract extension with Barnsley.<ref name=2018Contract>{{cite news |title=Jack Walton: Barnsley goalkeeper signs new contract |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44688285 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=27 January 2019 |date=2 July 2018}}</ref>
On 13 August 2020, Walton signed a new three-year contract extension with Barnsley.<ref name=2020Contract>{{cite news |title=Jack Walton: Barnsley goalkeeper signs new three-year contract |url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2020/august/walton-2023/ |publisher=Barnsley FC }}</ref>

On 30 January 2023, after making just one league appearance all season, Walton moved up a division by signing for [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] for an undisclosed fee. Luton goalkeeper [[Harry Isted]] moved in the opposite direction on loan for the rest of the season on the same day.<ref name=LutonMove>{{cite news |title=Jack Walton: Jack Walton joins from Barnsley and Harry Isted heads the other way! |url=https://www.lutontown.co.uk/news/2023/january/jack-walton/ |publisher=Luton Town FC }}</ref> Luton's season culminated in promotion to the [[Premier League]], but Walton failed to make an appearance. He left on loan prior to the season starting.

On 10 July 2023, it was announced that Walton had signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref name=DundeeUtdMove>{{cite news |title=Jack Walton: JACK WALTON MAKES LOAN SWITCH TO TANNADICE FROM LUTON TOWN |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7909/JACK-WALTON-MAKES-LOAN-SWITCH-TO-TANNADICE-FROM-LUTON-TOWN.html |publisher=Dundee United FC }}</ref> On 26 June 2024, having enjoyed a successful spell, which saw United promoted to the [[Scottish Premiership]], Walton returned to [[Tannadice]] on another season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/8446/CHAMPIONSHIP-WINNING-STOPPER-JACK-WALTON-RETURNS.html|title=CHAMPIONSHIP-WINNING STOPPER JACK WALTON RETURNS|publisher=Dundee United FC|date=26 June 2024|accessdate=26 June 2024}}</ref> 

On 22 July 2025, Walton joined Championship club [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] on a three-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.pnefc.net/news/2025/july/22/north-end-bring-in-goalkeeper-jack-walton/|title=North End Bring In Goalkeeper Jack Walton|website=www.pnefc.net|date=22 July 2025|accessdate=15 April 2026}}</ref> On 15 April 2026, he joined [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]] on a seven-day emergency loan.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.cambridgeunited.com/news/jack-walton-joins-emergency-loan|title=Jack Walton joins on Emergency Loan|website=www.cambridgeunitedcom|date=15 April 2026|accessdate=15 April 2026}}</ref>
