'''Rabbi Matondo''' (born 9 September 2000) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]. Born in England, he plays for the [[Wales national football team|Wales national team]].

Matondo played youth football for [[Cardiff City F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Cardiff City]] and [[Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy|Manchester City]]. He joined German club [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] in January 2019, where he made 32 first-team appearances and was sent on loan to [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] and [[Cercle Brugge KSV|Cercle Brugge]]. He had a three-and-a-half year spell at Scottish club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] before moving to Norwegian side [[SK Brann|Brann]].

Born in England to parents from the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|DR Congo]], Matondo was eligible to play for either country, as well as Wales, where he grew up. Having played for the [[England national under-15 football team|England under-15]] team, he later opted to represent Wales and played at [[Wales national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Wales national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels before making his debut for the senior national team in November 2018.

==Early life==
Matondo was born in [[Liverpool]], England but moved to [[south Wales]] as a child.<ref name="poached">{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cardiff-city-one-wales-brightest-11929955 |title=Cardiff City have one of Wales' brightest young talents snatched away from them by Manchester City |website=WalesOnline |publisher=Media Wales |last=Abbandonato |first=Paul |date=23 September 2016 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref> He grew up in the [[Tremorfa]] area of [[Cardiff]] where he first played football in local parks with his father and brothers.<ref name="kid">{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manchester-citys-rabbi-matondo-cardiff-15244426 |title=Manchester City's Rabbi Matondo: The Cardiff kid who's grown up to be the fastest player at one of the world's biggest clubs |website=WalesOnline |publisher=Media Wales |last=Coleman |first=Tom |date=9 October 2018 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref> His father Dada played football in his native [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|DR Congo]]. Two of his brothers, Cedrick and Japhet, also played football for Cardiff City, Newport County and Stoke City at youth level.<ref name="kid"/> As a teenager he attended [[Llanishen High School|St. Illtyds Catholic Highschool]].<ref name="kid"/>

==Club career==

===Early career===
Matondo began his career as a youth player with [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]. In 2016, he moved to [[Premier League]] side [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] for a small compensation fee under the [[Elite Player Performance Plan]], an initiative created by the Premier League regarding movement of youth players.<ref name="poached"/> Cardiff appealed against the move and Matondo was blocked from playing for Manchester City until March 2017 when the appeal was denied. However, a fee of £500,000 was reported to have been agreed.<ref name="cleared">{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manchester-city-starlet-rabbi-matondo-12734503 |title=Manchester City starlet Rabbi Matondo cleared to play after being snatched away from Cardiff City |website=WalesOnline |publisher=Media Wales |last=Vittles |first=Jack |date=13 March 2017 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref>

He made his debut for the [[Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy|Manchester City U21]] side in the [[EFL Trophy]] on 15 August 2017 against [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/eds/match-report/2017/august/rotherham-united-man-city-eds-checkatrade-trophy-match-report |title=Rotherham United 1–1 City |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |last=Edwards |first=John |date=15 August 2017 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref> scoring his first goal in the side's next match, a 2–1 defeat to [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mancity.com/citytv/match%20highlights/2017/october/~/link.aspx?_id=4151928D76C64F719BDB0E23801ADA6A&_z=z&=1 |title=Bradford City 2–1 City |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |last=Edwards |first=John |date=24 October 2017 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref> He added two more goals in the [[2018–19 EFL Trophy]],  the game's only away to [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] in the final group game,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Garnett |first1=Richard |title=Tranmere knocked out of the Checkatrade Trophy by Manchester City U21s |url=https://www.wirralglobe.co.uk/news/17190826.tranmere-knocked-out-of-the-checkatrade-trophy-by-manchester-city-u21s/ |access-date=20 February 2019 |work=Wirral Globe |date=31 October 2018}}</ref> and one more in a 3–3 draw at [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] in the second round, as well as netting in the subsequent penalty shootout win.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reds out of trophy after shoot-out loss to City kids |url=https://www.barnsleychronicle.com/article/barnsley-3-manchester-city-u21s-3-2018-12-04 |access-date=20 February 2019 |work=Barnsley Chronicle |date=4 December 2018}}</ref>

===Schalke 04===
On 30 January 2019, Matondo signed for [[Bundesliga]] club [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] for a reported fee of up to £11 million on a four-and-a-half-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/man-city-rabbi-matondo-schalke-15755225|title=Rabbi Matondo transfer: Manchester City starlet completes £11million Schalke switch|publisher=Manchester Evening News|date=30 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47030685|title=Rabbi Matondo: Schalke sign Manchester City and Wales winger|date=30 January 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=30 January 2019}}</ref> He made his professional league debut three days later in a 2–0 home loss to [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], as a 75th-minute substitute for [[Sebastian Rudy]]; on 16 February he was given a start in a goalless home draw with [[SC Freiburg]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Former Manchester City youth player Rabbi Matondo: "It's been easy to adapt at Schalke"|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/ex-man-city-youth-player-rabbi-matondo-makes-full-bundesliga-debut-schalke-3377-2429|access-date=20 February 2019|publisher=Bundesliga|date=16 February 2019}}</ref> On 28 September 2019, he scored his first goal for Schalke in a 3–1 away victory over [[RB Leipzig]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/rabbi-matondo-schalke-i-think-we-can-keep-this-going-now-7249|title=Schalke's Rabbi Matondo: "I think we can keep this going now"|publisher=Bundesliga|date=29 September 2019}}</ref>

On 7 January 2021, Matondo joined [[EFL Championship]] club [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on a loan deal until the end of the [[2020–21 Stoke City F.C. season|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/2021/january/Matondo-completes-loan-move/|title=Matondo completes loan move|date=7 January 2021|website=Stoke City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55580553|title=Rabbi Matondo: Stoke City sign Wales winger on loan from FC Schalke 04|date=7 January 2021|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He played 11 times for Stoke, scoring once in a 1–1 draw with [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on 24 April 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56781840|title=Nottingham Forest 1-1 Stoke|publisher=[[BBC]] |date=24 April 2021 |access-date=26 April 2021}}</ref>

On 9 August 2021, Matondo agreed to join [[Cercle Brugge KSV|Cercle Brugge]] on a season-long loan with an option to make the move permanent.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://schalke04.de/en/team/rabbi-matondo-moves-loan-cercle-brugge/|title=Rabbi Matondo moves on loan to Cercle Brugge|website=FC Schalke 04|date=9 August 2021}}</ref>

===Rangers===
On 12 July 2022, [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] announced the signing of Matondo on a four-year deal, subject to international clearance.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62134902 |title=Rabbi Matondo: Rangers sign Wales winger from Schalke on four-year deal |website=BBC Sport |date=12 July 2022 |accessdate=12 July 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rangers Sign Rabbi Matondo |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/rangers-sign-rabbi-matondo/2XKonGDxT6rHWIrjyECCFj |access-date=12 July 2022 |website=www.rangers.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> He made his debut for the club against [[Belgium|Belgian]] side [[Royale Union Saint-Gilloise|Union Saint-Gilloise]] during a [[UEFA Champions League]] qualifier loss on 2 August.<ref>{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62377416   | title=Union Saint-Gilloise 2-0 Rangers  | work=BBC Sport | date=2 August 2022 }}</ref>
On 4 October 2022, he made his 5th [[UEFA Champions League]] appearance for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] away against [[Liverpool]] as a substitute. Rangers lost 2-0, however their first big chance in the game came through Matondo in the 84th minute (3 minutes after he came on), where his pace allowed him to breeze past [[Joel Matip]] and [[nutmeg (association football)|nutmeg]] Liverpool goalkeeper [[Alisson Becker]], but had his shot cleared off the line by [[Kostas Tsimikas]] before it could be tapped into the net by [[Fashion Sakala]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/kostas-tsimikas-liverpool-aces-incredible-goal-line-clearance-vs-rangers-35962425|title=Kostas Tsimikas: Liverpool ace's incredible goal line clearance vs Rangers|publisher=One Football |date=4 October 2022 |access-date= 5 October 2022}}</ref>
Matondo scored his first [[UEFA Champions League]] goal in a 1st leg Qualifier on 22 August 2023 vs [[PSV Eindhoven]] slotting home a first-time finish into the bottom corner after a counter-attack to equalise.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/685787|title=Rangers 2-2 PSV Eindhoven (22 Aug, 2023) Final Score|publisher=ESPN |date=22 August 2023 |access-date=8 January 2024}}</ref> He left Rangers in March 2026.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Rabbi Matondo Joins SK Brann|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rabbi-matondo-joins-sk-brann/w6EWu0vVDv0BcFLa582jS |access-date=31 March 2026 |website=www.rangers.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref>

===Loan to Hannover 96===
On 30 January 2025, Matondo signed for [[Hannover 96]] on loan from Rangers for the remainder of the [[2024–25 Hannover 96 season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hannover96.de/newscenter/news/details/34807-debuet-unter-weltfussball-legende-fuenf-fakten-ueber-rabbi-matondo.html|title=Five Facts About Rabbi Matondo|website=hannover96.de|date=30 January 2025}}</ref>
Matondo scored 34 minutes into his debut against [[Hamburger SV]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rangersreview.co.uk/news/24903625.watch-rangers-loanee-matondo-scores-stunning-solo-goal-debut/|title=Watch as Rangers loanee Matondo scores stunning solo goal on debut|publisher=Rangers Review|date=2 February 2025}}</ref>

===SK Brann===

On 31 March 2026, Matondo joined [[SK Brann|Brann]] on a permanent deal.<ref name="auto"/> In August 2026 he was released by Brann.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cj360lpyzx7o|title=Gossip: Sheffield United lead race for winger Rabbi Matondo|date=21 July 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
In September 2026, Matondo joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on trial<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pilcher |first=Ross |date=26 September 2026 |title=Rabbi Matondo gets Hibs transfer chance as former Rangers winger joins Marink Reedijk's squad in La Manga |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/rabbi-matondo-gets-hibs-transfer-37705452 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=www.dailyrecord.co.uk}}</ref>, before joining them on a free transfer on 7 October, signing a contract until the end of the season, with an option for an additional year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cmy4xpgeydn3o|title=Rabbi Matondo: Hibernian sign former Rangers winger for rest of season with one-year option|date=7 October 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Rabbi Matondo Signs For Hibs|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2026/october/07/rabbi-matondo-signs-for-hibs/|work=hibernianfc.co.uk|date=7 October 2026}}</ref> Matondo made his debut for the club on 10 October in a 1-0 loss at [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

==International career==
Matondo was eligible to represent DR Congo, England or Wales at international level.<ref name="kid"/> He represented England at under-15 level before switching allegiance to Wales at [[Wales national under-17 football team|under-17]] level.<ref name="cleared"/> He made 10 appearances for the under-17 team.<ref name="walesu17u21stats">{{cite web |url=https://www.besoccer.com/player/matches/r-matondo-319498 |title=R. Matondo |website=besoccer.com |access-date=14 August 2022}}</ref> He received his first call up to the [[Wales national under-21 football team|Wales under-21]] squad in September 2017,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41428832 |title=Wales add Cian Harries and Rabbi Matondo |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 September 2017 |access-date=21 November 2018}}</ref> making his debut for the side in a 3–1 victory over [[Liechtenstein national under-21 football team|Liechtenstein]].<ref name="Soccerway">{{Soccerway|426966|accessdate=21 November 2018}}</ref> After appearing in four qualifying matches as a substitute,<ref name="Soccerway"/> he made his first start for the under-21 side in a 1–1 draw with [[Georgia national under-21 football team|Georgia]] in the second of two friendlies against the nation in June 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sofascore.com/georgia-u21-wales-u21/hwcsyCc |title=Georgia U21 1–1 Wales U21 |website=sofascore.com |access-date=21 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.faw.cymru/en/news/u21-squad-announced-georgia-double-header/ |title=U21 Squad Announced For Georgia Double Header |publisher=Football Association of Wales |date=20 May 2018 |access-date=21 November 2018}}</ref> He played eight games in total at under-21 level.<ref name="walesu17u21stats"/>

In November 2018, Matondo received his first call up for the [[Wales national football team|senior]] Welsh squad for a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Albania national football team|Albania]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/wales-add-manchester-citys-rabbi-15431237 |title=Wales add Manchester City's Rabbi Matondo to squad for Albania friendly and fans are loving it |website=WalesOnline |publisher=Media Wales |last=Davies |first=Matthew |date=18 November 2018 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref> He made his international debut during the match on 20 November as a 78th-minute substitute in place of [[Sam Vokes]] as Wales lost 1–0 in [[Elbasan]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/45710849 |title=Albania 1–0 Wales |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 November 2018 |access-date=20 November 2018}}</ref>

In May 2019, after travelling back to England from a Welsh national team training camp in Portugal, Matondo was escorted from the plane by police after "behaving disruptively".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48465481|title=Rabbi Matondo: Police escort 'disruptive' Wales winger from flight|date=30 May 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref>

On 8 October 2020, Matondo started for Wales in a friendly against England.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54366319|title=England 3-0 Wales: Dominic Calvert-Lewin debut goal helps England beat Wales |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 October 2020 |access-date=8 October 2020}}</ref>

On 1 June 2022, Matondo came on as a half time substitute for Wales in a [[UEFA Nations League|Nations League]] Group A game against [[Poland national football team|Poland]]. Wales lost 2–1 with Matondo providing the assist for [[Jonny Williams]]'s Wales goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61574469|title=Poland 2-1 Wales: Much changed visitors impress in Nations League defeat|publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 June 2022 |access-date=2 June 2022}}</ref>

On 22 March 2025, Matondo came on in the second half for Wales in a [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|World Cup qualifier]] against [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]]. Wales won 3-1 with Matondo scoring his first international goal in the closing stages of the match.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c625rzpeld6t | title=Reaction as Wales beat Kazakhstan 3-1 in their opening 2026 World Cup qualifier }}</ref>

'''Nesta Pierre Guinness-Walker''' (born 14 September 1999) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|left back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==Personal life==
He is the grandson of actor [[Matthew Guinness]] and the great-grandson of actor Sir [[Alec Guinness]].<ref name = "perform">{{Cite web|url=https://londonnewsonline.co.uk/exclusive-interview-with-afc-wimbledon-prospect-nesta-guiness-walker-on-looking-to-perform-on-a-football-pitch-not-a-stage-or-the-big-screen/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190914180053/https://www.londonnewsonline.co.uk/exclusive-interview-with-afc-wimbledon-prospect-nesta-guiness-walker-on-looking-to-perform-on-a-football-pitch-not-a-stage-or-the-big-screen/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=14 September 2019|title=Exclusive interview with AFC Wimbledon prospect Nesta Guiness-Walker on looking to perform on a football pitch – not a stage or the big screen|date=30 August 2019|accessdate=26 June 2021}}</ref> He grew up in [[Twickenham]] and is of part-Barbadian descent.<ref name = "perform"/>

==Career==
Guinness-Walker played youth football for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]],<ref name = "BBC"/> spending two years with Chelsea and one year with Tottenham, before leaving at the age of 11,<ref name = "perform"/> before playing Sunday League football as a teenager.<ref name = "Wimbledon"/> He joined non-league [[Metropolitan Police F.C.|Metropolitan Police]] at the age of 17.<ref name = "Wimbledon"/> Following a successful trial period he signed for [[AFC Wimbledon]] in May 2019.<ref name = "BBC">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48398624|title=Nesta Guinness-Walker: AFC Wimbledon sign left-back from Metropolitan Police|date=24 May 2019|accessdate=30 May 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Wimbledon in a 2–1 defeat to [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] on 20 August 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49326904 |title=Ipswich 2–1 AFC Wimbledon |date=20 August 2019 |publisher=BBC|accessdate=21 August 2019}}</ref> He was offered a new contract by the club at the end of the 2021–22 season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2022/may/retained-list-announced/|title=Retained List Announced|website=www.afcwimbledon.co.uk}}</ref> but he left the club on 5 July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afcwimbledon.co.uk/news/2022/july/squad-update/|title=Squad Update|website=www.afcwimbledon.co.uk}}</ref>

On 29 July 2022, [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] announced the signing of Guinness-Walker on a one-year contract following a successful trial.<ref>{{cite web |title=GUINNESS-WALKER SIGNS ONE-YEAR DEAL WITH ROYALS |url=https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2022/july/29/guinness-walker-signs-one-year-deal-with-royals/ |website=readingfc.co.uk |publisher=Reading F.C. |access-date=29 July 2022 |date=29 July 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62348280|title=Reading sign left-back Guinness-Walker|work=BBC Sport |date=29 July 2022 }}</ref> On 17 May 2023, Reading activated a clause in Guinness-Walker's contract to keep him at the club for the [[2022–23 Reading F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NEW DEALS OFFERED AS CONTRACTS COME TO THEIR CONCLUSION |url=https://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/2023/may/17/new-deals-offered-as-contracts-come-to-their-conclusion/ |website=readingfc.co.uk |publisher=Reading F.C. |access-date=17 May 2023 |date=17 May 2023}}</ref>

On 24 January 2024, Guinness-Walker joined League One club [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2023–24 Stevenage F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stevenagefc.com/news/2024/january/nesta-guinness-walker-reading-stevenage-fc-football-club-sky-bet-league-one-efl-english-football-league/|title=Nesta Guinness-Walker joins on loan from Reading|website=www.stevenagefc.com|date=24 January 2024|accessdate=24 January 2024}}</ref>

He was released by Reading at the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2024 |title=Clinton Mola and Sam Hutchinson among four released by Reading |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cw940xrvd2po |access-date=8 May 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 27 September 2024, Guinness-Walker joined League One side [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] on a short-term contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ntfc.co.uk/news/2024/september/27/nesta-guinness-walker-signs-for-northampton-town/|title=NESTA GUINNESS-WALKER SIGNS FOR NORTHAMPTON TOWN|website=www.ntfc.co.uk|date=27 September 2024|accessdate=27 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c5yj7dv18p1o|title=Nesta Guinness-Walker: Ex-Reading full-back joins Northampton Town|date=27 September 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> The contract was extended in December 2024 until summer 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.northamptonchron.co.uk/sport/football/cobblers-defenders-sign-extended-contracts-4917779|title=Cobblers defenders sign extended contracts|date=19 December 2024|website=Northampton Chronicle and Echo}}</ref> He was offered a new contract at the end of the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cnvpqrmz63zo|title=Northampton Town: Jon Guthrie deal extended, but Jordan Willis and Tom Eaves released|date=5 May 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 8 July 2026, Guinness-Walker joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dons Land Nesta Guinness-Walker on Two-Year Deal - Aberdeen FC |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/en/news/dons-land-nesta-guinness-walker-on-two-year-deal |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=www.afc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

'''Lewis William Mayo''' (born 19 March 2000) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

Mayo began his career at Rangers and has previously had loan spells with [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Early life==
Mayo excelled as a student and attained straight As at High School.<ref name=":0" />

==Career==
A highly-promising graduate of the [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] youth academy, of which he was a member since the age of
10,<ref>[https://www.glasgowworld.com/sport/football/bishopbriggs-club-helping-to-nurture-the-stars-of-tomorrow-2747624?amp Bishopbriggs club helping to nurture the stars of tomorrow], Glasgow World, 28 June 2012</ref> Mayo signed a three-year deal with the [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]] club in October 2018 under the management of [[Steven Gerrard]] and academy manager [[Graeme Murty]].{{Citation needed|date=March 2020}} Mayo is described as a versatile player, however primarily operates in defensive positions.{{Citation needed|date=March 2020}}

Mayo featured and scored for Rangers in a 5–0 pre-season win over [[Oxford United]] at Ibrox and has also played in three [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] games for Rangers Colts, making it to the competition's semi-final stage in 2020, after captaining the side for a 2–0 quarter-final win over [[Wrexham F.C.|Wrexham]].{{Citation needed|date=March 2020}}

A Rangers fan since a young age, Mayo described the challenges of playing against players such as [[Jermain Defoe]] and [[Alfredo Morelos]]: "Jermain Defoe has been excellent as well because I play against him. He will tell me what I am doing well. It is hard and the thing is, it is either him or Alfredo Morelos in training, so you are not really getting a break. It is one or the other."<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1=McCarthy |first1=David |title=Lewis Mayo reveals relentless Rangers training regime as Alfredo Morelos and Jermain Defoe provide ultimate school of hard knocks |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/lewis-mayo-reveals-relentless-rangers-20889088 |website=www.dailyrecord.co.uk |date=16 November 2019 |publisher=Daily Record |accessdate=4 March 2020}}</ref>

===Loan moves===
In the January 2020 transfer window, Mayo joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Partick Thistle]] on loan until the end of the season with the [[Maryhill]] side.<ref>{{cite web |title=Loan News: Lewis Mayo joins on loan |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/loan-news-lewis-mayo-joins-on-loan/ |website=www.ptfc.co.uk |publisher=Partick Thistle F.C. |accessdate=4 March 2020}}</ref> Mayo made his debut in a 0–0 draw at home to [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]], receiving a man of the match award for his performance.<ref>{{cite news |title=Thistle & QoS fight out goalless draw |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51623933 |access-date=29 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mayo looking to build on debut bow |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/mayo-looking-to-build-on-debut-bow/ |website=Partick Thistle FC |access-date=29 June 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Due to the Coronavirus pandemic cutting short the season, Mayo's loan was ended early as he returned to Rangers after making 3 appearances for The Jags, with his game time being limited due to being injured upon signing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/loan-update-2/|title=Loan Update|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

Mayo moved on a season-long loan to Scottish Championship side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in September 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/18748043.dunfermline-sign-lewis-mayo-rangers-season-long-loan/ |title=Dunfermline sign Lewis Mayo from Rangers on season long loan |first=Ross |last=Hart |work=Dunfermline Press |publisher=Newsquest |date=25 September 2020 |accessdate=25 September 2020}}</ref>

He was loaned to Partick Thistle for a second time in July 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/19471220.partick-thistle-sign-rangers-defender-lewis-mayo-loan/|title=Partick Thistle sign Rangers defender Lewis Mayo on loan|website=Glasgow Times|date=27 July 2021 }}</ref> Mayo scored his first Thistle and career goal, scoring the winner in a 1-0 win over Hamilton Academical.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59271689|title=Partick Thistle edge out Hamilton|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In June 2022, Mayo joined newly promoted [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-23 |title=Lewis Mayo joins Killie on a season-long loan from Rangers |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/lewis-mayo-joins-killie-on-a-season-long-loan-from-rangers/ |access-date=2022-06-23 |website=Kilmarnock FC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/rangers-defender-lewis-mayo-joins-kilmarnock-on-loan |title=Rangers defender Lewis Mayo joins Kilmarnock on loan |first=Andy |last=Coyle |website=STV Sport |date=23 June 2022 |accessdate=23 June 2022}}</ref>

=== Kilmarnock ===
On 20 July 2023, Mayo joined [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] for an undisclosed fee,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lewis Mayo Signs For Kilmarnock |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/lewis-mayo-signs-for-kilmarnock/5wSRzRTsqA3sSqF9RpiYAk |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=www.rangers.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> signing a three-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Highet |first=Lochlin |date=2023-07-20 |title=Kilmarnock sign Rangers defender Lewis Mayo permanently on three-year deal |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/rangers-defender-lewis-mayo-joins-30514943 |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
On 28 May 2026, Mayo agreed to join Scottish Premiership club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a three-year deal.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/en/news/dons-land-defender-as-mayo-agrees-aberdeen-move|title=Dons Land Defender as Mayo Agrees Aberdeen Move|website=www.afc.co.uk|date=28 May 2026|accessdate=28 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Josh Mulligan''' (born 12 November 2002) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as either a midfielder or defender for {{Scottish football updater|Hibernia}} club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{soccerbase|120208|accessdate=19 August 2019}}</ref> He has previously played for Lochee Harp Boys Club, [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] and [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]].

==Club career==
===Dundee===
Mulligan made his first team debut with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in the final game of the [[2018–19 Dundee F.C. season|2018–19 season]] against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], in which he came on as a substitute.<ref>{{cite web|last=McDougall|first=Mark|date=18 May 2019|title=What Dundee debutants were doing one hour after facing St Mirren|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/what-dundee-debutants-were-doing-16166374|accessdate=15 September 2019|publisher=Daily Record}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=McLauchlin|first=Brian|date=18 May 2019|title=Dundee 2–3 St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48236247|accessdate=15 September 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Mulligan would feature in the [[Scottish League Cup]] the following season.

In January 2020, Mulligan went on loan with [[Scottish League Two]] league leaders [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2 January 2020|title=Dundee midfielder Mulligan signs on at Cove Rangers for rest of the campaign|url=https://www.coverangersfc.com/news/dundee-midfielder-mulligan-signs-on-at-cove-rangers-for-rest-of-the-campaign/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200712011627/https://www.coverangersfc.com/news/dundee-midfielder-mulligan-signs-on-at-cove-rangers-for-rest-of-the-campaign/|archive-date=12 July 2020|access-date=10 July 2020|website=Cove Rangers FC|url-status=dead}}</ref> Despite the early curtailment of the season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland|COVID-19 pandemic]], Cove were declared League Two champions after a resolution to finish the season from the [[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]] was passed.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=15 April 2020|title=SPFL Resolution Approved By Clubs In All Four Divisions|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/spfl-resolution-approved-by-clubs-in-all-four-di|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=10 July 2020|website=SPFL.co.uk}}</ref>

In October 2020, Mulligan signed a new contract with Dundee keeping him at the club until 2023, and immediately joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=5 October 2020|title=Josh signs new deals and moves on loan|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/josh-signs-new-deal-and-moves-on-loan/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=5 October 2020|website=Dundee FC}}</ref> Mulligan suffered an ankle injury early on in his club debut against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], and in November would undergo surgery that would keep him out until the following season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=10 October 2020|title=Dundee United 0 Peterhead 1|url=https://www.peterheadfc.org/2020/10/10/dundee-united-0-peterhead-1/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=21 November 2020|website=peterheadfc.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=19 November 2020|title=Josh Mulligan not available until 2021|url=https://www.peterheadfc.org/2020/11/19/josh-mulligan-not-available-until-2021/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=21 November 2020|website=peterheadfc.org}}</ref>

In June 2021, Mulligan would once again join Peterhead on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|date=17 June 2021|title=Lyall and Josh join Peterhead on loan|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/lyall-and-josh-join-peterhead-on-loan/|access-date=17 June 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> Despite this, Mulligan would represent Dundee B against Peterhead in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cran|first=George|title=Dundee B 1-2 Peterhead: Blue Toon come from behind to knock Dee youngsters out of Challenge Cup|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/2449165/dundee-b-1-2-peterhead-blue-toon-come-from-behind-to-knock-dee-youngsters-out-of-challenge-cup/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=The Courier|date=11 August 2021 |language=en-GB}}</ref> He would score his first senior goal with the ''Blue Toon'' in a 5–0 win against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Peterhead v Dumbarton|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58688243|access-date=2021-10-03}}</ref> During his successful 2nd stint with the club, Peterhead teammate and media personality [[Simon Ferry]] compared his work-rate to that of [[Gareth Bale]], and described him as "powerful, strong and direct", and as a "Rolls-Royce" footballer.<ref>{{Citation|title=HEARTS SNATCH DRAMATIC DRAW AT IBROX & SKY HAVE NO SPFL GAMES ON TV🤯{{!}} Keeping The Ball On The Ground| date=19 October 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uDQNzkGyfGE|language=en|access-date=2021-12-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Cran|first=George|title=Dundee kid Josh Mulligan responds to 'Rolls-Royce' praise AND Gareth Bale comparison from Peterhead star Si Ferry|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/2737284/rolls-royce-gareth-bale-dundeefc-josh-mulligan-praise-peterhead-si-ferry/|access-date=2021-12-06|website=The Courier|date=17 November 2021 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

After a successful first half to the season, Mulligan was recalled early by Dundee in January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-17|title=Players return from loan|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/players-return-from-loan/|access-date=2022-01-17|website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website|language=en-US}}</ref> He would make his first start for the team in February, in an away victory over [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Dundee fight back to move off bottom|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60225005|access-date=2022-02-09}}</ref> Mulligan would score his first goal for Dundee against his former club Peterhead in the [[Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Dundee see off impressive Peterhead|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60283722|access-date=2022-02-14}}</ref> His first league goal would come in a 3–1 victory over [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |title=Dundee 3-1 Hibs: Charlie Adam screamer caps first victory in 13 as Dee keep slim survival hopes alive |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/3281021/dundee-3-1-hibs-charlie-adam-screamer-caps-first-victory-in-13-as-dee-keep-slim-survival-hopes-alive/ |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=The Courier |date=10 May 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Mulligan would score the winner for Dundee's first league win of the [[2022–23 Dundee F.C. season|2022–23 season]] in an away win over [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Raith Rovers v Dundee |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62358465 |access-date=2022-08-06}}</ref> He followed that up a week later with a fine strike to seal a 4–2 victory over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee end Arbroath run in six-goal thriller |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62431314 |access-date=2022-08-13}}</ref> After injuries to teammates, Mulligan would perform well at right-back in the latter half of the season for the ''Dark Blues'' and was a key contributor in Dundee winning the [[Scottish Championship]] at season's end.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>

On 3 June 2023, Dundee announced that Mulligan had signed a new two-year contract, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-03 |title=Mulligan commits to the Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/mulligan-commits-to-the-dee/ |access-date=2023-06-03 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> In October, it was announced Mulligan needed surgery on a [[hernia]] which would keep him out for several weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2023-10-27 |title=Dundee receive good and bad injury news ahead of Livingston clash as one star set for 'three or four weeks' out |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4794608/dundee-fc-team-news-good-bad-injury-reports-livingston/ |access-date=2023-10-28 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> Mulligan would return in December and would come in and out of the team until being injured again with a hamstring tear in March 2024 which would keep him out for a month or so.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robertson |first=Neil |date=2024-03-16 |title=Tony Docherty reveals Josh Mulligan injury timeline and Owen Beck fitness hope for Dundee v Rangers clash |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4923139/tony-docherty-reveals-josh-mulligan-injury-timeline-and-owen-beck-fitness-chances-for-dundee-v-rangers-clash/ |access-date=2024-03-16 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Mulligan left Dundee under freedom of contract after the 2024–25 season was completed, and the club subsequently agreed a compensation package with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c2lpqpkw7gyo |title=Hibs & Dundee agree Mulligan compensation |website=BBC Sport |date=13 November 2025 |accessdate=13 November 2025}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
Mulligan signed a four-year contract with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in June 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c80p7dkg3v0o |title=Hibernian: Josh Mulligan joins after Dundee exit |website=BBC Sport |date=27 June 2025 |accessdate=27 June 2025}}</ref> On 24 July 2025, Mulligan made his first competitive appearance for the ''Hibees'' in [[Denmark]] away to [[FC Midtjylland]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Midtjylland vs Hibernian: Live coverage, stats and match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3vd41z0l5pt |access-date=2025-07-24 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 17 August, Mulligan scored his first Hibernian goal in a [[Scottish League Cup]] victory away to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Livingston vs Hibernian: Premier Sports Cup radio commentary, updates & report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cy85rjg2k9et |access-date=2025-08-17 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International==
Mulligan was selected for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad in May 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61507036 |title=Rangers' Alex Lowry one of five new call-ups by Scotland Under-21s |website=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2022 |access-date=19 May 2022}}</ref> He would make his international debut as a substitute in a goalless draw against [[Belgium national under-21 football team|Belgium]] in Group I of the [[2023 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Scotland U21s hold leaders Belgium to 0-0 draw |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61698438 |access-date=2022-06-05}}</ref> Five days later, he would make his first international start away to [[Denmark national under-21 football team|Denmark]], and played the full 90 minutes in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Denmark U21 v Scotland U21 |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61765064 |access-date=2022-06-10}}</ref> In September 2022, Mulligan would score his first international goal in an away friendly against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lorimer |first=Scott |title=Dundee teen Josh Mulligan stars in Scotland under-21 win - but injury concern hangs over St Johnstone's Adam Montgomery |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/3720523/dundee-st-johnstone-josh-mulligan-adam-montgomery-star-scotland-under-21/ |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=The Courier |date=22 September 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In October 2025, Mulligan received his first [[Scotland national football team]] call-up in advance of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group C|2026 FIFA World Cup qualifier]] at home to [[Belarus national football team|Belarus]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coyle |first=Andy |date=2025-10-11 |title=Barron and Mulligan drafted into Scotland squad to face Belarus |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/connor-barron-and-josh-mulligan-called-into-scotland-squad-ahead-of-belarus-world-cup-qualifier |access-date=2025-10-13 |website=STV News |language=en-GB}}</ref> He was an unused substitute in the 2–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scotland v Belarus LIVE - FIFA World Cup qualifying - TV, radio, clips, team news, updates, stats, report & reaction |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cy8537g4vvyt |access-date=2025-10-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Dylan Tait''' (born 1 October 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club  club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

Tait started his career with [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], having first signed a senior contract in 2019.<ref name="profile"/> Hibernian signed him in August 2021 then loaned him back to Raith as part of the deal. He has since had loan spells with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] and [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], with him permanently joining the latter in June 2024.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-06-14 |title=DYLAN TAIT RETURNS! - Falkirk Football Club |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/06/14/dylan-tait-returns/ |access-date=2024-06-15 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Club career ==
=== Raith Rovers ===
Tait made his debut for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on the final matchday of the 2018–19 [[Scottish League One|League One]] campaign, coming on as a late substitute in a 1–1 draw with [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]]. Tait made a further 13 appearances in the [[2019–20 Raith Rovers F.C. season|2019–20 season]], scoring 3 goals as Raith Rovers were promoted to the [[Scottish Championship]]. Tait started as Raith Rovers began their [[2020–21 Raith Rovers F.C. season|2020–21]] Championship season with a 3–0 win over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] providing the assist for his side's second goal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rovers Return With Comfortable Win|url=https://www.raithrovers.net/45206/raith-rovers-3-0-arbroath.htm|accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref>

===Hibernian===

[[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] signed Tait in August 2021 for an undisclosed fee, and loaned him back to Raith Rovers until January 2022 as part of the deal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/raith-rovers-star-dylan-tait-signs-for-hibs-3367200 |title=Raith Rovers star Dylan Tait signs for Hibs |first=Paul |last=McCabe |newspaper=Fife Today |date=1 September 2021 |accessdate=1 September 2021}}</ref> On 20 January 2022, Tait joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on loan for the remainder of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/dylan-taits-delight-at-killie-loan-deal/ |title=Dylan Tait's delight at Killie loan deal |publisher=Kilmarnock FC |date=20 January 2022 |accessdate=20 January 2022}}</ref>

Tait was loaned to [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in September 2022,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/dylan-tait/ | title=Dylan Tait | publisher=Arbroath FC | work=arbroathfc.co.uk | date=1 September 2022 | access-date=4 September 2022}}</ref> and [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in July 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hibs' Tait joins Hamilton on loan |language=en-GB |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c0dpe18rvz9o |date=3 July 2023 |access-date=4 July 2023}}</ref> His loan with Hamilton was ended in January 2024 and he then moved on loan to their [[2023–24 Scottish League One|League One]] title rivals [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], where he won the title. He left Hibernian at the end of the 2023/24 season.

<big>'''Falkirk'''</big>

Tait joined Falkirk on the 14th June 2024 on a permanent undisclosed transfer following the expiry of the loan deal with Hibernian.<ref name=":0" />

'''Callum Wright''' (born 2 May 2000) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership|Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].

Born in [[Merseyside]], Wright began with [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] and [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] before moving to the youth setup of [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in 2015. He then left for [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] in 2018. Wright was loaned out to [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] in the 2021–2022 season, helping them secure promotion to [[EFL League One|League One]] after a successful loan spell. He returned the following season and helped Cheltenham achieve their highest ever finish in the third tier. He then moved permanently to [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] in 2022, but struggled for gametime and signed for Plymouth in January 2023.

==Early and personal life==
Wright grew up in [[Huyton]] and attended [[Cardinal Heenan Catholic High School]] in [[West Derby]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/leicester-city-loanee-callum-wright-5814687|title=Callum Wright on growing up on same estate as Steven Gerrard|first=Jon|last=Palmer|date=20 August 2021|website=[[Gloucestershire Live]]}}</ref> The Bluebell Estate in Huyton where he was raised was also the home to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s [[Steven Gerrard]] and [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] striker [[David Nugent]].<ref name=nyt>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3301243/2022/05/09/i-dont-know-if-leicester-want-me-to-stay-callum-wright-on-his-future/ |title='I don't know if Leicester want me to stay' – Callum Wright on his future |website=The Athletic |author=Rob Tanner |date=10 May 2022 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> He grew up "idolising" the former, and served as a Liverpool team mascot at the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] semi-final against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2008.<ref name="auto1"/>

===Leicester City===
Wright eventually chose [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], signing a three-and-a-half year contract in February 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leicestermercury.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/who-callum-wright-everything-you-1150350|title=Callum Wright: What you need to know about City's new signing|first=James|last=Sharpe|date=1 February 2018|website=[[Leicester Mercury]]}}</ref> Wright made his Leicester under-23 debut on 2 February 2018 in a 1–0 defeat to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the [[Professional Development League|Premier League 2]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lcfc.com/pages/en/media-article/Wright-Not-Fazed-By-Foxes-Challenge |title=Wright Not Fazed By Foxes Challenge |website=Leicester City |author=Sam Stevens |date=5 February 2018 |access-date=15 February 2025 }}</ref> While at Leicester, he was called up to the [[England national under-18 football team|England U18]] to play in the 2018 [[Panda Cup]] in China.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lcfc.com/pages/en/media-article/Foxes-Set-For-Pre-World-Cup-International-Duty |title=Foxes Set For Pre-World Cup International Duty |website=Leicester City |author=Laura Scigliano |date=24 May 2018 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref>

====2020–21 season: First Cheltenham Town loan====
Wright joined [[EFL League Two]] side [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] on loan in February 2021 for the remainder of the season.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lcfc.com/pages/en/media-article/Callum-Wright-Joins-Cheltenham-Town-On-Loan |title=Callum Wright Joins Cheltenham Town On Loan |website=Leicester City |date=1 February 2021 |access-date=15 February 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55893723|title=Leicester loan Wright to Cheltenham|work=BBC Sport |date=February 2021 }}</ref> He made his Cheltenham Town debut on 16 February 2021, starting in a league match away to [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/february/full-time-walsall-robins/ |title=Report & highlights: Walsall 1-2 Robins |website=www.ctfc.com |author=Murry Toms |date=16 February 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> The match finished 2–1 to Cheltenham with Wright scoring the winner.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leicestermercury.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/leicester-city-loanee-praised-not-5014681 |title=Leicester City loanee praised for not playing like a 'crisp packet' as he marks debut with goal |author=Jordan Blackwell |date=17 February 2021 |website=Leicester Mercury |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> Manager [[Michael Duff (footballer)|Michael Duff]] praised Wright for not looking "like a crisp packet, floating around and getting knocked over."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/midfielder-out-season-key-man-5011716 |title=Midfielder out for season, but key man due back in a fortnight - Cheltenham Town boss Michael Duff after the 2-1 win at Walsall |website=Gloucestershire Live |author=Jon Palmer |date=16 February 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref>  On the final matchday on 8 May, Wright scored in a 4–1 win against [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]] to secure the League Two title.<ref name=chmp>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/may/full-time-the-town-are-champions/|title=Report & highlights: The Town are Champions|website=www.ctfc.com |author=John Townley |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509085554/https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/may/full-time-the-town-are-champions/ |archive-date=9 May 2021}}</ref> He finished the season 17 appearances with four goals in his debut campaign with Cheltenham.<ref name=bbc>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58104239|title=Cheltenham sign Perry and Wright on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=5 August 2021 }}</ref> His goal on 2 April 2021, a volley in a 4–0 win over his former club Tranmere Rovers won Cheltenham's Goal of the Season.<ref name="auto1" />

====2021–22 season: Second Cheltenham Town loan====
In August 2021 he returned to Cheltenham Town for a season-long second loan spell, who were now in [[EFL League One|League One]].<ref name=bbc /> His contract for Leicester was due to expire in the summer of 2021 but he activated a one-year extension when rejoining Cheltenham.<ref name=nyt /> His first match of the season came on 10 August in a 2–0 win over [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] in the [[EFL Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/august/full-time-bristol-rovers-town/ |title=Report & highlights: Bristol Rovers 0-2 Town |website=www.ctfc.com |author=Murry Toms |date=10 August 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> His league debut came on 14 August in a 3–1 defeat at home to [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/august/report-town-1-3-wycombe-wanderers/ |title=Report & highlights: Town 1-3 Wycombe Wanderers |website=www.ctfc.com |author=Christian Parry |date=14 August 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> He scored his first goal on 17 August against [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]], the equaliser in a match that eventually finished in a 2–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/august/full-time-town-ipswich-town/ |title=
Report & highlights: Robins 2-1 Ipswich Town |website=www.ctfc.com |author=Murry Toms |date=17 August 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> After the match, manager Michael Duff compared Wright's ability to impact games to [[Frank Lampard]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cheltenham-town-boss-michael-duff-5800113 |title="Hopefully we'll have a few more of these days" - Cheltenham Town boss Michael Duff after the 2-1 win over Ipswich Town |website=Gloucestershire Live |author=Jon Palmer |date=17 August 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> After one goal and 3 assists in 6 appearances in August, he won Cheltenham's Player of the Month.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/september/callum-wright-chosen-as-autovillage-player-of-the-month-for-august/ |title=Callum Wright chosen as Autovillage Player of the Month |website=www.ctfc.com |author=Luke Saunders |date=6 September 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> Wright also won August Goal of the Month for a goal he scored on 27 August in a 1–1 draw to [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/burton-albion-v-cheltenham-town-5839105 |title=Burton Albion v Cheltenham Town RECAP: Robins pegged back by Brewers after Callum Wright strike |website=Gloucestershire Live |author=Jon Palmer |date=28 August 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/september/callum-wright-wins-august-goal-of-the-month-award/ |title=Callum Wright wins August Goal of the Month award |website=www.ctfc.com |author=Luke Saunders |date=28 September 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref>

However, it was revealed in September that Wright had sustained a [[Fibular collateral ligament|lateral ligament injury]] and could be out for 6 months.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/leicester-city-loan-star-callum-5950038 |title=Leicester City loan star Callum Wright sidelined for six months |website=Gloucestershire Live |author=Jon Palmer |date=21 September 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> He made his return 2 months later on 23 November in a 2–0 victory against [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]], coming on as a substitute for [[Alfie May]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2021/november/report-gillingham-robins/ |title=Report & highlights: Gillingham 0-2 Robins |website=www.ctfc.com |author=Richard Joyce |date=23 November 2021 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref> His goal on 8 January in a 1–1 draw against Burton, described as a "stunning volley", won January's Goal of the Month.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2022/january/report-robins-1-1-burton-albion/ |title=Report & highlights: Robins 1-1 Burton Albion |website=www.ctfc.com |author=George Bennett |date=8 January 2022 |access-date=16 February 2025 }}</ref><ref name=potm>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2022/february/callum-wright-chosen-as-january-autovillage-player-of-the-month/ |title=

When the window opened, I knew it could happen. I said to my agent and my family: 'I just need to get it done. I want to go there and become one of them.'"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/callum-wright-first-interview |title=Callum Wright {{!}} First Interview |website=Plymouth Argyle |date=4 January 2023 |access-date=17 February 2025 }}</ref>

He started a full debut on 7 January in a goalless draw to [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/steven-schumacher-callum-wright-how-8006591 |title=Steven Schumacher on Callum Wright and how he differs from Morgan Whittaker |website=Plymouth Live |author=Chris Errington |date=8 January 2023 |access-date=17 February 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/report-bolton-wanderers-0-argyle-0 |title=REPORT {{!}} BOLTON WANDERERS 0 ARGYLE 0 |website=Plymouth Argyle |date=7 January 2023 |access-date=17 February 2025 }}</ref>  Wright scored his first goal in his [[Home Park|home]] debut against his former club Cheltenham in a 4–2 victory on 21 January.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/plymouth-argyle-keep-up-ferocious-8054687 |title=Plymouth Argyle keep up ferocious pace at top of League One by beating Cheltenham Town |website=Plymouth Live |author=Chris Errington |date=21 January 2023 |access-date=17 February 2025 }}</ref> Wright finished the season with 20 league appearances for Plymouth, 23 in all competitions, and four goals.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/player/214 |title=Callum Wright |website=Plymouth Argyle |access-date=17 February 2025 }}</ref>

====2023–24 season====
Wright started Plymouth's [[EFL Championship|Championship]] season opener on 5 August 2023 in a 3–1 victory against [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/report-argyle-3-huddersfield-town-1 |title=REPORT {{!}} ARGYLE 3 HUDDERSFIELD TOWN 1 |website=Plymouth Argyle |date=5 August 2023 |access-date=19 February 2025 }}</ref> He suffered a knee ligament injury in a 4–1 defeat to [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] on 19 September 2023, and it was reported he could miss up to seven weeks despite not needing surgery.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/plymouth-argyle-dealt-callum-wright-8786847 |title=Plymouth Argyle dealt Callum Wright knee ligament injury blow |website=Plymouth Live |author=Chris Errington |date=28 September 2023 |access-date=18 February 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66949983 |title=Callum Wright: Plymouth Argyle midfielder suffers knee ligament injury |website=BBC Sport |date=28 September 2023 |access-date=18 February 2025 }}</ref> He made his return in a 3–3 draw against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] on 4 November, and made his first start on 9 December in a 4–0 defeat to former club Leicester.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/callum-wright-plymouth-argyle-injury-8967948 |title=Callum Wright out to make up for lost time with Plymouth Argyle after injury |website=Plymouth Live |author=Chris Errington |date=12 December 2023 |access-date=17 February 2025 }}</ref> After manager [[Steven Schumacher]] left for [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] in December, [[Ian Foster (footballer)|Ian Foster]] was appointed to replace him.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67886504 |title=Ian Foster: Plymouth Argyle appoint former England Under-20 boss as head coach |website=BBC Sport |date=5 January 2024 |access-date=19 February 2025 }}</ref> Under Foster, Wright fell out of favour,  playing one league match before Foster was sacked.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://footballleagueworld.co.uk/plymouth-argyle-callum-wright-wayne-rooney/ |title=Plymouth Argyle flop could have Home Park u-turn under Wayne Rooney: View |website=Football League World |author=Adam Le Roux |date=30 July 2024 |access-date=19 February 2025 }}</ref> Wright finished the season with eight starts in 21 league appearances without scoring.<ref name=scwy />

====2024–25 season====
Wright came on as a substitute for [[Mustapha Bundu]] against [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] on 11 August 2024, a match which finished in a 4–0 loss.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/report-sheffield-wednesday-4-0-argyle |title=Report {{!}} Sheffield Wednesday 4-0 Argyle |website=Plymouth Argyle |date=11 August 2024 |access-date=19 February 2025 }}</ref> Wright faced a red card for what new manager [[Wayne Rooney]] called "a stupid tackle" on [[Joel Latibeaudiere]] in a 4–0 defeat to [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] on 26 December 2024 and was suspended for three matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/callum-wright-plymouth-wayne-rooney-9821117 |title=Callum Wright ban leaves injury-hit Plymouth Argyle even more depleted |website=Plymouth Live |author=Chris Errington |date=27 December 2024 |access-date=18 February 2025 }}</ref>  Under new manager [[Miron Muslić]], Wright saw more gametime after having limited playing time under Rooney.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/muslic-plymouth-argyle-callum-wright-9941762 |title=Miron Muslic fixing the Plymouth Argyle puzzle over Callum Wright |website=Plymouth Live |author=Chris Errington |date=13 February 2025 |access-date=18 February 2025 }}</ref> In the fourth round of the FA Cup, Plymouth drew Liverpool, the club Wright supports.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theleaguepaper.com/features/434229/reds-tie-couldnt-be-more-wright-for-me/ |title=Plymouth Argyle vs Liverpool: 'Reds tie couldn't be more right for me', says Callum Wright |website=The Football League Paper |author=Chris Dunlavy |date=9 February 2025 |access-date=19 February 2025 }}</ref> Wright started the match, which Plymouth won 1–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2025/feb/09/plymouth-argyle-v-liverpool-fa-cup-live |title=Plymouth Argyle 1-0 Liverpool: FA Cup – as it happened |website=The Guardian |author=Michael Butler |date=9 February 2025 |access-date=19 February 2025 }}</ref> Plymouth owner Simon Hallett praised Wright for "playing like a man possessed", and Wright swapped shirts with Liverpool player [[Luis Díaz (footballer, born 1997)|Luis Díaz]] after the match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/sport/football/simon-hallett-praises-miron-muslic-9934939 |title=Simon Hallett praises Miron Muslic for 'very positive' Plymouth Argyle impact |website=Plymouth Live |author=Chris Errington |date=11 February 2025 |access-date=18 February 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2025/02/greatest-shirt-swap-boyhood-reds-dream-plymouth-players-on-liverpool-win/ |title="Greatest" shirt swap & boyhood Reds' dream – Plymouth players on Liverpool win |website=www.thisisanfield.com |author=Joanna Durkan |date=10 February 2025 |access-date=18 February 2025 }}</ref>

====Wigan Athletic (loan)====
On 4 July 2025, Wright joined League One side [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2025/july/04/latics-sign-callum-wright-on-loan--/|title=Latics sign Callum Wright on loan!|website=wiganathletic.com|date=4 July 2025|accessdate=4 July 2025}}</ref>

He was released by Plymouth at the end of the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c99lnjkm4nmo|title=Brendan Galloway among nine released by Plymouth Argyle|date=7 May 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Hibernian===

'''Mitchy-Yorham Ntelo Mbala''' (born 4 May 2001) is a Belgian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref name="soccerway">{{Soccerway|660620}}</ref>

==Club career==
Ntelo is a youth academy graduate of [[Standard Liège]]. On 23 July 2021, club announced that three players including Ntelo will join Dutch side [[MVV Maastricht]] on a season long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=3 JONGE ROUCHES OP UITLEENBASIS NAAR MVV MAASTRICHT|url=https://standard.be/nl/news/3-jonge-rouches-op-uitleenbasis-naar-mvv-maastricht|date=23 July 2021|access-date=24 August 2021}}</ref> He made his professional debut on 9 August 2021 in a 1–0 league win against [[Jong FC Utrecht|Jong Utrecht]]. On 20 August, he scored his first [[Hat-trick|three goals]] in professional career in a 3–2 win against [[Helmond Sport]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ntelo offre la victoire au MVV Maastricht avec un triplé|url=https://www.walfoot.be/news/2021-08-21/ntelo-offre-la-victoire-au-mvv-maastricht-avec-un-triple|date=21 August 2021|access-date=24 August 2021}}</ref>

In August 2022, Ntelo joined [[R. Charleroi S.C.|Charleroi]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Le jeune attaquant Mitchy Ntelo quitte le Standard et rejoint le Sporting de Charleroi|url=https://www.lesoir.be/457859/article/2022-08-04/le-jeune-attaquant-mitchy-ntelo-quitte-le-standard-et-rejoint-le-sporting-de|date=4 August 2022|access-date=4 August 2022}}</ref> On 30 January 2024, he joined Bulgarian club [[PFC Lokomotiv Plovdiv|Lokomotiv Plovdiv]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ЛОКОМОТИВ ПОДПИСА ДОГОВОР С МИЧИ НТЕЛО|url=https://lokomotivpd.com/lokomotiv-podpisa-dogovor-s-michi-ntelo/|language=bg|date=30 January 2024|access-date=31 January 2024}}</ref>

On 27 August 2024, Ntelo joined [[Yverdon-Sport FC|Yverdon]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.yverdonsport.ch/mitchy-ntelo-nouvel-attaquant-a-ys/|title=MITCHY NTELO, NOUVEL ATTAQUANT A YS|trans-title=MITCHY NTELO, NEW ATTACKER AT YS!|language=fr|website=Yverdon-Sport FC|date=27 August 2024}}</ref>

On 8 August 2026, Ntelo joined [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Aberdeen F.C.|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cd0xy9dlgnjo |title=Aberdeen buy versatile Belgian forward Ntelo |date=8 August 2026 |access-date=9 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Ntelo is a former Belgian youth international.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mitchy-Yorham Ntelo Mbala|url=https://www.rbfa.be/en/international/10419/career|access-date=24 August 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in Belgium, Ntelo is of [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] origin.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ntelo, un jeune attaquant belgo-congolais, préfère le Standard à l'Antwerp et Francfort|url=https://www.lesoir.be/281220/article/2020-02-19/ntelo-un-jeune-attaquant-belgo-congolais-prefere-le-standard-lantwerp-et|date=19 February 2020|access-date=24 August 2021}}</ref>

'''Thibault Klidjé''' (born 10 July 2001) is a Togolese-French<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.africatopsports.com/2020/02/21/thibault-klidje-un-talent-togolais-aux-girondins-de-bordeaux/|title=Thibault Klidje : un talent togolais aux Girondins de Bordeaux|date=February 21, 2020}}</ref> professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], and the [[Togo national football team|Togo national team]]. He has previously played for [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] and [[FC Luzern|Luzern]].

==Career==
Klidjé began his career with the Togolese clubs [[Espoir Tsevie]], and [[Gomido FC|Gomido]] before signing with the reserves of French club [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] on 21 February 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.africatopsports.com/2020/02/21/thibault-klidje-un-talent-togolais-aux-girondins-de-bordeaux/|title=Thibault Klidje : un talent togolais aux Girondins de Bordeaux|date=February 21, 2020}}</ref>

On 31 August 2022, Klidjé signed for [[Swiss Super League]] club [[FC Luzern|Luzern]] on a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 August 2022 |title=Blessé, Thibault Klidjè rejoint la Suisse |url=https://www.republicoftogo.com/toutes-les-rubriques/sport/blesse-thibault-klidje-rejoint-la-suisse |access-date=28 September 2022 |website=Republicoftogo.com |language=fr}}</ref>

On 13 July 2025 Klidjé signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on a three year contract, becoming their record signing.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 July 2025|title= THIBAULT KLIDJÉ JOINS HIBS!|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2025/july/13/thibault-klidj--joins-hibs-/|access-date=13 July 2025|website=hibernianfc.co.uk|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c5ykwwk9984o |title=Hibs break transfer record for Togo striker Klidje |website=BBC Sport |date=13 July 2025 |accessdate=13 July 2025}}</ref> Klidjé played mainly as a substitute in the first part of the 2025–26 season, scoring four goals in 26 appearances, and was loaned to [[Danish Superliga]] club [[Randers FC|Randers]] on 2 February 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cvgxy9x5535o  |title=Hibs buy Felix Passlack and Ante Suto as Munashe Garananga joins on loan  |website=BBC Sport |date=2 February 2026 |accessdate=3 February 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
He debuted with the [[Togo national football team|Togo national team]] on 9 October 2021 in a 1–1 [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF)|World Cup qualifier]] draw against [[Congo national football team|Congo]]. In 2018, he represented the [[Togo national under-20 football team|Togo national U20 team]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Togo - Kongo 1-1 (0-1). 3. kolejka el. MŚ - Afryka|url=https://sport.interia.pl/fifa-ms/news-togo-kongo-1-1-0-1-3-kolejka-el-ms-afryka,nId,5571786|date=9 October 2021|access-date=9 October 2021}}</ref>

'''Iurie Iovu''' (born 6 July 2002) is a Moldovan professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and the [[Moldova national football team|Moldova national team]].

==Club career==
He was raised in the system of [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] and began receiving call-ups to their senior squad in early 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://moldfootball.com/ro/news/-jurijj-jjovu-v-shotlandii-ochen-fizicheskijj-stil-igry-a-fizika-ehto-moja-sil-naja-storona|title=Iurie Iovu: "În Scoția domină un stil de joc bazat pe forța fizică, iar acesta este punctul meu forte"|trans-title=Iurie Iovu: "In Scotland, a style of play based on physical strength dominates, and this is my strong point"|language=ro|publisher=Moldfootball.com|date=22 June 2025|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref> He remained on the bench on all those occasions.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/01/16/italy/serie-a/as-roma/cagliari-calcio/3558453/|title=Roma v Cagliari game report|date=16 January 2022|access-date=31 August 2022}}</ref>

On 31 August 2022, Iovu signed a two-year contract with [[Serie B]] club [[Venezia F.C.|Venezia]] and was immediately loaned out to [[NK Istra 1961|Istra 1961]] in Croatia, with an obligation to buy.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Venezia|url=https://www.veneziafc.it/news/iurie-iovu-al-venezia-fc|title=IURIE IOVU AL VENEZIA FC|date=31 August 2022|access-date=31 August 2022|language=it}}</ref>

In 2025, he signed for Scottish side [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], becoming the first [[Moldova]]n player to sign for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5263745/dundee-united-iurie-iovu-jim-goodwin-transfer/|title=Dundee United seal Iurie Iovu deal as Jim Goodwin hails ‘fearless’ stopper|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]]|date=10 June 2025|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
He made his debut for [[Moldova national football team]] on 15 November 2021 in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group F|World Cup qualifier]] against [[Austria national football team|Austria]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5413528/iurie-iovu-dundee-united-scottish-cup-history/|title=Iurie Iovu recalls cup agony he can’t let repeat itself with Dundee United|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]]|date=17 January 2026|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[FIFA]]|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/worldcup/qatar2022/qualifiers/uefa/match-center/400155667|title=Austria v Moldova game report|date=15 November 2021|accessdate=30 November 2021}}</ref>

'''Bert Johan Esselink''' (born 16 August 1999) is a Dutch professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

==Club career==

===Early career===
Born in [['s-Heerenberg]], Esselink started his career in the youth academy of Dutch club [[De Graafschap]], before joining his first senior club [[PAEEK]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.voetbalzone.nl/doc.asp?uid=399190|title='Ik werd weggestuurd bij Jong De Graafschap en speel nu bij zo'n grote club'|publisher=voetbalzone.nl}}</ref>

===PAEEK===
On 15 July 2020, it was officially announced that Esselink signed for [[PAEEK]] until June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sigmalive.com/sports/football/cyprus/b-league/640413/ypegrapse-o-bert-esselink-video|title=Υπέγραψε ο Bert Esselink (Video) | News}}</ref>

He made his professional debut on 12 September 2020 in a [[Cypriot Second Division]] game against [[Achyronas Liopetriou]].

On 27 June 2021, PAEEK announced the renewal of Esselink's contract until 31 May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://paeekfc.com/transfernews/bertesselink|title=Ανανέωση συμβολάιου με Bert Esselink}}</ref>

===APOEL===

On 9 January 2022, it was officially announced that Esselink signed for [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] until 2024 after his release clause was exercised.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.apoelfc.com.cy/article/symfonia-meteggrafis-me-paeek-gia-bert-esselink|title = Συμφωνία μετεγγραφής με ΠΑΕΕΚ για Bert Esselink}}</ref>

====Loan to Olympiakos Nicosia====

On 26 August 2022, he was loaned for a year to [[Olympiakos Nicosia]].

===Stal Mielec===
On 3 July 2023, Esselink signed a one-year contract with Polish [[Ekstraklasa]] side [[Stal Mielec]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bert Esselink a member of PGE FKS Stala Mielec |url=https://stalmielec.com/en/bert-esselink-zawodnikiem-pge-fks-stali-mielec-2/ |publisher=[[Stal Mielec]] |language=pl |date=3 July 2023}}</ref> On 9 April 2024, his deal was extended for another season after meeting the requirements listed in his contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kontrakt Berta Esselinka przedłużony na kolejny sezon |url=https://stalmielec.com/kontrakt-berta-esselinka-przedluzony-na-kolejny-sezon/ |publisher=asd |access-date=9 April 2024 |language=pl |date=9 April 2024}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
In June 2025, Esselink signed a two-year contract with Scottish Premiership club Dundee United.
