'''Ross James Graham''' (born 23 February 2001) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central defender]] for  {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. He has also played for [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] and [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on loan before making his Premiership debut for Dundee United in 2022.

==Early life==
Graham was born in [[Blairgowrie and Rattray|Blairgowrie]], Perth and Kinross,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hart |first1=Ross |title=Pars: Centre back Graham arrives |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/19415046.dunfermline-ross-graham-joins-loan-dundee-united/ |access-date=30 January 2022 |work=Dunfermline Press |date=2 July 2021}}</ref> where he attended Newhill Primary School. He began playing football at Blairgowrie & Rattray Community F.C. From 2013 he attended [[St John's Roman Catholic High School]] in Dundee where he was part of the [[Scottish Football Association]] (SFA) Performance School Programme.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Menzies |first1=Johnathon |title=Local lads selected for football development programme |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/local-news/local-lads-selected-football-development-2721790 |access-date=30 January 2022 |work=Daily Record |date=15 August 2013}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ross Graham is the son of former footballer who shares his son's name as James Ross Graham his dad played football as a striker for Scottish clubs such as [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]], [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] and [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]].{{cn|date=November 2024}}

==Career==
===Club===
As well as progressing through the SFA programme, Graham joined the [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] Academy in 2012 from Dundee West. He was initially an attacking [[midfielder]] before being converted to a [[central defender]]. After impressing for the club's under-17 team, he signed a professional contract in July 2018. Early in the [[2018–19 Dundee United F.C. season|2018–19 season]], he made two first team appearances as youthful United teams faced [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone Colts]] and [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ross Graham Player Profile |url=https://www.arabarchive.co.uk/player.php?id=1937 |access-date=30 January 2022 |work=Arab Archive}}</ref>

In September 2019, Graham signed a new three-year contract with Dundee United.<ref>{{cite news |title=Academy graduate Ross Graham extends contract |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6209/ACADEMY-GRADUATE-ROSS-GRAHAM-EXTENDS-CONTRACT.html |access-date=30 January 2022 |publisher=Dundee United F.C. |date=6 September 2019}}</ref> After being an unused substitute for the first team on several occasions, he joined [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] on loan in January 2020 for the rest of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ross Graham joins Elgin City on loan |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6395/ROSS-GRAHAM-JOINS-ELGIN-CITY-ON-LOAN.html |access-date=30 January 2022 |publisher=Dundee United F.C. |date=18 January 2020}}</ref> He made eight appearances for Elgin before the season was cut short due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref name="PandJ">{{cite news |last1=Skinner |first1=Andy |title=Ross Graham wants to use spell on loan at Cove Rangers from Dundee United to 'learn men's game' |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/cove-rangers/2572846/ross-graham-wants-to-use-spell-on-loan-at-cove-rangers-from-dundee-united-to-learn-mens-game/ |access-date=30 January 2022 |work=The Press and Journal |date=16 October 2020 |location=Aberdeen}}</ref>

Graham began the 2020–21 season training with Dundee United's first team squad before going on loan again, joining [[Scottish League One|League One]] club [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] in October for the rest of the season.<ref name="PandJ" /> He made 23 appearances for Cove in all competitions. In July 2021 he signed a further three-year contract extension with Dundee United and then immediately departed on another season's loan, with [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Woodger |first1=Calum |title=Ross Graham signs new deal at Dundee United and immediately joins Dunfermline on season-long loan |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2349616/ross-graham-signs-new-deal-at-dundee-united-and-immediately-joins-dunfermline-on-season-long-loan/ |access-date=30 January 2022 |work=The Courier |date=1 July 2021 |location=Dundee}}</ref>

At Dunfermline, Graham played in the first seven matches of the season, but after only one further appearance and a change of manager at the club, his loan was cut short in January 2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hart |first1=Ross |title=McCann pens new deal as defender departs |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/news/19823351.dunfermline-lewis-mccann-signs-deal-ross-graham-departs/ |access-date=30 January 2022 |work=Dunfermline Press |date=4 January 2022}}</ref> Returning to Dundee United, he made his league debut for the club as a substitute against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in a 1–0 [[Scottish Premiership]] defeat at [[Celtic Park]] on 29 January 2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Ewan |title=Tam Courts hails Dundee United young guns as he rues late heartbreak at Celtic Park |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2957988/tam-courts-hails-dundee-united-young-guns-at-celtic-park/ |access-date=30 January 2022 |work=The Courier |date=29 January 2022 |location=Dundee}}</ref>

===International===
Graham played three times for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] team during 2022, scoring one goal.<ref>{{SFA Profile|id=267561|name=Ross Graham}}</ref>

Ivezić made his debut for [[Serbia national football team|Serbia national team]] on 25 January 2023 in a friendly match against USA. '''Miguel Changa Chaiwa''' (born 7 June 2004) is a Zambian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership ]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and the [[Zambia national football team|Zambia national team]].

==Club career==

A youth product of Shamuel Academy, Chaiwa joined the Zambian club Atletico Lusaka on loan in 2022. 

===Young Boys===
He transferred to the Swiss club [[BSC Young Boys|Young Boys]] on 14 June 2022, signing a 4-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zambianfootball.co.zm/miguel-chaiwa-joins-bsc-young-boys/|title=Miguel Chaiwa joins BSC Young Boys|date=June 14, 2022}}</ref> On 14 February 2024, Chaiwa moved on loan to [[FC Schaffhausen|Schaffhausen]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=FC Schaffhausen|url=https://www.fcschaffhausen.ch/2024/02/14/riesentalent-chaiwa-zum-fcs/|title=Riesentalent Chaiwa zum FCS|trans-title=Huge talent Chaiwa to FCS|date=14 February 2024|access-date=14 February 2024|language=de}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
Chaiwa moved to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in August 2025 for an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cvgnvg15pwyo |title=Hibs fend off 'lot of interest' to sign Young Boys midfielder Chaiwa |website=BBC Sport |date=8 August 2025 |accessdate=8 August 2025}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on this third appearance, on 28 August 2025, during a UEFA Conference League playoff against Legia Warszawa.

==International career==
Chaiwa represented the [[Zambia national under-17 football team|Zambia U17]]s in 2019 and 2020. He debuted for the senior [[Zambia national football team|Zambia national team]] in a friendly 3–1 loss to [[Iraq national football team|Iraq]] on 20 March 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lusakatimes.com/2022/03/20/chaiwa-reflects-on-chipolopolo-debut/|title=Zambia : Chaiwa Reflects on Chipolopolo Debut|date=March 20, 2022}}</ref>

On 10 December 2025, Chaiwa was called up to the Zambia squad for the [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cafonline.com/afcon2025/news/daka-leads-zambia-s-final-totalenergies-caf-afcon-squad-as-newcomers-earn-surprise-call-ups/|title=Daka leads Zambia’s final TotalEnergies CAF AFCON squad as newcomers earn surprise call-ups|publisher=[[Confederation of African Football]]|date=11 December 2025|access-date=12 December 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Chaiwa's father, [[Changa Chaiwa|Changa]] was also a professional footballer in Zambia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zambiantelegraph.com/sport/miguel-chaiwa-back-at-atletico-lusaka-from-shamuel/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717220647/https://zambiantelegraph.com/sport/miguel-chaiwa-back-at-atletico-lusaka-from-shamuel/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=17 July 2022|title=Miguel Chaiwa back at Atletico Lusaka from Shamuel|date=February 14, 2022}}</ref>

'''Azeem Kerr Abdulai''' (born 9 December 2002) is a [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]. Born in Scotland, he represents the [[Sierra Leone national football team|Sierra Leone national team]].

==Career==

Abdulai was a youth at Celtic and Leicester before starting his senior career with [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/azeem-abdulai-being-same-pitch-neymar-embracing-swansea-way|title=Azeem Abdulai | From being on the same pitch as Neymar to embracing the Swansea Way | Swansea|website=www.swanseacity.com}}</ref> On 9 August 2022, Abdulai debuted for Swansea during an EFL Cup loss to [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]].<ref>{{Soccerway|756424}}</ref>

He scored his first goal for Swansea on 13 August 2024 in an [[EFL Cup]] tie against [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]].<ref>{{cite news 
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5ydxz9nz15t
|title=Swansea 3-1 Gillingham
|publisher=[[BBC]] 
|date=13 August 2024|access-date=17 August 2024}}</ref>

===Leyton Orient===
On 22 January 2025, Abdulai signed for [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] on a two-and-a-half year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.leytonorient.com/news/2025/january/22/orient-complete-permanent-signing-of-azeem-abdulai/|title=Orient complete permanent signing of Azeem Abdulai|website=www.leytonorient.com|date=22 January 2025|accessdate=23 January 2025}}</ref> On 28 January, in his second appearance for the club, he scored a first career hat-trick in a 6–2 thrashing of [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ckg03zyjxyjt|title=Exeter City 2–6 Leyton Orient: Azeem Abdulai hits hat-trick|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 January 2025|accessdate=29 January 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Abdulai was born in Scotland to a Sierra Leonean father and Scottish mother. He represented Scotland at under-21 international level, making his debut in March 2023.<ref name="auto"/> Abdulai switched his international status to Sierra Leone in 2026,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibsobserver.co.uk/news/26561443.hibs-midfielder-lands-first-senior-international-call-up/  |title=Hibs midfielder lands first senior international call-up |website=Hibs Observer |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=18 September 2026 |accessdate=25 September 2026}}</ref> and made his full international debut in a 3–2 defeat against Zimbabwe on 24 September.

'''Jack Milne''' (born 10 February 2003) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/jack-milne/742733/|title=Scotland - J. Milne - Profile with news, career statistics and history - Soccerway|website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref> He has also played for [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] and [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] on loan. Originally a central midfielder, then a holding midfielder, Milne was successfully converted into a central defender.

==Career==
Born in [[Aberdeen]], Milne attended the SFA Performance School at [[Hazlehead Academy]] and the Aberdeen Youth Academy at Under 12s aged 11 years old, and was rewarded with a full time contract in the summer of 2020. He played one year at Under 18s, before being loaned out to [[Highland Football League|Highland League]] side Brechin City for the first half of the 2021–22 campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brechincity.com/bcfc/p/p/315|title=Brechin City Football Club|website=www.brechincity.com}}</ref> He also impressed whilst playing for the Aberdeen B-team in their [[Scottish Challenge Cup|SPFL Trust Trophy]] games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/player/jack-milne/|title=Jack Milne|website=Aberdeen FC}}</ref>

He made his senior debut for Aberdeen in a [[Scottish League Cup]] Group Stage match against [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] on 10 July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/commentary/live-peterhead-v-aberdeen/|title=LIVE: Peterhead v Aberdeen|website=Aberdeen FC}}</ref> He made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut on 1 October 2022, coming on as a second-half substitute in a 4–1 win against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63017808|title = Aberdeen swat away Kilmarnock on McInnes' return|website=BBC Sport | date=October 2022 }}</ref>

On 12 January 2023, Milne joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Milne heads to Kelty on loan |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c6p8nr6z1pxo |date=12 January 2023 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In May 2026, Milne was accused of [[Racism in association football|racism during a game]] towards Livingston striker [[Jeremy Bokila]]; the allegation was "not proven".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cwy2rgw7dxgo|title=Aberdeen's Jack Milne alleged racist abuse towards Jeremy Bokila 'not proven'|date=11 May 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

'''Zachary Albert Sapsford''' (born 16 August 2002) is an Australian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

== Early life ==
Sapsford was born on 16 August 2002 in [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]], Australia, having grown up in the [[List of Sydney suburbs|suburb]] of [[Bondi, New South Wales|Bondi]] in the [[Eastern Suburbs (Sydney)|Eastern Suburbs]]. He is of [[Jewish Australians|Jewish]] descent, and was developed at [[Hakoah Sydney City East FC|Maccabi Hakoah]], a Jewish [[Soccer in Australia|soccer]] club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.australianjewishnews.com/wanderers-sign-jewish-teenager-zac-sapsford/|title=Wanderers sign Jewish teenager Zac Sapsford|publisher=[[Australian Jewish News]]|date=9 June 2022}}</ref>

== Club career ==
In 2022, Sapsford signed for Australian side [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]], where he played alongside former [[Spain national football team|Spain]] international [[Juan Mata]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5265187/who-is-zac-sapsford-dundee-united-transfer/|title=Who is Zac Sapsford? Dundee United’s new derby specialist with Juan Mata secret handshake|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]]|date=11 June 2025|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>
Sapsford made his [[A-League Men]] debut against [[Brisbane Roar FC|Brisbane Roar]] on 22 October 2022 coming off the bench in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ultimatealeague.com/match/?match_id=2545 |title=Western Sydney Wanderers vs Brisbane Roar. Round 3, 2022-23|website=Ultimate A-League|date=22 October 2022}}</ref> He scored his first senior goal for the Wanderers in a  1–0 [[Sydney Derby (A-League Men)|Sydney Derby]] win against Sydney FC on 25 November 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sapsford snatches three Derby points |url=https://wswanderersfc.com.au/news/sapsford-snatches-three-derby-points |publisher=Western Sydney Wanderers |access-date=27 November 2023 |date=25 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sapsford: It's surreal |url=https://wswanderersfc.com.au/news/sapsford-its-surreal |publisher=Western Sydney Wanderers |access-date=27 November 2023 |date=26 November 2023}}</ref>  He was regarded to have established himself as a regular starter<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48691915/sapsford-eyes-socceroos-call-breakout-season-scotland|title=Sapsford eyes Socceroos call-up after breakout season in Scotland|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=6 May 2026|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref> and scored nine goals during his final season while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football360.com.au/zac-sapsford-on-ex-western-sydney-boss-alen-stajcic/|title=Dundee United striker Sapsford pays tribute to ex-Wanderers boss Stajcic for igniting his career: 'He was the coach I needed'|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=Football360|date=28 January 2026|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 10 June 2025, Sapsford signed for Scottish Premiership club Dundee United on a three-year deal for an undisclosed fee. Upon signing for the club, he played in the [[UEFA Conference League]], where he formed an attacking partnership with [[England|English]] footballer [[Max Watters]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united-hero-zac-sapsford-35695920|title=Dundee United hero Zac Sapsford aiming for even bigger European highs than Vienna|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|date=8 August 2025|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Following the 2025 [[Bondi Beach shooting]], an [[Antisemitism in Australia|antisemitic]] [[Terrorism in Australia|terrorist]] attack in [[Bondi Beach|his home]] [[List of Sydney suburbs|suburb]], Sapsford paid tribute to the victims of what became [[Australia]]'s worst terrorist attack in history by wearing a [[black armband]]. His aunt and uncle were in attendance at the [[Hanukkah]] by the Sea event, which was the target of the shooting, surviving the attack without injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football360.com.au/zac-sapsford-bondi-beach-tribute/|title=Aussie striker Zac Sapsford's moving tribute to his community and Bondi victims on Day of National Mourning|first=David|last=Weiner|publisher=[[Football360]]|date=22 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Adam Matthew Mayor''' (born 10 April 2004) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|left-sided wing-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].

==Career==
Born in [[Liverpool]], Mayor was signed to Tranmere rovers at the age of 8 after being spotted playing for his local team Frameline Juniors. After being released Mayor spent time with [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] before joining [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Adam Mayor - Forward - U18s - Morecambe |url=https://www.morecambefc.com/teams/u18s/forward/adam-mayor/ |website=www.morecambefc.com |access-date=18 December 2022}}</ref> He made his first-team debut on 27 August 2022, coming on as an 89th-minute substitute for [[Arthur Gnahoua]] in a 4–0 defeat to [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]] at the [[Globe Arena (football stadium)|Globe Arena]]. Three days later, he played in an [[EFL Trophy]] group stage game with [[Everton F.C. Reserves and Academy|Everton U23]], where he converted his [[penalty kick]] in the 7–6 shoot-out victory following a 3–3 draw.<ref>{{cite news |title=Morecambe vs Everton U21 on 30 Aug 22 - Match Centre - Morecambe |url=https://www.morecambefc.com/matches/fixtures/first-team/202223/august/morecambe-vs-everton-u21-on-30-aug-22/ |access-date=18 December 2022 |work=www.morecambefc.com |date=30 August 2022}}</ref> He scored his first career goal in the competition on 18 October, in a 2–1 defeat at [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]]; Mayor said that "the ball came across and it happened quickly, I think Arthur [Gnahoua] missed the ball and then it just bounced to me perfectly to hit it first time".<ref>{{cite news |title=Mayor hopes to have made an impression |url=https://www.morecambefc.com/news/2022/october/mayor-hopes-to-have-made-an-impression/ |access-date=18 December 2022 |work=www.morecambefc.com |date=18 October 2022 |language=en-gb}}</ref> His first goal in [[EFL League One]] came on 29 October, in a 1–1 draw at [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mayor Made Up Following Late Leveller |url=https://www.morecambefc.com/news/2022/october/mayor-made-up-following-late-leveller/ |access-date=18 December 2022 |work=www.morecambefc.com |date=30 October 2022 |language=en-gb}}</ref>

===Millwall===
On 31 January 2024, Mayor signed for [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] on a long-term contract for an undisclosed fee, mooted to be £300,000, potentially rising to £1 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.millwallfc.co.uk/news/2024/january/31/millwall-announce-adam-mayor-signing/|title=Millwall announce Adam Mayor signing|website=www.millwallfc.co.uk|date=31 January 2024|accessdate=31 January 2024}}</ref>

On 31 January 2025, Mayor returned to [[EFL League Two|League Two]], joining [[Bromley F.C.|Bromley]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/forward-adam-mayor-joins-on-loan/|title=Forward Adam Mayor joins on loan|website=www.bromleyfc.co.uk|date=31 January 2025|accessdate=31 January 2025}}</ref>

'''Kanayochukwu Megwa''' (born 5 March 2004) is an Nigerian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Hibernia}} side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{Soccerway|kanayochukwu-megwa/857307}}</ref>

==Career==

===Hibernian===
Born in London, Megwa spent time on trial with English Championship clubs including [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] and [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Brom]] before signing with Scottish club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in the summer of 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/player/kenayo-megwa|title=Kanayo Megwa|accessdate=17 July 2023|website=Hibernianfc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Ross|last=Pilcher|url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/kanayo-megwa-targets-new-hibs-23184186.amp|website=FootballScotland|accessdate=17 July 2023|title= Kanayo Megwa targets new Hibs deal and first team spot after impressive start to life as a pro |date=22 February 2022}}</ref> He signed a new contract with Hibernian in March 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/kanayo-megwa-signs-new-hibs-26359440.amp|website=Edinburgh Live|accessdate=17 July 2023|title=Kanayo Megwa signs new Hibs deal as starlet makes loan transfer to Kelty Hearts|first=Alan|last=Galindo|date=1 March 2023}}</ref>

Megwa joined [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] of the [[Scottish League One]] on loan for the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/kanayo-megwa-eager-to-keep-improving-as-hibs-kid-raves-about-loan-experience-4082233|title= Kanayo Megwa eager to keep improving as Hibs kid raves about loan experience|first=Patrick|last=McPartlin|date=28 March 2023|website=Edinburgh News}}</ref>  He made his league debut on 4 March 2023 for Kelty Hearts against [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/news/23379667.kelty-hearts-john-potter-delighted-kanayo-megwa/|website=Dunfermelinepress.com|accessdate=17 July 2023|title= Kelty Hearts: John Potter 'delighted' with Kanayo Megwa|date=11 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2023/03/04/scotland/second-division/kelty-hearts/edinburgh-city-fc/3800884/|website=Soccerway|title=KELTY HEARTS VS. EDINBURGH FC 1–2|date=4 March 2023}}</ref>

On his return to Hibernian, Megwa trained with the first-team squad on their pre-season tour of Spain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Johnson praise for Megwa and other Hibs youths|date=9 July 2023|access-date=17 July 2023|website=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c2qdr3v25k3o}}</ref> He made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut on 12 August 2023, as a second-half substitute against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2023/08/13/scotland/premier-league/motherwell-fc/hibernian-football-club/4104363/|website=Soccerway|date=22 August 2023|accessdate=12 August 2023|title=MOTHERWELL VS. HIBERNIAN 2–1}}</ref>

In August 2024, Megwa signed a four-year deal which committed him to Hibs until summer 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-23 |title=Kanayo Megwa signs new four-year Hibs deal |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cvg3rzpwjr5o |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Kanayo Megwa made his European debut in the [[2025–26 UEFA Europa League qualifying|2025-26 Europa League qualifying]]. He came off the bench in both legs of Hibernian's tie with [[FC Midtjylland]] of Denmark, which they lost 3-2 on aggregate.<ref name="sb2526" />

===Airdrieonians (loan)===
In September 2023, he moved on loan to [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c51q1wwl27jo | title=Megwa joins the Hibs loan contingent at Airdrie |website=BBC Sport | date=21 September 2023 | accessdate=21 September 2023}}</ref> The following month he made his league debut for Airdrie against [[Ayr United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/hibs-loanees-debut-bright-spot-31155089.amp|website=Daily Record|accessdate=11 October 2023|title=Hibs loanee's debut was a bright spot on a dull day for Airdrie, admits boss|first=Andy|last=McGilvray|date=11 October 2023 }}</ref>
Hibs recalled Megwa from his loan at Airdrie in January 2024.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-kid-earns-loan-recall-and-has-sights-set-on-first-team-4483693 |title=Hibs kid earns loan recall – and has sights set on first team |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=18 January 2024 |accessdate=18 January 2024 |first=John |last=Greechan}}</ref> After making a few first team appearances for Hibs, he returned on loan to Airdrie a month later.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com//sport/football/hibs/hibs-confirm-loan-transfer-airdrie-kanayo-megwa-4528446 | title=Hibs confirm loan transfer exit as SPFL club hail 'dynamic' star's arrival |first=Ben |last=Banks |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=21 February 2024 |accessdate=22 February 2024}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle (loan)===
Megwa joined Scottish Championship side [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a season long loan in September 2024.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/kanayo-megwa-arrives-on-loan-from-hibs/ | title=Kanayo Megwa arrives on loan from Hibs }}</ref> He made his debut at right back in a 1-0 home victory over [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], wearing shirt number 30. Through the 2024-25 season, Megwa made 30 appearances in all competitions, including starting all four play-off ties the club contested. Megwa registered one assist across all appearances, helping [[Brian Graham (footballer)|Brian Graham]] score in a 1-1 home draw with [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in February 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Partick Thistle vs Airdrieonians: Scottish Championship report & stats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gzgr09k78t |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Megwa returned to his parent club at the conclusion of his loan period  following the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Squad Update – 4th June 2025 |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/squad-update-4th-june-2025/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

==Style of play==
A defender with the potential to be versatile, Megwa played for Hibernian in the [[UEFA Youth League]] at right-back, right-wingback, right-sided centre-back in a back four  and left-sided and right-sided centre-back in a back three formation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/why-the-rapid-rise-of-kanayo-megwa-can-help-solve-positional-riddle-for-hibs-4214609 |website=Edinburugh News|accessdate=17 July 2023|title= Why the rapid rise of Kanayo Megwa can help solve positional riddle for Hibs|first=Patrick|last=McPartlin|date=13 July 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Megwa was born in London and raised in Nigeria to Nigerian parents.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/kanayo-megwa-shares-hibs-first-team-dream-3579393|website=Edinburgh News|accessdate=17 July 2023|title=Kanayo Megwa shares Hibs first-team dream as defender speaks on moving to Scotland, Paul McGinn inspiration, and his football upbringing|first=Patrick|last=McPartlin|date=22 February 2022}}</ref>

'''Gavin Molloy''' (born 19 October 2001) is an Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]].

==Career==
Molloy spent his early career with [[Drogheda United F.C.|Drogheda United]], [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] and [[Shelbourne F.C.|Shelbourne]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/player/11126345/gavin_molloy/|title=Gavin Molloy | Stats | History | Career Details | Images | extratime.com - The Home of Irish Football - Extratime.com|website=www.extratime.com}}</ref> and eventually became the [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the latter team in March 2023.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/we-lost-my-grandad-a-few-weeks-ago-but-he-was-in-my-thoughts-and-i-hope-it-made-the-family-proud/42378796.html|title='We lost my grandad a few weeks ago, but he was in my thoughts – and I hope it made the family proud'|date=10 March 2023|website=Irish Independent}}</ref> He signed a new contract with Shelbourne in July 2022,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/gavin-molloy-extends-shelbourne-contract-as-jack-scott-leaves-st-pats/41836749.html|title=Gavin Molloy extends Shelbourne contract as Jack Scott leaves St Pat's|date=13 July 2022|website=Irish Independent}}</ref> in April 2023,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/articles/30296/gavin-molloy-signs-new-deal-shels/|title=Gavin Molloy signs new deal with Shels|first=Dave|last=Donnelly|website=extratime.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/soccer-news/damien-duff-warning-rivals-over-29649552|title=Damien Duff in warning to rivals over star man, as Gavin Molloy signs new deal|first=Mark|last=McCadden|date=6 April 2023|website=Irish Mirror}}</ref> and again in February 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://shelbournefc.ie/gavin-molloy-signs-new-deal-2/|title=Gavin Molloy signs new deal|first=Shelbourne|last=FC|date=14 February 2024}}</ref> With Shelbourne he was a runner-up in the [[2022 FAI Cup]] final.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6559945/gavin-molloy-using-fai-cup-final-heartache-to-fuel-aberdeen-silverware-dream/|title=Defender Gavin Molloy using FAI Cup final heartache to fuel Aberdeen silverware dream|first=Sean|last=Wallace|date=16 August 2024}}</ref>

On 14 June 2024, it was announced that Molloy would sign a three-year contract with Scottish side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 1 July, joining the club for an undisclosed fee,<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 June 2024 |title=Aberdeen FC - Gavin Molloy is first summer signing |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2024/06/14/gavin-molloy-is-first-summer-signing/ |access-date=23 June 2024 |website=Aberdeen FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=14 June 2024 |title=Aberdeen: Barron, Roos and Stewart leaving, Hoilett could stay |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/crgg179d4kpo |access-date=16 June 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=14 June 2024 |title=Shelbourne defender Gavin Molloy joins Aberdeen |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/2024/06/14/shelbourne-defender-gavin-molloy-joins-aberdeen/ |access-date=23 June 2024 |website=The Irish Times}}</ref> reported to be worth [[£]]75,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wallace |first=Sean |date=17 June 2024 |title=Revealed: The release clause which allowed Aberdeen to sign Gavin Molloy |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6504445/new-aberdeen-signing-gavin-molloys-release-clause-revealed/ |access-date=23 June 2024 |website=The Press and Journal}}</ref> After Molloy's departure, Shelbourne won the league on the final day of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McLaughlin |first=Kevin |date=1 November 2024 |title=Harry Wood fires Shelbourne to league title in Derry |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2024/1101/1478531-wood-fires-shelbourne-to-league-title-in-derry/ |website=RTÉ.ie}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His grandfather, [[Theo Dunne]], was also a footballer and similarly captained Shelbourne.<ref name="auto"/> His second cousin, [[Richard Dunne]], was also a footballer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6504025/gavin-molloy-peter-ambrose-sold-on-move-to-aberdeen-by-jimmy-thelin/|title=How Gavin Molloy and Peter Ambrose were sold on move to Aberdeen by Jimmy Thelin|first=Paul|last=Third|date=16 June 2024}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Heidelberg]], [[Baden-Württemberg]], Germany, Klein joined the academy of [[FC Astoria Walldorf]] before switching to [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim]] a year later. In 2019, aged 18, Klein was picked as part of the squad for [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim II|Hoffenheim II]] for the upcoming season.

He made no appearance during the 2019–20 season, but debuted the following season. He made 16 league appearance during the 2020–21 season, attracting a transfer from [[Bundesliga]] club [[FC Augsburg]].<ref name="be">{{cite web|url=http://besoccer.com/player/daniel-klein-627400|title=Daniel Klein at Be Soccer|website=besoccer.com|access-date=27 September 2024|archive-date=4 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241004025358/https://www.besoccer.com/player/daniel-klein-627400|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.co.uk/football/player/_/id/321060/daniel-klein|title=Daniel Klein's player information|website=espn.co.uk/football|access-date=27 September 2024|archive-date=24 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240824053653/https://www.espn.co.uk/football/player/_/id/321060/daniel-klein|url-status=live}}</ref>

===FC Augsburg===
On 2 July 2021, FC Augsburg signed Klein and immediatiely assigned to the reserve team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://int.soccerway.com/players/daniel-klein/542625|title=Daniel Klein's transfer history|website=Soccerway|access-date=20 September 2024|archive-date=18 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240518124927/https://int.soccerway.com/players/daniel-klein/542625/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2023, Augsburg sent Klein out on a season-long loan to [[3. Liga]] club [[SV Sandhausen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sofascore.com/player/daniel-klein/930282|title=Transfer History For Daniel Klein|website=sofascore.com|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref>

On 30 June 2024, Klein signed a contract extension, keeping him at the club until 25 September 2028.

===Loan to SV Sandhausen===
Klein went on a season long loan to [[3. Liga]] club [[SV Sandhausen]] in 2023. He made four appearances in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://skysports.com/football/player/189308/daniel-klein|title=Daniel Klein's Career Records|website=skysports.com/football|access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
Born to a [[German people|German]] father and [[Indonesian people|Indonesian]] mother, Klein is eligible to represent either [[Germany national football team|Germany]] or [[Indonesia national football team|Indonesia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/goalpost_asia/p/DCLupXFRPAx/|title=Daniel Klein is interested in playing for Indonesia|date=4 February 2025|access-date=4 February 2025|website=instagram.com|language=en}}</ref>

Klein represented [[Germany national football team|Germany]] at [[Germany national under-15 football team|under-15]] to [[Germany national under-19 football team|under-19]] level.<ref>{{cite web|title=Daniel Klein|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/daniel-klein/542625/|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in Germany, Klein is of Indonesian descent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Profil Daniel Klein, Kiper FC Augsburg Keturunan Indonesia|url=https://www.idntimes.com/sport/soccer/profil-daniel-klein-kiper-fc-augsburg-keturunan-jerman-bali-00-qftxr-nms550/amp|date=8 November 2024|website=idntimes.com|language=id}}</ref>

'''Owen Elding''' (born 7 March 2006) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]. Born in England, he represents the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland national team]].

==Early life==
Elding was born in [[Boston, Lincolnshire|Boston]] in England and also lived in [[Stockport]] when his father played there,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/a-new-start-for-new-boy-elding-987278|title=A new start for new boy Elding|date=5 September 2007|website=Manchester Evening News}}</ref> before moving to [[Riverstown]], [[County Sligo]] when his father [[Anthony Elding|Anthony]] signed for [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] in 2013.<ref name="Hibs signing">{{Cite web |date=29 January 2026 |title=Career So Far: Owen Elding |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2026/january/29/career-so-far--owen-elding/ |access-date=7 April 2026 |website=www.hibernianfc.co.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260407235707/https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2026/january/29/career-so-far--owen-elding/|url-status=live|archive-date=7 April 2026}}</ref> Elding attended Ardkeeran Primary School with fellow Sligo teammate, [[Johnny Kenny]], where he also played Gaelic football.<ref name="auto" /> He began playing association football with [[Ballinamallard United F.C.|Ballinamallard United]].<ref name="Hibs signing" /> He later played for Arrow Harps in Riverstown, before switching to Manulla F.C., where he performed well enough to be called up to the [[Mayo League]] representative side. After returning to Arrow Harps, Elding featured for the Sligo/Leitrim League representative side.<ref name="auto" />

==Career==
===Youth career===
Elding's performances earned him a successful trial with the [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] Academy and he joined the club's under-13 team in 2019. He moved to [[Longford Town F.C.|Longford Town]]'s academy in 2021 for two seasons while his father was coaching there, before returning to [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] in 2023.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sligorovers.com/owen-elding-interview/|title=Owen Elding Interview – Sligo Rovers|date=5 July 2023}}</ref> In March 2022, Elding scored the winning goal in the National School's Cup Final for his school Coola Post Primary School, in a 3–2 win over Scoil Ruáin in Tipperary at the [[Athlone Town Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressreader.com/ireland/sligo-weekender/20220331/282939568808850|title=All-Ireland delight at last for progressive Coola PPS|publisher=Sligo Weekender|date=31 March 2022|via=www.pressreader.com}}</ref> He won a third-tier league title at under-17 level in October 2022 with [[Longford Town F.C.|Longford Town]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ltfc.ie/2022/10/u17s-win-league-title/|title=U17's win league title!|date=4 July 2025}}</ref> In November 2024, he featured in the National Under-20 Shield Final for the [[Sligo Rovers F.C.|Sligo Rovers]] Under-20s as they were defeated 2–1 by [[Shelbourne F.C.|Shelbourne]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/sligo/sport/soccer/another-final-heartbreak-for-sligo-rovers-under-20s-as-shelbourne-score-last-minute-winner/a638557291.html|title=Another final heartbreak for Sligo Rovers' Under 20s as Shelbourne score last minute winner|date=11 November 2024|website=Irish Independent}}</ref>

On 29 January 2026, Elding signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on a four-and-a-half-year contract for an undisclosed fee, believed to be €400,000 up front plus add-ons.<ref>https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2026/january/29/owen-elding-is-a-hibee-/</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-41783213.html|title=Hibernian set to sign Owen Elding from Sligo Rovers|first=John|last=Fallon|date=27 January 2026|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 1 February 2026, coming off the bench in a 0–0 draw with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at [[Easter Road]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/former-sligo-rovers-star-owen-elding-praised-as-hibs-deny-rangers/a932085475.html|title=Former Sligo Rovers star Owen Elding praised as Hibs deny Rangers|date=1 February 2026|website=www.independent.ie}}</ref> On 14 February 2026, he made his first start for the club and opened the scoring in a 2–0 win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] with a 42nd-minute header.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp9m5x2ged4t|title=Hibernian vs St. Mirren: Scottish Premiership updates & match report|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/owen-elding-goal-hibs-beat-st-mirren-6957481-Feb2026/|title=Owen Elding marks his full Hibs debut with goal against St Mirren|first=Press|last=Association|date=14 February 2026|website=The 42}}</ref> On 4 April 2026 he opened the scoring in a 3–0 win at home to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] after just 13 seconds, getting on the end of [[Felix Passlack]]'s pass.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2026/0404/1566745-elding-scores-after-13-seconds-in-hibernian-win/|title=Elding scores after 13 seconds in Hibernian win|date=4 April 2026|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref>

'''Findlay Marshall''' (Born 17 April 2006) is a Scottish footballer who currently plays as a midfielder for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

== Club career ==

=== Aberdeen ===
Marshall started his career with the youth team Dyce Boys Club, before joining [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]'s academy. On 20 September 2023, Findlay signed his First Professional Contract with the club on a 3 year deal, that would see him at the club until 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aberdeen FC - Findlay Marshall Agrees Contract Extension |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2023/09/20/findlay-marshall-agrees-contract-extension/ |access-date=2 September 2025 |website=Aberdeen FC |language=en}}</ref> Marshall was told at the beginning of the 2025-26 season he was free to leave the club, but has since moved on loan to [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]]. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Cryle |first=Ryan |date=4 July 2025 |title=REVEALED: Aberdeen youth academy product Findlay Marshall told he can leave club this summer |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6798544/aberdeen-academy-product-findlay-marshall-told-he-can-leave/ |access-date=5 September 2025 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref>  

=== Edinburgh City ===
At the Beginning of the [[Transfer window|January Transfer Window]] in the [[2023–24 in Scottish football|2023-2024]] season, Marshall joined [[Scottish League One|Scottish League one]] side [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] on loan until the end of season.

=== Cove Rangers ===
Marshall moved to [[Scottish League One|Scottish league one]] side [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] at the start of the [[2024–25 in Scottish football|2024-2025]] season on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Richard |date=2 August 2024 |title=Young Dons Adam And Findlay Sign-On |url=https://coverangersfc.com/2024/08/02/young-dons-findlay-and-adam-sign-on/ |access-date=2 September 2025 |website=Cove Rangers FC |language=en}}</ref> Marshall featured in the SPFL Team of the week for week 28 after a 3-1 victory over [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in which he scored 2 Goals. <ref name=spfltotw>{{Cite web |title=Team of the Week {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/team-of-the-week-50451 |access-date=2 September 2025 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> He also appeared in SPFL Team of the week for week 38 after a 4-2 victory over [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] with Marshall providing a goal and an assist.<ref name=spfltotw /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Britton |first=Ruaraidh |date=2 August 2024 |title=Aberdeen youngsters Findlay Marshall and Adam Emslie join Cove Rangers on loan |url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/aberdeen-youngsters-findlay-marshall-adam-9457137 |access-date=5 September 2025 |website=Aberdeen Live |language=en}}</ref>

=== Arbroath ===
At the start of the [[2025–26 in Scottish football|2025-2026]] season Marshall moved to [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a season long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aberdeen FC - Young Don Heads out on Loan |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2025/07/08/young-don-heads-out-on-loan/ |access-date=2 September 2025 |website=Aberdeen FC |language=en}}</ref> Marshall helped guide Arbroath to a Scottish Premiership Promotion Playoffs<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-01 |title=Pars to kick off play-off campaign at home after Lichties stalemate |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/26073405.dunfermline-draw-arbroath-ahead-premiership-play-off/ |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=Dunfermline Press |language=en}}</ref> and Nominated for PFA Scotland SPFL Young Player of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ninetwo |first=Design |date=2026-04-27 |title=POTY Nominations {{!}} Premiership, SWPL |url=https://pfascotland.co.uk/poty-nominations-premiership-swpl/ |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=PFA Scotland |language=en-US}}</ref> 

== International career ==
Marshall was called up to the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Under-17]] team in 2023 for their UEFA Under-17 Euro campaign. Marshall came off the bench in the 84th Minute against France Under-17, a game Scotland lost 3-1. Marshall was also an unused substitute for the games against Germany and Portugal. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Scotland Under 17s begin EURO 2023 campaign with France defeat after spirited display |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-17s-begin-euro-2023-campaign-with-france-defeat-after-spirited-display/ |access-date=2 September 2025 |website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==
Šuto was born in Croatia, and holds dual Croatian and Australian citizenship through his [[Melbourne]]-born father.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nine.com.au/sport/football/news-2026-australia-socceroos-squad-named-fifa-series-cameroon-curacao-20260319-p5qd1b.html|title=Star who has never been to Australia named in Socceroos squad|date=19 March 2026|website=Nine}}</ref>

Following his signing and subsequent debut goal for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 4 February 2026, a possible selection for the [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia national team]] was suggested by media outlets in Australia, due to the unlikelihood of him being selected for the [[Croatia national football team|Croatia national team]]. Hibernian also has two other Australian internationals: [[Martin Boyle]] (who scored in the same match) and [[Jack Iredale]], both of whom were born in [[Scotland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football360.com.au/socceroos-news-ante-suto-hibernian-transfer-news-fee-details-latest/|title=Forward who is eligible to play for the Socceroos makes $848k move to Scotland|first=Jake|last=Rosengarten|publisher=[[Football360]]|date=3 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football360.com.au/socceroos-news-ante-suto-goal-video-watch-hibernian-dundee-united/|title=Possible Socceroo scores 93rd minute winner in dream debut with Aussies everywhere|first=Jake|last=Rosengarten|publisher=[[Football360]]|date=5 February 2026}}</ref> Following the suggestions, he admitted that he would like to represent the Socceroos.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football360.com.au/socceroos-news-ante-suto-how-hibernian-striker-is-eligible-for-australia-world-cup-hopes-latest/|title=Shock World Cup bolter in talks with Football Australia: How he's eligible for Socceroos revealed|first=Barry|last=Anderson|publisher=[[Football360]]|date=18 February 2026}}</ref>

Following a good spell of form at club level, Šuto was called up to the Australia squad for the first time in March 2026 to face [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] and [[Curaçao national football team|Curaçao]] in the [[FIFA Series]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theage.com.au/sport/soccer/popovic-names-three-uncapped-players-but-no-volpato-in-socceroos-squad-20260319-p5pr6j.html|title=Popovic names three uncapped players – but no Volpato – in Socceroos squad|first=Vince|last=Rugari|publisher=[[The Age]]|date=19 March 2026}}</ref>
